1001: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, multiple Warbosses, Boyz, Gretchin, Nobz, Stormboyz, and Painboyz hauled forward in Trukks and Battlewagons, this is a mass-infantry brawler running primarily Equatorial Hordes for early pressure via Scouts 6" on MOB/KOMMANDOS units. The plan is to flood midboard objectives with cheap screening Gretchin, deliver hard-hitting melee blobs into the enemy's face through transport, and grind scoring zones with sheer weight of bodies. It punishes low-model elite armies that cannot clear volume efficiently, leveraging Painboy durability buffs and multiple Warboss activations to keep key mobs fighting through attrition. Armies with strong ranged volume or high-damage overwatch tools can bleed the advance before it lands, stranding expensive cargo in wrecked transports and collapsing the tempo engine.
1002: Built around Wazdakka Gutsmek, Deffkoptas, Warbikers, Flash Gitz in Trukks, and Tankbustas, this is a More Dakka!/Speedwaaagh! Speed Freeks swarm that floods the mid-board with fast, shooty bodies and infantry riding transports. The plan is to Advance everything using Speedwaaagh! turbo moves to hit 24" threat ranges, trigger the Waaagh! to stack Sustained Hits 1 onto the Infantry's already-Assault shooting, then overwhelm targets with volume-of-fire while Tankbustas handle armour. It punishes lists that rely on static gun lines or fragile elite infantry, since the sheer number of activations and mid-board presence denies space before the opponent can establish defensive screens. Armies with strong anti-vehicle saturation or high-AP shooting crack it open by stripping Trukks early and leaving the passenger Infantry exposed in the open.
1003: Built around Wazdakka Gutsmek, multiple Warbiker squads, Deffkoptas, Wartrakks, a Deffkilla Wartrike, Big Mek Dakkarigs, a Warboss, and Gretchin screens, this is a fast, mid-table brawling horde that floods the board with cheap bodies and mobile threats simultaneously. The plan is to swamp the midfield early with bikes and fast vehicles, pin opponents into their deployment zone, then grind them off objectives through sheer weight of attacks and layered melee pressure while Gretchin babysit backfield primaries. It punishes armies that struggle to kill high volumes of tough, spread-out targets, as dedicating firepower to Warbikers means Boyz and Deffkoptas survive to score, and vice versa. It cracks under concentrated high-AP shooting or strong alpha-strike lists that can strip the bike screen before the Orks ever close to combat range.
1004: Built around Magnus the Red, massed Rubric Marines transported in Chaos Rhinos, Scarab Occult Terminators, and a supporting cast of Sorcerers, Chaos Spawn screens, Tzaangor Enlightened, and a winged Daemon Prince, all operating under Grand Coven. The plan is to cycle Grand Coven's Command phase abilities — extending Psychic weapon ranges and amplifying their lethality — while Rhinos push Rubrics into scoring positions and Magnus and the Daemon Prince threaten priority targets from range or in melee. This build punishes armies relying on durable mid-table infantry, layering psychic shooting across multiple units so any single threat-removal answer leaves three more intact. It cracks when faced with aggressive alpha-strike lists that strip the Rhinos early and strand Rubrics out of position before the psychic engine can come online.
1005: Built around Sekhetar Robots, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Tzaangor Enlightened (both melee and Fatecaster Greatbow variants), Sorcerers, a Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings, and Magnus the Red in the Hexwarp Thrallband detachment, this is a layered horde that floods the board with durable, Tzeentch-blessed bodies across multiple unit types. The win condition runs through Flow of Magic board control — contest No Man's Land objectives early to keep the detachment's buff active, then use Sekhetar Robots as a mid-table brawling anvil while Magnus, the Daemon Prince, and massed ranged fire layer lethal output on priority targets. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear volume, exploiting the combination of resilient infantry blobs and hard-hitting monster support to trade extremely efficiently. Armies with strong board-wide anti-horde tools or objective denial that can contest No Man's Land before the Flow of Magic activates will pressure the scoring engine hard, and anything that drops Magnus early removes the build's most concentrated threat vector.
1006: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Tzaangor Enlightened, and a deep support bench of Sorcerers and a winged Daemon Prince, this Grand Coven list layers psychic firepower across every phase behind a screen of Tzaangors and Chaos Spawn. The engine is Imbued Manifestation and Psychic Maelstrom cycling through Grand Coven's command-phase abilities to extend and amplify psychic ranged output, while Rhino-mounted Rubrics push onto mid-board objectives and Magnus bullies key targets or zones independently. It punishes static, low-mobility armies that can't contest the mid-table before the psychic escalation locks them out of scoring lanes. Armies that can deep-strike or alpha-strike past the chaff screen and isolate Magnus early expose how dependent this list is on its primarch surviving long enough to pay off his points.
1007: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened, Sekhetar Robots, Sorcerer in Terminator Armour, Scarab Occult Terminators, Defilers, Rubric Marines, and Sorcerers, this list layers psyker-buffed infantry transport pressure with Vehicle fire support across multiple detachment synergies. The win condition is sustained board control through stacked ritual healing keeping psyker units alive, Sekhetar Robots gaining Psychic attacks and boosted WS from nearby psykers, and Defilers squeezing out re-rolled hit, wound, and damage rolls when parked beside those same psyker models. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that struggle to clear layered infantry waves while simultaneously dealing with Defiler and Forgefiend shooting. However, high-volume mortal wound output or anti-psyker disruption cracks the engine by stripping the psyker bubble that every core synergy depends on.
1008: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines, Mutalith Vortex Beasts, and a deep bench of Exalted Sorcerers, Sorcerers, Chaos Spawn, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, Sekhetar Robots, Rhino-transported infantry, and a winged Daemon Prince, Grand Coven floods the board with psychic firepower while cycling its once-per-battle command phase abilities — Imbued Manifestation extending psychic weapon ranges, then Psychic Maelstrom layering mortal-wound pressure — to win through attrition and board saturation. The plan is to hold mid-table with expendable Spawn and Tzaangors screening for Magnus and the Mutaliths, who generate sustained lethal output across multiple threat vectors while Enhancements like Eldritch Vortex of E'Taph and Umbralefic Crystal amplify key characters. It punishes lower-model-count elite armies that can't efficiently clear the horde screen before the psychic engine fires. Armies that alpha-strike Magnus early or out-range the psychic weapons before Imbued Manifestation activates crack this list open, as the entire kill chain depends on keeping the big threats alive long enough to cycle through those one-use abilities.
1009: Built around Mutalith Vortex Beasts, Lords of Change, Rubric Marines, Screamers, Kairos Fateweaver, Exalted Sorcerers, Pink Horrors, and Tzaangor Enlightened, this Changehost of Deceit army floods the table with a deep, layered daemon-and-marine hybrid roster that generates consistent psychic output across multiple threat vectors. The engine is Daemonic Illusions — keeping Psyker units near Scintillating Legions models to maintain 4+ invulnerable saves against ranged attacks while Mutalith Vortex Beasts press forward as durable mid-table brawlers that force opponents to commit resources or cede ground. It punishes gunline and elite-shooting armies hard, where the layered invulnerability and sheer body count make efficient damage-trading almost impossible. It cracks against fast melee armies that can isolate and pick apart the Psyker aura bubbles before they fully establish, collapsing the save stack and exposing the infantry underneath.
1010: Built around Rubric Marines in volume, Exalted Sorcerers, Mutalith Vortex Beasts, Sekhetar Robots, Tzaangor Enlightened with fatecaster greatbows, and Sorcerers, this list leans on the Ritual of Regeneration detachment's heal-on-manifest ability to keep Psyker units topped up across the game. The plan is sustained attrition: manifest Rituals repeatedly to recover wounds on key pieces while Rubrics hold objectives and the Mutalith and Robots apply layered pressure across multiple threat vectors. This punishes mid-range gunlines that lack the concentrated firepower to delete durable, self-healing blobs in a single activation, stretching their removal budget thin across a wide horde front. It cracks open against aggressive alpha-strike armies or elite melee that can isolate and delete Psyker models before Rituals resolve, collapsing the regeneration engine entirely.
1011: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings, and Chaos Spawn screening en masse, this is a Grand Coven psychic pressure list that cycles its three Command phase abilities — extended Psychic range, boosted Psychic lethality — to layer punishment across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. The win condition is stacking mortal wounds and high-AP Psychic shooting through Magnus and the Terminators while Rubrics hold mid-board objectives under durable saves, forcing opponents to choose between trading into elite infantry or surrendering primary points. It punishes gunlines and elite low-model-count armies brutally, as the extended Psychic range and lethal layering mean those lists can't stay outside threat bands while still contesting. Dense horde screens and fast melee armies that can collapse the Chaos Spawn bubble and tie up Magnus in combat crack this list open by shutting off its Command phase engine before it fires.
1012: Built around Allarus Custodians, Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, Blade Champions, Trajann Valoris, Witchseekers, Prosecutors, Vertus Praetors, and a Shield-Captain in Allarus armour, all operating under Lions of the Emperor — which grants +1 to Hit and +1 to Wound whenever a non-Vehicle Custodes unit fights without a friendly unit within 6". The plan is to spread individual units across the board in deliberate isolation, triggering the detachment bonus on every attack to punch well above statline while contesting objectives with elite bodies that are extremely hard to shift. This build punishes mid-density armies that can't reliably bubble-wrap every unit, since isolating targets is trivially easy and each Custodes model then hits and wounds at a level that dismantles normal infantry and medium armour alike. Massed screening and tight coherent blobs crack it open — deny the isolation bubble, lose the bonus, and suddenly gold-clad elites are paying premium points for ordinary stats.
1013: Built around Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, Allarus Custodians, Blade Champions, Contemptor-Achillus Dreadnoughts, and Caladius Grav-Tanks, this list runs the Might of the Moritoi detachment to push its Walker units to exceptional speed — +2" Movement plus bonuses to advance and charge rolls — turning already-durable elites into a fast, multi-threat wave. The plan is to pressure multiple objectives simultaneously, using buffed Dreadnoughts to crash into key targets while Shield Host's Critical Hit escalation on melee attacks lets the infantry grind through whatever survives. It punishes elite low-volume armies hard, where Custodes' layered toughness and lethal melee can trade up across the board without fear of being overwhelmed in return. However, high-volume, high-AP shooting or mass mortal wound output can crack the small model count wide open, and losing even one or two key pieces early collapses the threat density the entire list depends on.
1014: Built around Allarus Custodians, Vertus Praetors, a Shield-Captain on Dawneagle Jetbike, and Witchseekers and Prosecutors as screening infantry, this list runs across a split detachment field — roughly equal thirds choosing Tharanatoi Hammerblow, Solar Spearhead, or Silent Hunters — giving it a mobile, layered toolbox identity rather than a single dominant gameplan. The win condition is aggressive board control: Allarus drop via ingress to threaten charges, Vertus Praetors project mobile anti-armour threat, and Witchseekers plus Prosecutors flood secondaries and deny opponent actions. It punishes slower, elite infantry armies that cannot screen ingress vectors, letting Allarus land, re-roll charges under Hammerblow, and delete anchor units before opponents stabilise. However, it cracks against high-volume shooting that strips Custodians unit-by-unit before the charge lands, as losing even one or two Allarus before impact dramatically reduces the punch of each expensive, low-model squad.
1015: Built around Vertus Praetors, Shield-Captains on Dawneagle Jetbikes, Venatari Custodians, and Telemon Heavy Dreadnoughts, with Allarus Custodians, Custodian Wardens, Witchseekers, and Prosecutors filling out a deep, varied roster under the Might of the Moritoi detachment, which grants all Custodes Walkers +2" Movement and +1 to advance and charge rolls. The plan is to use the boosted Walker mobility alongside fast jetbike units to crash into mid-board early, delete priority targets through layered melee threat, and bury opponents in simultaneous pressure across multiple angles rather than committing a single kill chain. It punishes slow, castle-heavy lists that cannot respond to multi-vector aggression — the sheer range of dangerous unit types forces poor prioritisation and leaves no safe trade. The weakness is spread thin: without a single overwhelming hammer, a disciplined opponent who identifies and isolates the most dangerous units piecemeal can unpick the list before it fully converges.
1016: Built around Allarus Custodians, Custodian Wardens, Venerable Contemptor Dreadnoughts, Vertus Praetors, and Valerian, supported by Prosecutors and Witchseekers as cheap objective bodies, running Lions of the Emperor and Might of the Moritoi to supercharge both its elite infantry and its walkers. The plan is to isolate elite units to trigger Lions of the Emperor's +1 to hit and wound, then layer that boosted lethality across multiple threat vectors — accelerated Dreadnoughts crashing in with enhanced movement and charge rolls while Allarus and Wardens independently threaten flanks with their own buffed combat output. It punishes medium-armour armies that lack the volume to screen every lane, since the combination of fast-moving Walkers and independently operating elite infantry overwhelms any defensive positioning built for a single main threat. Its weakness is mass cheap screens and objective-denial swarms, which force elite units into proximity with each other and collapse the Lions of the Emperor isolation requirement before the kill chain ever fires.
1017: Built around Contemptor-Achillus and Contemptor-Galatus Dreadnoughts supported by Allarus Custodians, Shield-Captains in Terminator armour, Custodian Guard, Wardens, Dawneagle jetbike Shield-Captains, and Telemon heavies, this is a Lions of the Emperor list that pairs its infantry isolation bonus — +1 to hit and wound when no friendly unit is within 6" — with the Might of the Moritoi strat pushing Walkers to sprint and slam into combat faster. The plan is layered threat saturation: mobile Dreadnoughts crash contact zones while isolated infantry delete priority targets with boosted hit-and-wound rolls, grinding points through kills and contested objectives simultaneously. It punishes slow, bunched armies that hand it free isolation windows and can't match the sheer durability-per-model of gold-armoured elites. Spread-out, screen-heavy lists that deny isolation bubbles and chaff out the Dreadnoughts' charge lanes expose its relatively low model count and blunt both detachment payoffs at once.
1019: Built around Vertus Praetors, Venatari Custodians, and a Shield-Captain on Dawneagle Jetbike as fast melee strikers, with Allarus Custodians and their Shield-Captain dropping in via ingress to threaten the backfield, operating under Shield Host with Tharanatoi Hammerblow stacked on top. The plan is to use the Shield Host Ka'tah rotation to spike critical hits in melee while Hammerblow Terminators ingress, re-roll their charges, and crack priority targets, with Witchseekers and Prosecutors screening flanks and contesting secondaries. It punishes slow, durable armies that cannot screen multiple simultaneous threats — the combination of jetbike pressure from one angle and Terminator ingress from another creates an anti-tank overload that elite infantry lists struggle to answer. However, it cracks open against armies that can screen deep-strike zones tightly, denying the Hammerblow charge re-rolls entirely and leaving the Terminators stranded while the jetbike units trade unfavourably without a melee support anvil.
1020: Built around Venatari Custodians, Allarus Custodians, Witchseekers, Vertus Praetors, Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, and a Blade Champion, all operating under Lions of the Emperor, which rewards individual units fighting in isolation with +1 to Hit and +1 to Wound. The plan is to spread these elite, hard-hitting units across the board so each fights alone, maximizing that isolation bonus, then use their collective mobility and melee weight to grind through objectives and kill scoring threats before the opponent can consolidate. This build punishes elite armies that lack the volume to screen multiple isolated threats simultaneously, as the Lions bonus makes even moderate Custodes units punch well above their point cost in a trade. The weakness is anything that can flood the board with cheap bodies to collapse that isolation bubble, or high-volume shooting that removes key pieces before they reach their targets, since the list has limited bodies to absorb attrition across a full game.
1021: Built around Caladius Grav-Tanks, Allarus Custodians, Witchseekers, and Custodian Wardens, this Lions of the Emperor list uses elite infantry transported aggressively across the board, hunting isolated enemy units to trigger the detachment's +1 Hit and +1 Wound bonus when no friendly units are within 6". The win condition is a layered kill chain: Caladius tanks soften targets at range while Allarus Custodians and Wardens drop into isolated engagements, punishing fragile screening units and mid-field objective holders simultaneously. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies hardest, where the Lions bonus activates reliably and every swing overperforms against expensive targets. Horde lists and dense screening crack it open by clustering cheap bodies that deny the isolation bonus and clog charge lanes before the infantry can commit.
1022: Built around Allarus Custodians deep-striking via ingress and crashing into melee with re-rolled charge rolls, supported by Caladius Grav-Tanks, Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, and a Blade Champion providing layered melee threat across the board. The engine is the Tharanatoi Hammerblow detachment's ingress-into-charge loop: Terminators drop in, re-roll their charge, and the Shield Host's Ka'tah toggling — either Critical Hits on 5+ or improved AP — amplifies the kill chain turn by turn while Caladius tanks apply skimmer fire pressure to force splits in opposing attention. It punishes elite-infantry lists that lack dense screening, where the Terminators land cleanly and the mobile threat stack from Grav-Tanks plus Blade Champion overwhelms any single defensive layer. However, horde screens that deny clean ingress zones and armies with strong alpha-strike reach can collapse the charge-dependent kill plan before it pays off.
1023: Built around Jakhals, Flesh Hounds, Bloodletters, Lords on Juggernaut, Khorne Berzerkers, Exalted Eightbound, Forgefiends, Skarbrand, Daemon Princes, and Slaughterbound across Khorne Daemonkin and Vessels of Wrath, this is a Blood Tithe-fuelled mixed-arms horde that floods the board with mortal and daemonic bodies while Characters like the Lord on Juggernaut punch up via Vessels of Wrath's Cleave or AP boost on their melee attacks. The engine is attrition-through-volume: destroy units to bank Blood Tithe points, then spend them for mid-game power spikes while Forgefiends provide ranged anti-armour cover and fast units like Flesh Hounds contest objectives across every flank. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot clear the sheer number of bodies fast enough to prevent Blood Tithe generation, and Skarbrand's threat forces awkward positioning decisions. However, highly mobile shooting lists that can delete key Character models before Vessels of Wrath triggers, or armies with reliable screen-clearing tools, drain the Blood Tithe engine before it achieves critical mass.
427: Built around multiple Crisis suit variants (Sunforge, Starscythe, Fireknife), Coldstar Commanders, Commander Farsight, Broadsides, and Stealth Suits screening the whole package, the Experimental Prototype Cadre extends all Battlesuit Character ranged attacks by 6", then layers Kauyon's mid-to-late Sustained Hits 1 and modifier-ignoring Guided shots on top to create a fire-superiority engine that only gets more dangerous as the game progresses. The plan is to use Pathfinders to Spot and guide Crisis suits into firing lanes where Sustained Hits 1 amplifies already high-volume anti-armour output, while Kroot Carnivores and Vespid hold objectives so the suits stay mobile and keep shooting. It punishes elite mechanised lists badly — the extended range and late-game Sustained Hits stack cripples armies that need to close distance to neutralise firepower. Heavy alpha-strike lists that can land melee threats early crack it open before Kauyon activates, and anything that collapses the Pathfinder spotting chain degrades the Guided bonus the whole engine relies on.
428: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams, Twin Lance, Riptide Battlesuits, Broadsides, Crisis Starscythes, Piranhas, and Vespid Stingwings under Mont'ka, this is a hyper-mobile anti-armour force that threatens every corner of the board from turn one. Mont'ka grants [ASSAULT] across the first three battle rounds, letting the entire army advance and still unload full firepower, while Guided units gain [LETHAL HITS] to punish anything with a meaningful save — the kill chain runs through Pathfinders marking targets and heavies deleting them in the same activation. It excels against elite, low-volume armies where Lethal Hits and massed S7–S10 shooting overwhelms invulnerable saves and heavy armour before they can respond. Saturated horde screens and aggressive melee threats that can tie up Riptides and Crisis suits early crack this list open, since it lacks the volume to efficiently clear chaff while simultaneously holding objectives.
430: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Kâhl, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Hekaton Land Fortresses, this is a close-range brawler that floods the midfield with elite, durable infantry backed by heavy fire support. The engine is straightforward but punishing: close to within 9" where the Hearthguard Covenant's re-roll wound rolls of 1 activates on eligible units, then grind through the opponent's army while Hernkyn Pioneers and Yaegirs contest objectives and feed the YP engine from the Needgaârd Oathband each time a unit is destroyed. It punishes armies that trade units freely—cheaper screens and chaff-heavy lists hand over YP and get outmuscled in melee by Hearthguard before they can answer. Lists that can hold the midfield at arm's length, apply long-range anti-tank pressure before the 9" window opens, or strip the Kapricus Carrier transport before Hearthguard disembark will crack this build wide open.
436: Built around waves of Poxwalkers flooding the board, Myphitic Blight-Haulers hunting armour, Typhus and Malignant Plaguecasters extending Contagion Range through Paragons of Putrescence, and Foetid Bloat-Drones brawling mid-table, this list weaponises Shamblerot Vectorium's free Poxwalker reinforcements to sustain a suffocating Battleline presence across every battle round. The plan is to drown opponents in expendable bodies that regenerate faster than they can be cleared, while Blight-Haulers run mobile anti-armour pressure and Contagion aura debuffs compound across overlapping characters to make the swarm punishing to engage at any range. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't clear volume efficiently — the free Poxwalker injections mean killing the swarm is a treadmill, not a solution. Lists with high-volume mortal wounds or board-wide indirect fire can bypass the attrition engine entirely, and the build's midfield brawling is only moderately durable once the character bubble is stripped.
438: Built around Kastelan Robots buffed by Cybernetica Datasmiths, Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, Skitarii Rangers screens, Tech-Priest Enginseers, Servitor Battleclades, Onager Dunecrawlers, and Skorpius Disintegrators, all operating under Cohort Cybernetica — which pushes Legio Cybernetica units 2" faster and adds 1 to their Objective Control while unshocked. The plan is to march boosted, high-OC Robots into mid-board, contest objectives with inflated control values, and layer shooting from Dunecrawlers and Disintegrators to peel off anything trying to dig them out. It punishes slow, infantry-heavy gunlines that can't shift durable, high-OC bodies from objectives before scoring windows close. However, aggressive alpha-strike armies that can battle-shock the Robots early strip both the OC bonus and the detachment's mobility edge simultaneously, collapsing the scoring engine before it stabilizes.
439: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, massed Skitarii Marshals, Tech-Priest Manipuli, Hastarii Fusiliers, Rangers, Vanguard, Sicarian Infiltrators, and Servitor Battleclades delivered aboard Skorpius Duneriders, with Ironstrider Ballistarii providing mobile anti-armour support. The list floods the midboard with transported infantry hordes, using layered buffs from Marshals and Manipuli to stack lethal firepower into objectives while Sicarians threaten flanks and disrupt backfield plays. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count armies by drowning them in bodies and overlapping threat vectors across multiple board sectors simultaneously. It struggles against fast, high-damage alpha-strike lists that can crack the Duneriders early and strand the infantry before the layered buff engine comes fully online.
441: Built around multiple Librarians (including Terminator-armoured variants), Inner Circle Companions, Deathwing Knights, Azrael, and Sternguard Veterans, this list runs Librarius Conclave with Unforgiven Task Force to layer psychic disciplines — Divination's re-rolls and Pyromancy's firepower — over elite melee and gunline elements. The win condition is controlling mid-table objectives through Deathwing Knights and Inner Circle Companions boosted by Unforgiven Task Force's Objective Control buff while Azrael and Sternguard saturate threats with re-roll-supported shooting. It punishes slower elite armies that can't efficiently answer both a durable melee hammer and a sustained-fire gunline simultaneously. However, fast alpha-strike forces or mass-horde lists that flood objectives before the OC buff activates can overwhelm it — and at under-50% wins, those matchups expose the build's relative fragility when the Psychic Discipline selection misfires.
446:
Built around Sanguinary Guard (averaging nearly 2.5 squads), Jump Pack Captains, Inceptors, Assault Intercessors with jump packs, and Gladiator Lancers, this is a highly mobile assault force running the Encarmine Speartip detachment, whose core trick lets Sanguinary Guard fall back and still shoot and charge in the same turn.

The plan is relentless pressure: Sanguinary Guard anchor the threat, refusing to be tied up in combat, while Gladiator Lancers handle armour and Inceptors provide mobile fire support — collectively making it nearly impossible for an opponent to safely hold objectives or screen.

It punishes slower gunlines and armies that rely on locking jump infantry in melee, because the fall-back-and-charge loop keeps Sanguinary Guard perpetually active and threatening.

It struggles against fast, high-volume anti-infantry output that can strip Guard units before they cycle back, or armies that can overwhelm the moderate screens of scouts and infiltrators and deny the charge angle entirely.
447: Built around Chosen, Defiler warbands, Huron Blackheart, Abaddon the Despoiler, Masters of the Maelstrom, and screens of Cultist Mobs backed by Red Corsairs Raiders, this is a Cabal of Chaos list that layers psyker firepower on top of a durable mid-board brawling core. The engine runs Dark Pacts to boost Heretic Astartes Psyker shooting with +1 Strength while Abaddon and Chosen crash the midfield, using cultist waves to hold secondaries and bleed opposing activations. The Fellhammer Siege-host's wound-roll penalty against strength-over-toughness attacks makes the brick stubbornly hard to shift with conventional anti-infantry shooting, punishing armies that rely on volume mid-strength fire. Massed mortal wounds, high-AP melee at range, or anything that bypasses wound rolls entirely — such as devastating wounds spam — tears through the cultist chaff and collapses the scoring base before the brawlers can close.
448: Built around Cultist Mobs, Defilers, Venomcrawlers, Vashtorr the Arkifane, and Warpsmiths, this list floods the board with Heretic Astartes Daemon Vehicles and uses Soulforged Warpack's Dark Pact invoking to stack +1 to Wound on ranged attacks and +2 Attacks in melee, turning every Daemon Engine into a threat multiplier that compounds across the shooting and fight phases simultaneously. The win condition is mobile anti-armour pressure — Defilers and Venomcrawlers threaten tanks and heavy infantry from turn one while Cultists screen objectives and Vashtorr supercharges the engine by supporting the Daemon Vehicle keyword synergies. It punishes slow, elite armour-heavy lists that can't clear multiple high-toughness Daemon Engines in a single turn before the Dark Pact buffs compound. Armies with reliable debuffs to Leadership — making Dark Pact tests more dangerous — or mass mortal-wound output that bypasses wound rolls crack it open by collapsing the Pact engine the entire list depends on.
449: Built around Chaos Terminator squads, Kravek Morne, Mutilators, and Cultist Mobs screening them forward, this is a grinding mid-board brawler that wins through attrition and presence rather than finesse. The plan is to plant Terminators and Mutilators on centrally contested objectives while Legionaries and Cultists absorb chip damage and trade up, letting the armoured core outlast opposing infantry across turns. It punishes elite low-model-count lists hard, where durable multi-wound units can absorb the firepower that would clear a horde while the screens deny easy charges. It cracks under concentrated high-AP anti-tank overload or heavy mortal wound output that bypasses the wound-roll resilience of the brick and strips both the screen and the expensive core in the same turn.
450: Built around Wyches, Incubi, Venoms, Raiders, Lady Malys, Drazhar, Lelith Hesperax, Succubus, Mandrakes, Scourges, and Reavers, this is a fast, layered mixed-arms swarm that floods the table with skimmer-ferried infantry and expendable bodies in every corner of the board. The plan is to overwhelm opponents through sheer volume of threats — Raiders and Venoms deliver Incubi and Wyches into critical combats while Mandrakes and Reavers contest secondaries and Scourges provide heavy-weapon reach to punish exposed targets. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't deal with simultaneous threats across multiple vectors, forcing impossible priority choices against layered lethality and screen saturation. It cracks open against high-volume shooting that strips transports before the payloads land, stranding fragile infantry in the open and collapsing the delivery mechanism the entire engine depends on.
451: Built around Drazhar, Lady Malys, Archons leading Incubi, Wyches, and Lelith Hesperax, all ferried across the board in a dense fleet of Venoms and Raiders running Kabalite Agonysts and Skysplinter Assault. The plan is to deliver elite melee threats directly into the opponent's scoring pieces while Scourges and Kabalite Warriors apply ranged pressure, using layered infantry volume across multiple transports to contest every objective simultaneously. This build punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't answer multiple fast moving threats at once — flooding the board with bodies forces trades that favor the Drukhari player's redundancy. It cracks open against high-AP shooting that strips transports early, since losing Venoms and Raiders before the charge negates the entire delivery engine.
455: Built around Skorpekh Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Lokhust Destroyers, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, their respective lords, Nekrosor Ammentar, the Void Dragon, and Lychguard, this is a Cursed Legion all-in Destroyer Cult force that escalates its own Strength characteristic through kills and half-strength triggers, turning each successful combat into a snowballing murder engine. The plan is to use Ophydians' infiltration and Skorpekhs' melee threat to crack open the opponent's frontline, triggering the Cursed Legion cascade so that Lokhust shooting arrives with boosted Strength to finish vehicles and monsters in the same turn. It punishes lists that commit expensive multi-wound units into the midboard piecemeal, since the kill-triggers chain freely against exposed elites and the Void Dragon adds a durable secondary anvil. Anything that screens aggressively, denies early charges, or removes the Destroyer units before they can kill-cascade — particularly alpha-strike armies with deep range or mass mortal output — can flatline the escalation engine before it starts.
456: Built around Technomancers, Canoptek Wraiths, Doomstalkers, Canoptek Reanimators, and the Nightbringer, this is a mobile, self-sustaining swarm that keeps its machines fighting through constant resurrection pressure while projecting threat across the whole table. The win condition is controlling the Power Matrix — owning No Man's Land objectives to extend the army's reanimation and ability bubble outward, then leveraging Doomstalkers as a fire-support spine and Wraiths as aggressive mid-table contesters to deny opponents scoring while banking primary. It punishes slow, low-model-count armies that struggle to clear bodies fast enough before Technomancers and Reanimators cycle units back onto objectives. However, high-tempo alpha-strike lists that can surgically remove Technomancers early collapse the resurrection engine before the Power Matrix ever stabilizes.
459: Built around Rogal Dorn Commanders, Scout Sentinels, Hellhounds, Leman Russ variants (Battle Tank and Exterminator), Rogal Dorn Battle Tanks, and Tech-Priest Enginseers, this is a mechanised armoured column running the Designation Force detachment, where Scout Sentinels and Infantry Smoke units plant Signal Flares to paint targets for the rest of the fleet. The win condition is layered designation fire: Sentinels sprint forward to mark high-value threats, then the massed Squadron guns delete them from the gunline, with Hellhounds covering flanks and burning out infantry screens that would otherwise block line of sight. This build punishes armour-heavy and elite lists brutally — stacking Squadron volume fire against expensive targets it has already designated strips even durable vehicles efficiently. It cracks open against fast aggressive armies that can swamp the Sentinels before flares land, collapsing the designation chain and leaving the static gunline shooting blind into a melee it cannot escape.
461: Built around massed Plaguebearers, Great Unclean Ones, Rotigus, Sloppity Bilepipers, Poxbringers, Nurglings, Beasts of Nurgle, Skull Cannons, and Epidemius operating under the Plague Legion detachment, this is a suffocating mid-board brawler that buries the opponent in rotting bodies. The win condition is sustained attrition pressure: Plague Legion's Shadow of Chaos forces Battle-shock tests on anything within 9" of Nurgle units each Command phase, while Warptide lets Plaguebearers advance and still charge, flooding objectives with Battleline that punishes failed morale with compounding deny-and-hold. It excels against elite low-model armies that struggle to clear the sheer volume of durable, layered threats, forcing anti-tank overload decisions between Skull Cannons and the lumbering Greater Daemons. Armies with consistent long-range shooting or heavy blast weapons that can thin screens before the advance reach contact will crack the attrition engine before it fully engages.
465: Built around Daemonettes, Defilers, Infractors, Lord Exultants, Tormentors, and Chaos Rhinos, this Carnival of Excess list floods the mid-table with Empowered infantry and daemon engines, layering Sustained Hits onto nearly every unit through tight Emperor's Children/Legions of Excess proximity bubbles. The win condition is a coordinated mid-board brawl where Rhino-delivered Infractors and Tormentors hit Empowered, stripping elite units through sheer volume of Sustained Hits attacks while Lord Exultants amplify output and Defilers provide mobile anti-armour muscle. It punishes elite low-model-count armies badly — anything that can't absorb mass Sustained Hits output across multiple fronts simultaneously gets dismantled piecemeal before it can consolidate. Armies that can collapse the Empowerment bubble through long-range firepower or screen the Rhinos off deployment deny the proximity engine before it gets rolling, cracking the list wide open.
466: Built around Flawless Blades, Tormentors, Infractors, Lord Exultants, Lucius the Eternal, Winged Daemon Princes, Chaos Spawn, and Defilers, this list runs primarily under Mercurial Host with most lists adding Spectacle of Slaughter to give Flawless Blades Fights First. The plan is to advance aggressively using re-roll-Advance mobility to flood the midboard with infantry delivered by Rhinos, then use Fights First Flawless Blades as a counter-punch anvil while Defilers and Daemon Princes hunt armour from multiple angles. It punishes slower, lower-model-count armies that struggle to contest multiple objectives simultaneously against a high-volume, transport-delivered threat package. However, anything that can shut down the advance phase with dense screens, hard-hitting shooting, or alpha-strike pressure before the melee engine engages will leave this list scrambling to recover.
467: Built around Marneus Calgar, Victrix Honour Guard, Repulsor Executioners, Ballistus Dreadnoughts, and a broad infantry core of Scouts, Intercessors, Bladeguard, and Jump Pack Assault Intercessors, this is a Blade of Ultramar gunline that layers mobile pressure on top of heavy firepower. Calgar's ability to recycle Combat Doctrines drives the engine — cycling through Doctrines repeatedly to stack their effects on Adeptus Astartes units keeps the Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts firing at peak efficiency while infantry flood objectives. It punishes slower, durable armies that want to trade attrition, overwhelming them with stacked shooting buffs before they can close range. Aggressive alpha-strike lists and elite melee threats that can strip the Honour Guard bubble and isolate Calgar crack it open, removing the Doctrine engine before it generates enough value.
468: Built around Vulkan He'stan, multiple Infernus Squads, Land Raider Redeemers, and a pair of Librarians, this list uses Forgefather's Seekers to give every Astartes ranged weapon the Assault rule and +1 Strength within 12", turning short-range fire into a punishing close-quarters gunline. The engine is a freight train of flame: Redeemers deliver Infernus Squads into the 12" bubble where the Strength bonus kicks in, while the Librarius Conclave Librarians cycle psychic disciplines to layer re-rolls or movement buffs onto the advancing wall of bodies. It punishes horde armies and lightly-armoured infantry severely, flooding the board with high-volume, boosted-Strength fire that few screening units survive. The critical weakness is anything that keeps it at arm's length — long-range anti-tank or deep-strike threats that pick off Redeemers before they deliver their cargo strand the Infernus Squads out of their optimal kill range.
470:
Built around War Dog Karnivores, Brigands, Executioners, and Stalkers, this all-cavalry Chaos Knights force runs the Houndpack Lance detachment, which grants Sustained Hits 1 to all War Dog attacks targeting a single designated enemy unit each Command phase.

The plan is to flood the board with fast armoured threats, designate a priority target every turn, and funnel the entire pack's output into it — layering melee and shooting kill chains to delete one unit at a time while cheap Cultist Mob screens hold objectives.

It punishes elite low-model-count lists savagely, as the Sustained Hits 1 focus-fire engine overloads saves on high-toughness targets that can't hide behind screen depth.

Mass cheap chaff — particularly large infantry blobs that can tarpit War Dogs in melee and deny them clean target selection — clogs the engine and bleeds out the pack before it can cycle through enough priority designations to win.
471: Built around Nurglings, Beasts of Nurgle, War Dog Karnivores, Knight Despoilers, and War Dog Brigands, this Infernal Lance list buries opponents in a layered tide of durable daemon chaff backed by hard-hitting Knights pushing up the board. The plan is to use Nurglings and Beasts as sticky, resilient screens that hold and contest objectives while Karnivores and Despoilers hunt armour, with Malefic Surge Empowering Knights to punch above their weight in key combats. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear the endless daemon screens while simultaneously dealing with multiple armoured threats engaging from different angles. Lists that can generate high volumes of mortal wounds or multi-damage shooting to efficiently clear both the chaff layer and the Knights simultaneously will crack it open before the daemon grind takes hold.
473: Built around Paladin Squads, Brotherhood Terminator Squads, Grand Master Voldus, Brotherhood Chaplains, and supporting Strike and Interceptor Squads, this list runs the Argent Assault detachment to ensure Paladins wound up even when punching into high-Toughness targets. The win condition is layered melee pressure across multiple fronts — Paladins grind through elite infantry and monsters while Terminators, frequently supplemented by Hallowed Conclave's Fell Back and fight/shoot ability, contest and reclaim objectives without surrendering board presence after a bad combat. It punishes slow, durable armies that rely on Toughness to survive melee, since the core detachment strips that defensive buffer from Paladins entirely, and the mobile toolkit of Interceptors keeps the pressure spread wide. However, high-volume shooting lists that can strip Paladins before they engage, or armies that deny the melee phase through layered screens, crack this build open by neutering the wound-roll engine before it fires.
474: Built around Interceptor Squads, Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Castellan Crowe with Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, Brotherhood Terminators, and Purgation Squads, all operating under the Banishers detachment, which unlocks Sustained Hits 1 or additional melee punch on a Leadership test each fight phase. The plan is to flood midfield with mobile psychic infantry, use Interceptors' surge moves after shooting via Immaterial Interdiction to threaten multiple objectives simultaneously, while Purgation Squads pin and battle-shock enemies with Fires of Purgation to create scoring windows. It punishes static elite armies that can't contest multiple points at once, leveraging sheer infantry volume and mobility to overwhelm objective control. It struggles against high-volume anti-infantry shooting that thins squads before they can fight, leaving too few bodies to hold the board.
475: Built around wall-to-wall Adeptus Astartes Battleline infantry — Crusader Squads, Assault Intercessors, and Intercessors — led by the Emperor's Champion, Helbrecht, Marshals, and Castellans, and backed by a battery of Repulsor Executioners, this is a suffocating mass-advance gunline that refuses to choose between shooting and moving. The Bastion Task Force rule lets every Battleline unit Advance or Fall Back and still shoot, charge, and perform Actions, so the list scores by blanketing objectives with bodies while the Repulsor Executioners pour fire over the top. That combination of volume infantry and heavy skimmer fire punishes anything that wants to trade piece-for-piece against a smaller elite army, simply burying opponents in activations and ablative wounds. The weakness is raw hitting power against high-toughness armour-save targets — when an opponent brings enough durable threats that the sheer weight of mediocre attacks can't close the efficiency gap, the list struggles to convert board presence into kills.
477: Built around Grey Hunters, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Priests, Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, Logan Grimnar, and Blood Claws, this is a mass-infantry melee brawler that floods the table with bodies across multiple detachment configurations. The plan is to overwhelm the mid-board through sheer model count and multi-threat pressure — characters buff adjacent infantry into combat, Terminators punch hard into priority targets, and Grey Hunters action-while-shooting to score secondaries without sacrificing board presence. It punishes gunline armies that lack the volume of shots needed to clear waves of cheap infantry before the melee tide crashes home. It cracks against elite or mechanized lists that can selectively delete key characters and Terminators early, stripping the buffs that hold the threat stack together.
478: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators in multiple squads, Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Thunderwolf Cavalry, and Wolf Guard Headtakers operating under Saga of the Great Wolf, this is a wall of elite, durable melee bodies that floods mid-table and dares the opponent to fight through it. The win condition is controlling the center through sheer physical presence — Terminators and Thunderwolves lock down key zones while Grimnar and Arjac amplify the kill output, turning the mid-board into a grinding attrition trap the opponent cannot safely ignore or bypass. It punishes shooting-heavy armies that lack the volume or AP to chew through multiple Terminator bricks efficiently, wearing them down faster than they can trade. It cracks open when faced with high-mobility alpha-strike lists or massed mortal wounds that sidestep the armor save wall entirely, bypassing the jam before it can be set.
480: Built around Armiger Warglaives, Armiger Helverins, a Knight Crusader, and a Knight Castellan, this list floods the table with medium and large walkers across every threat range. The plan is to apply relentless anti-armour pressure from multiple angles simultaneously — Helverins suppress at range while Warglaives chase down vehicles and monsters in melee, forcing opponents to split resources and concede priority targets. It punishes armour-heavy lists badly, stacking mobile anti-armour output that most vehicle-dense builds simply cannot absorb across multiple turns. Where it struggles is against elite infantry and screens: the list lacks the concentrated anti-horde volume to efficiently clear bodies off objectives, leaving it vulnerable to anything that can park cheap wounds in the way and deny scoring.
481: Built around the Knight Castellan, Armiger Warglaives, and Knight Crusader, this list leans into the Dominus Foebreakers detachment's core trick: friendly Dominus units gain +1 to hit rolls against targets sheltering in terrain, turning the board's cover into a liability for the opponent rather than a refuge. The plan is to advance aggressively with the Castellan and Crusader's massed firepower while Warglaives pressure flanks, punishing armies that castle in ruin clusters and scoring through attrition kills rather than passive objective sitting. It absolutely dismantles static gunlines and terrain-hugging elite infantry, where the hit bonus activates constantly and the volume of high-strength shooting creates anti-tank overload. It struggles against fast, mobile armies that can strip the Armigers early, deny the terrain hit bonus by staying in the open, and leverage the Knights' mediocre scoring efficiency against them.
482: Built around the Knight Castellan, Knight Crusader, Cerastus Knight Lancer, Armiger Warglaives, and Armiger Helverins, this is a mixed-arms Freeblade Company list that fields a sprawling household of independently operating war engines, each ticking back a wound per Command phase and shrugging damage on 6s. The plan is to apply layered anti-armour pressure across the whole board simultaneously — the Castellan and Crusader saturate targets with high-volume firepower while the Lancer and Warglaives hunt vehicles in melee, grinding opponents down through attrition rather than a single alpha strike. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to trade efficiently against multiple durable Titanic threats, especially when the passive wound regeneration keeps Knights alive through chip damage. Against armies that can concentrate overwhelming lethality onto one Knight at a time — or flood the board with screens to block the Lancer's charges — the build's relatively thin resilience and below-50% win rate expose it as susceptible to focused target priority.
483: Built around Broodlords, Genestealers, Biovores, Norn Emissaries, Neuroliictors, and the Red Terror, this is a high-mobility infiltration swarm that floods the midboard with fast, hard-hitting melee bodies while Biovores suppress backfield objective holders with indirect mortar fire. The win condition is board saturation — Neuroliictors and Lictors create infiltration corridors that let Genestealers threaten priority targets turn one, while Broodlords amplify their lethality and the Norn Emissary applies Singular Purpose pressure that forces opponents to either commit resources or cede scoring lanes. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot contest multiple simultaneous threats, overloading their damage allocation against a wave that replaces losses faster than it can be cleared. Mass blast weapons, high-volume indirect fire, and armies with strong screen saturation crack this list open by denying the approach corridors that make the Genestealer charge engine function.
484: Built around Norn Assimilators, Biovores, Pyrovores, Norn Emissaries, the Swarmlord, and Psychophages, this Assimilation Swarm list is a regenerating attrition engine that floods the midfield with durable, self-healing monstrosities. The win condition is grinding opponents down through the Harvester regeneration loop — returning slain Infantry models or healing wounded monstrosities each Command phase — while scoring objectives from a position of permanent board presence that opponents cannot permanently clear. It punishes lists relying on burst damage and alpha strikes, because healing and model restoration means the damage threshold required to actually remove units keeps climbing beyond what most lists can sustain in a single activation window. It cracks open against consistent high-volume anti-monster output or mass mortal wounds that outpace the regeneration ceiling, and elite low-model-count armies that can isolate and delete Harvesters before the loop even triggers.
485: Built around Norn Emissaries, Tyrannofexes, Maleceptors, Exocrines, Norn Assimilators, Biovores, and a Hive Tyrant, this is a wall of Tyranid Monsters under the Crusher Stampede detachment, where damaged units hit and wound more reliably, and healthy ones punch above their weight on objectives with boosted Objective Control. The plan is to flood mid-board with high-OC monsters that are actively harder to remove as they take wounds, while Tyrannofexes and Exocrines strip armour at range and Biovores suppress screens, creating a grinding attrition engine that scores through presence and resilience. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't efficiently saturate anti-monster firepower across so many large targets simultaneously. Armies that can mass mortal wounds, force Battle Shock at scale, or land a clean alpha strike that spikes multiple monsters below half early will short-circuit the damage-bonus engine before it gets rolling.
486: Built around near-five squads of Boyz averaging nearly five units deep, Painboys, Ghazghkull Thraka, Warbosses, Bigbosses, Kommandos, Stormboyz, Wazdakka Gutsmek, and a Weirdboy, this is a Green Tide detachment wall of Ork infantry designed to drown the table in green. The engine is Sustained Hits 1 on every Boyz melee attack combined with Lethal Hits against non-Monsters and non-Vehicles on any unit that charged, turning each successful charge wave into a cascading kill chain that scores through sheer combat attrition and objective flood. It punishes elite-infantry lists brutally — the raw volume of Lethal and Sustained hits overwhelms armies that rely on a small number of high-value bodies to hold the midfield. It cracks open against heavy Monster and Vehicle spam, where Lethal Hits are stripped away and the melee output drops sharply against the targets it most needs to remove.
487: Built around Squighog Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, Beastboss, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Kill Rigs, and Mozrog Skragbad, this is a wall of Beast Snagga muscle that floods the midboard and refuses to let go. The detachment's +1 AP against Monsters and Vehicles turns every charge into a lethal anti-armour chain, so the win condition is simple: crash into the opponent's big threats, strip their heavy hitters, and let the sheer volume of bodies bury objectives. Gretchin screens protect the advance while layered lethality means even elite combat armies struggle to chew through the horde before the Squighogs hit back harder. The build cracks when facing mass-ignore-AP shooting or long-range alpha strike lists that can thin the horde before it reaches combat range, since the whole engine stalls if the mob doesn't make contact.
488: Built around Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Gretchin screens, Lootas, Tankbustas, Big Mek Dakkarigs, Flash Gitz, and Trukk-delivered infantry, this Dread Mob list activates its Walker units each fight or shooting phase to roll one or two D6, generating randomised special rules that stack devastating offensive output on already-dangerous machines. The win condition is layered attrition and mid-board control: Gretchin and Zodgrod Wortsnagga's boosted screens absorb punishment while Trukks ferry Tankbustas into anti-armour range, Lootas and Flash Gitz punish anything that clusters, and Wazdakka threads mobile pressure between objectives. It absolutely punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot clear massed bodies before the Orks' kill chain assembles — the combination of screening, transport delivery, and stacked shooting overwhelms armies trading unit-for-unit. Where it cracks is sustained precision shooting or heavy blast weapons that collapse Gretchin screens early, exposing the expensive support pieces before the Walker threat engine can be properly activated.
489: Built around Scarab Occult Terminators led by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Rubric Marines holding ground, Sekhetar Robots providing durable bodies, and Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows providing skimming ranged pressure, this is a mass-horde Thousand Sons list running the Hexwarp Thrallband detachment, which unlocks Flow of Magic benefits tied to controlling your deployment zone and No Man's Land objectives. The plan is to flood the mid-table with overlapping waves of bodies, leverage Flow of Magic by contesting No Man's Land objectives early, and use Empyric Onslaught-buffed shooting and layered lethal combat output to grind opponents off points. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear volume, as the sheer number of durable infantry and robots creates an anti-tank overload problem while the Enlightened apply consistent ranged harassment. Armies with strong area-denial tools or high-volume mortal wound output can crack the formation open by preventing the Flow of Magic activation and isolating the slower Terminator elements.
490: Built around Sekhetar Robots, Forgefiends, Defilers, Tzaangor Shamans, Exalted Sorcerers on Disc, Ahriman, and Rubric Marines, this is a psychically-supercharged vehicle gunline that turns its robots and daemon engines into Psyker-buffed killing machines under the Sekhetar Cohort and Warpforged Cabal detachments. The win condition is layering Psyker auras — Shamans and Sorcerers pushing +1 WS onto Robots while keeping Vehicles within 6" of Psykers to fish re-rolls on hits, wounds, and damage — grinding opponents down through sustained, accurate firepower across mid and long range. It punishes slower armoured lists that can't avoid the gunline footprint, overwhelming them with mobile anti-armour pressure from multiple Forgefiends and Defilers that are nearly impossible to screen against simultaneously. It cracks open when fast, high-volume chaff floods its Psyker bubble, stripping the aura coverage and collapsing the re-roll engine before the Robots can swing back.
492: Built around Custodian Guard, Allarus Custodians, Blade Champion, Custodian Wardens, Vertus Praetors, Witchseekers, and Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, this is a mobile elite infantry force running Shield Host — rotating each battle round between a Critical Hit threshold on melee attacks or improved Armour Penetration across the force. The plan is to threaten multiple vectors simultaneously: Allarus Custodians ingress and charge with re-roll support from Tharanatoi Hammerblow while Vertus Praetors and Witchseekers provide speed and screening to control the midboard and grind objectives through attrition. It punishes elite-light armies that can't generate enough volume of attacks to trade efficiently against the faction's characteristically tough multi-wound models. However, it cracks open under high-volume shooting from horde armies or lists that can reliably deny ingress lanes, stranding its key hammer units outside effective charge range.
499: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, Castigators, Immolators, and a deep roster of jump-pack infantry — Zephyrim, Seraphim, and Canonesses — this is an aggressive, layered force that floods the table with fast bodies and vehicle firepower. The engine is the Army of Faith detachment's double Act of Faith per phase, letting the army squeeze extra actions, rerolls, or surges of movement out of nearly every unit every turn, enabling a tempo-forward game of scoring primaries while threatening everything at range and in melee simultaneously. Castigators and Exorcists punish slow, armour-heavy lists that can't close the distance, while Immolator-mounted Dominions apply mobile anti-armour pressure that demands answers from multiple angles at once. The build struggles against fast, high-volume shooting that can strip its medium-wound vehicles and elite infantry before the double-Act economy pays off, since losing key pieces early collapses both the damage output and the objective control simultaneously.
505: Built around Techmarines (nearly two per list), Redemptor Dreadnoughts, Brutalis Dreadnoughts, and Ballistus Dreadnoughts, this is a mechanised wall of armoured walkers kept fighting by constant repair support, operating under Ironstorm Spearhead's per-phase re-roll on hit, wound, or damage for every Adeptus Astartes unit. The plan is to park a durable firebase of Ballistus and Redemptor firepower that grinds opponents down at range while Brutalis Dreadnoughts crash forward to contest mid-table and bully anything they reach. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't trade efficiently into multiple hard targets simultaneously, since the Techmarines keep the walkers operational and the per-unit re-rolls sustain output across the whole line. It cracks when faced with enough volume or high-damage anti-tank to overwhelm both the repair loop and the re-roll cushion before the Brutalis threat forces a response.
515: Built around twin Broodlords leading multiple Genestealer units, with Biovores, Maleceptors, Hormagaunts, Neurolictor, Lictor, and Norn Emissary filling out the roster under Invasion Fleet, this is a mobile, multi-threat swarm that floods every lane simultaneously. The core engine is Broodlord-buffed Genestealers crashing into mid-table on priority turns while chaff units like Hormagaunts contest secondaries and Biovores pressure backfield screens from range. It punishes infantry-heavy armies through sheer volume of attacks — the Invasion Fleet Hyper-adaptation amplifies output further against Infantry and Swarm targets — while the Neurolictor and Lictor layer disruption and deep-strike pressure onto opponents trying to stabilise. Dense elite armies with durable multi-wound models that laugh off low-AP swings can absorb the initial charge and grind back against a list that has limited staying power once its strike units are spent.
517: Built around near-paired Doomsday Arks, Canoptek Wraiths, the Silent King, Ophydian Destroyers, Flayed Ones, and the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, supported by Technomancers keeping it all breathing, this is a mobile ranged-firepower list that uses the Starshatter Arsenal detachment's objective-range hit bonus and ASSAULT keyword on vehicle weapons to shoot efficiently while moving. The win condition is contesting objectives aggressively so that Doomsday Arks fire at full accuracy while Wraiths, Ophydians, and Flayed Ones flood midboard with bodies that demand answers, Chrono-impedance Fields buying extra time for Technomancer-driven reanimation to cycle wounds back. It punishes lists that rely on volume infantry or slow-developing gunlines, where the hit bonus activates constantly and the layered melee threats make clearing objectives genuinely costly. Highly mobile elite armies or alpha-strike builds that can kill Doomsday Arks before they generate value — and deny the objective-proximity trigger — expose the list's reliance on that single synergistic condition.
518: Built around Skorpekh Lords leading Skorpekh Destroyer blobs under Awakened Dynasty's +1 to Hit aura, the Void Dragon, Nekrosor Ammentar, Illuminor Szeras, the Silent King, and a Lokhust Lord shepherding Heavy Destroyers, this list floods the board with layered threats across every range band. The engine is relentless mid-board pressure: Awakened Dynasty's hit bonus supercharges Skorpekh melee packets while the Void Dragon and Heavy Destroyers crack armour from range, forcing opponents to answer multiple kill vectors simultaneously. It punishes lists that concentrate resources on a single threat type, since spreading anti-tank to stop the Destroyers leaves the Skorpekh wave untouched and vice versa. It struggles against armies that can deny its approach corridors or tarpit the Skorpekh units before they swing, bleeding the hit-bonus packets through screens before they reach their targets.
521: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams, Ghostkeels, Riptides, Broadsides, and Commander Shadowsun operating under Advanced Acquisition Cadre and Kauyon, this list leans on hidden shooting — Stealth Battlesuits and Pathfinder Teams fire without breaking concealment — then transitions into a Kauyon-fueled late-game firepower spike from rounds three through five, where everything gains Sustained Hits 1 and Guided units ignore modifiers when targeting Spotted enemies. The win condition is attrition: screen with Piranhas and Vespid Stingwings to deny forward pressure, accumulate mid-game objective presence, and then overwhelm with amplified shooting once Kauyon activates. It punishes slow, durable armour-heavy lists by combining mobile anti-armour tools with the late-round damage multiplier to crack tough targets that other armies would stall against. Lists that alpha-strike the screening layer early or flood the midboard before Kauyon comes online deny it the time it needs to snowball.
522: Built around deep-striking Cthonian Beserks (averaging four squads) delivered en masse alongside Einhyr Hearthguard, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and a supporting web of Hernkyn Pioneers, Yaegirs, and Kapricus Carriers, this is a Dêlve Assault Shift list that floods the midboard with tough, aggressive infantry. The engine is volume and threat saturation — Beserks drop from deep strike to contest or clear objectives while Hearthguard and Land Fortresses anchor fire lanes, with the Hearthguard Covenant's wound-reroll-within-9" sharpening close-range shooting into a reliable kill chain. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that struggle to screen every angle simultaneously, drowning them in multi-vector pressure no single gunline can efficiently answer. However, high-lethality alpha-strike armies and anything with robust board-wide screening can strangle the deep strike timing and isolate the Beserks before they reach mass-action range, leaving the list overextended and unable to recover primary momentum.
524: Built around Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and Jump Pack Assault Intercessors supported by Scout and Intercessor screens, this is a Wrath of the Rock list that makes its elite infantry punishingly hard to wound by subtracting 1 from wound rolls whenever the attacker's Strength exceeds the target's Toughness. The plan is to park durable, high-threat melee hammers on objectives while Azrael and the Lion stack buffs and presence, grinding opponents down in a war of attrition they cannot win on raw damage output. It punishes anti-elite overload lists that rely on high-Strength, moderate-volume firepower — the wound-roll penalty turns those attacks into statistical dead ends. However, it struggles against lists that bypass the detachment ability entirely through weight of low-Strength shots or mortal wound spam, and the overall power ceiling leaves it thin against top-tier meta pressure.
525: Built around Sammael, Lion El'Jonson, Azrael, Land Speeder Vengeances, Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Outriders, the Ravenwing Command Squad, Deathwing Knights, and Scout screens operating under the Company of Hunters detachment, this is a fast, gun-heavy swarm that shoots on the move without penalty and falls back freely without losing its firepower. The kill chain runs through a wall of skimmer and mounted platforms advancing or falling back and still unloading full volleys, while Darkflight Pursuit strips cover saves from every RAVENWING FLY unit's ranged attacks to punish anything hiding in terrain. It brutalises gunline and horde armies that rely on cover and static positioning, because their primary defensive layer simply doesn't function against this volume of IGNORES COVER fire. Tight deployment and elite melee threats — particularly units that can lock speeders in combat before they retreat — are its genuine crack, since the build's durability is spread thin across individually fragile platforms.
526: Built around Lokhust Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, Ophydian Destroyers, Lokhust Lords, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, Lychguard, and the Overlord with Translocation Shroud, this is a multi-vector Necron murder machine that floods the board with fast, durable threat vectors across multiple phases. The plan is to overwhelm opponents by projecting lethal ranged pressure through Lokhust Destroyers and the Void Dragon while Ophydian Destroyers threaten sudden melee eruptions from unexpected angles, forcing opponents to defend multiple kill zones simultaneously rather than concentrating resources. Its high mobility toolkit punishes slower, static gunlines that can't reposition quickly enough to address threats from all directions at once. It cracks open against tight alpha-strike armies and anything capable of stripping the Lokhust Destroyers before they activate, since losing that ranged backbone early collapses the layered threat structure the entire plan depends on.
528: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Arjac Rockfist, and Grey Hunters flooding the board under the Saga of the Great Wolf detachment, this is a high-model-count melee brawler that uses the Veterans of the Fang rule to keep Grey Hunters scoring actions while the heavy hitters punch forward. The win condition is cycling Hunting Packs turn-by-turn — Encircling Jaws to guarantee charge ranges on Terminators and Headtakers, then shifting buffs to sustain pressure — while Grey Hunters hold and contest objectives without sacrificing their shooting eligibility. It punishes attrition-based gunlines that expect to bleed out a melee force through sheer volume of durable, multi-purpose bodies that contest every corner of the board simultaneously. It cracks against elite alpha-strike armies that can delete the Terminator and Headtaker packages before they close distance, stranding the slower Grey Hunter screens with nothing to protect.
529: Built around Grey Hunters, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, Wolf Scouts, and Ragnar Blackmane, this is a mass-infantry assault force running Saga of the Beastslayer, which grants Lethal Hits on every attack targeting Characters, Monsters, or Vehicles across the entire Adeptus Astartes roster. The win condition is flooding mid-table with bodies while the Lethal Hits engine dismantles whatever elite or armoured anchor the opponent relies on — Grey Hunters holding actions under Veterans of the Fang while combat units punch up into high-value targets. It punishes lists built around one or two expensive centrepiece units, since Lethal Hits converts raw volume of attacks into consistent character and vehicle kills without needing high AP. Armies that spread threat across many small cheap units dilute the Beastslayer engine and can outgrind the relatively fragile infantry core through attrition.
530: Built around Allarus Custodians, Vertus Praetors, Witchseekers, Custodian Wardens, Prosecutors, Valerian, and Shield-Captains on Dawneagle Jetbikes, this list runs the Lions of the Emperor detachment, which grants +1 to hit and +1 to wound on any non-Vehicle Custodes unit operating without friendly models within 6" — rewarding deliberate spacing over tight castle play. The win condition is isolating individual Custodes units to trigger that bonus and then hunting priority targets with elite melee and mobile shooting, using fast units like Praetors and Prosecutors to apply board pressure while Allarus Custodians drop onto backfield threats. It punishes elite, low-model-count lists brutally, because the hit-and-wound bonus compounds against high-toughness targets and turns every Custodian into an over-statted assassin. Dense screen armies and horde factions that deny clean isolation windows crack this build open, forcing units into proximity and stripping the detachment's entire offensive engine.
533: Built around multiple Commanders in Coldstar Battlesuits, Crisis Sunforge and Starscythe Battlesuits, The Twin Lance, Commander Farsight, Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams with Darkstrider, Broadsides, and Crisis Fireknife Battlesuits running Experimental Prototype Cadre plus Kauyon — every Battlesuit Character's guns reach 6" further, and from round three onward the whole force gains Sustained Hits 1 plus the ability to ignore modifiers when Guided units target Spotted enemies. The plan is to spend early turns screening and positioning while Pathfinders spot targets, then detonate into a mid-table brawl from round three when Kauyon activates, stacking Sustained Hits 1 onto high-volume anti-armour Crisis and Coldstar payloads to delete hard targets and bury opponents in VP. It punishes durable, low-model-count elite armies that want to trade units slowly, because the Sustained Hits surge turns already efficient anti-armour firepower into an overload their saves cannot absorb. Armies that alpha strike before round three or flood the board with cheap screens crack it open, denying the Kauyon payoff window and blocking Pathfinder spot-chains before they mature.
534: Built around Hekaton Land Fortresses, Sagitaurs, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Einhyr Hearthguard, and a broad infantry core of Kapricus Defenders, Hearthkyn Warriors, and Hernkyn Pioneers pushing up the middle, this is a mechanised gunline that fights firmly in the mid-table. The plan is to flood objectives with transport-delivered infantry while Thunderkyn and Hekatons saturate the midfield with sustained fire, pressuring the opponent to either contest on unfavorable terms or cede board control entirely. It punishes slower, durable armies that want to trade efficiently at range — the sheer volume of bodies and armoured chassis makes clean removal difficult before Einhyr Hearthguard close the distance. However, fast alpha-strike lists that can strip transports early and isolate the infantry core expose how dependent the build is on its vehicles staying alive.
537: Built around Plague Marines hauled up the board in Chaos Rhinos, Poxwalkers screening wide, a Biologus Putrifier amplifying plague weapon output, Deathshroud Terminators threatening deep strikes, a Malignant Plaguecaster, Lord of Contagion, Tallyman, and Daemon Prince of Nurgle rounding out the command structure, this is a Virulent Vectorium attrition engine. The plan is to plant Death Guard bodies on objectives, flip them to secured status at Command phase end, and let the Afflicted condition grind down anything that tries to contest — while layered plague weapon lethality punishes any unit that lingers nearby. It punishes mid-range brawler armies that need to hold ground: the combination of secured objectives, Afflicted harassment, and lethal close combat output makes trading into this list expensive. It struggles against fast, hard-hitting lists that can alpha-strike the Rhinos before deployment completes and deny the Command phase window needed to activate the Virulent Vectorium engine.
540: Built around Vindicators, Sanguinary Guard, Jump Pack Captains, Sanguinary Priests, and Bladeguard Veterans, this list pairs heavy armoured firepower with a fast-moving elite infantry core under the Angelic Inheritors detachment, selecting two Angelic Legacy buffs — most commonly Sanguinary Grace — to unlock aggressive repositioning for Character units. The engine is a layered pressure game: Vindicators blast midfield from distance while buffed Sanguinary Guard and Captains skirmish forward, using fell-back-and-shoot flexibility to keep scoring angles open across multiple turns. It punishes mid-density infantry armies that can't screen the advance, as the combined gunline and melee toolkit overwhelms defensive lines before they can reset. However, it struggles against high-volume anti-armour lists that can strip Vindicators early, gutting the fire-support backbone and leaving the elite infantry over-extended.
541:
Built around a Chaos Lord with Jump Pack leading multiple units of Raptors and Warp Talons, backed by Cultist Mob screens, Chosen, and Defilers, this is a mobile assault force running primarily Murdertalon Raiders — a detachment that rewards punishing weakened or battle-shocked enemies with re-rolled hit rolls and imposes -1 to hit on those same damaged units attacking back.

The plan is to strip enemy units below half-strength through Defiler fire and jump-pack harassment, then crash Warp Talons and Raptors into those degraded targets with full re-roll support, compounding the damage advantage each activation.

It punishes mid-table brawlers and infantry-heavy lists that can't avoid being whittled down, since the hit-bonus feedback loop accelerates once any unit starts bleeding.

It struggles against durable elite armies with high starting wounds-per-model that resist the below-half threshold trigger, leaving its primary re-roll engine inactive when the fight starts.
542: Built around Noise Marines, Chaos Bikers, Chosen, and Rhino-mounted infantry led by Huron Blackheart and supported by Defilers and a Lord Discordant, this is a Renegade Raiders force that blankets the table with Assault-capable ranged weapons and mobile anti-armour pressure across every phase. The win condition is objective-zone attrition: the detachment's AP improvement on attacks targeting units within range of objective markers means every firefight contested near a point punishes defenders harder, while Bikers and Raiders push into scoring positions early. It punishes static gunlines and armour-heavy lists by combining the Lord Discordant's anti-vehicle reach with Defiler fire and the sheer volume of Noise Marine shooting, all with move-and-fire freedom. Aggressive melee alpha-strike armies that can charge before this list settles onto objectives, or elite MSU builds that deny the clustered midboard fights this list needs, will crack it open.
543: Built around Talos pain engines and Cronos parasite engines as the haemonculi-flesh backbone, wrapped in Venoms and Raiders ferrying Incubi, Wyches, Wracks, and Kabalite Warriors across the table, with Scourges providing heavy-weapon reach, Mandrakes adding board-pressure, and the full suite of Drukhari characters sharpening every edge. The Realspace Raiders detachment's Harlequin and Anhrathe inclusion window layers additional threat vectors onto an already wide roster, flooding every lane while Talos and Cronos grind into mid-board brawls and skimmer-mounted infantry contest or deny objectives from turn one. This build punishes elite low-model armies brutally — the sheer volume of bodies, transport-delivered assault threats, and layered lethality overwhelm lists that can't deal with simultaneous multi-flank pressure. It cracks open against high-volume anti-infantry firepower or aggressive alpha-strike lists that can strip Venoms early, collapsing the transport engine before the infantry waves can deliver.
544: Built around multiple Skorpekh Lord-led Skorpekh Destroyer units, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, Nekrosor Ammentar, Illuminor Szeras, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers under Lokhust Lords, the Silent King, and Ophydian Destroyers, this Awakened Dynasty list weaponizes the detachment's +1 to Hit across nearly every combat and shooting unit on the table. The win condition is layered threat saturation — Ophydians and Skorpekhs hunt infantry midboard while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers and the Void Dragon crack vehicles, with Enaegic Dermal Bond keeping lead characters alive long enough to cycle damage into scoring turns.
