It punishes lists with spread-out, mid-toughness targets that can't absorb simultaneous melee and heavy anti-armour pressure from multiple angles. Concentrated alpha-strike armies or elite high-damage output can strip the attached characters before the hit-bonus engine fires, unraveling the whole threat package.
546:
Built around the Void Dragon, the Nightbringer, Immortals, and Flayed Ones under Hand of the Dynasty, this list fields multiple god-tier monsters as its primary damage dealers while Immortals push objectives with Assault-tagged shooting even after advancing.

The plan is to position C'tan as mobile, near-unkillable threats that force your opponent into impossible trades — while Flayed Ones pressure flanks and Immortals generate actions without sacrificing fire, accumulating primary points steadily.

It punishes elite low-model-count lists that can't produce enough concentrated damage to reliably kill multiple monsters in a single round, spreading their anti-tank thin across several nightmare targets.

The weakness is raw damage output against armies that can simply ignore the monsters and drown Immortals and Flayed Ones in volume, leaving the C'tan stranded without meaningful board control to back them up.
547: Built around Tech-Priest Enginseers, Scout Sentinels, Lord Solar Leontus, a Baneblade, and a Banesword, this list is a super-heavy gunline that uses Steel Hammer to fire its Titanic and Squadron units point-blank into engaged enemies without penalty, while Designation Force's designating mechanic extends detection range to strip cover and expose targets for the armour column. The win condition is straightforward attrition: keep the superheavies repaired and operational via Enginseers, use Sentinels to scout-screen and spot targets, then grind opposing armies under sustained high-volume, high-damage fire from multiple Titanic platforms simultaneously. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot flood the board fast enough to tie up multiple superheavies before the guns delete them piecemeal. Swarm lists and anything with reliable multi-turn melee access crack it open, since locking even one superheavy in combat neutralises its firepower and Enginseer repairs cannot keep pace with concentrated close-range punishment.
548: Built around Leman Russ Battle Tanks, Leman Russ Exterminators, Rogal Dorn Commanders, and Hellhounds, with Tempestus Scions, Tempestus Aquilons, Scout Sentinels, and Cadian Shock Troops rounding out the force under Bridgehead Strike. The plan is to flood the board with armour and drop Scions mid-game with +1 to hit on arrival, using Combined Arms' Lethal Hits on Squadron units to crack opposing vehicles while the Russ gunline and Hellhounds grind anything that contests objectives. It punishes elite-light armies that lack anti-tank overload by drowning them in durable vehicles that require more firepower to remove than they typically carry. It cracks open against high-volume anti-tank spam or alpha-strike lists that can strip the armoured core before the Scions' drop amplifies output enough to matter.
550: Built around Lords of Change and Plaguebearers, this list blends high-mobility Tzeentch shooting and spellcasting monsters with durable Nurgle bodies that contest objectives and absorb punishment. The win condition is layered threat saturation — Lords of Change hammer priority targets from range or combat while Plaguebearers and Beasts of Nurgle (present in nearly half of lists) lock down midfield objectives, forcing opponents to either trade inefficiently into tough infantry or let the big daemons operate freely. The Lords of the Warp detachment's +1 Leadership and OC on CHARACTER models amplifies the objective-hold game, and the Infernal Puppeteer enhancement (carried in half of lists) squeezes extra value from the daemon character toolkit against armies that can't efficiently remove multiple large threats simultaneously. Lists that can project lethal, high-volume anti-monster firepower at range while simultaneously clearing Plaguebearer screens will crack this open, since the build has no hard answer to being pressured on both axes at once.
551:
Built around Skarbrand, Flesh Hounds, Rendmasters on Blood Throne, Bloodcrushers, Skullmasters, Bloodletters, and Bloodthirster, this is an all-Khorne Blood Legion list that weaponizes reactive movement — whenever enemy units end a move within 8" of a Khorne Daemon unit, the army surges forward up to D6" for free, collapsing charge distances before the opponent can react.

The plan is to drown the midboard in multiple overlapping threat vectors simultaneously: Bloodcrushers and Flesh Hounds avalanche into objectives while Skarbrand and the Bloodthirster hunt priority targets, creating an anti-tank and brawling kill chain that is nearly impossible to address all at once.

It punishes slow or low-mobility armies brutally, as the surge mechanic rewards opponents who move at all and turns normal repositioning into an invitation.

Dense elite melee armies that can absorb the initial wave and fight back in kind, or fast screens that prevent the surge triggers from compressing charge distances, can stall the engine before it snowballs.
552:
Built around Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts as the heavy firepower core, screened by Scout and Intercessor squads, with Marneus Calgar and Victrix Honour Guard anchoring the center and Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs providing aggressive flanking pressure under the Gladius Task Force's Combat Doctrines.

The plan is to cycle Devastator Doctrine early to let Executioners advance and shoot without penalty, pouring macro-elimination firepower into priority targets while Jump Pack Intercessors and scouts contest objectives and force opponents to split attention between the guns and the pressure elements.

This list punishes static, elite armies that can't clear screens quickly — the layered Scout and Intercessor bubble absorbs incoming fire long enough for the guns to delete key pieces.

It cracks badly against fast, aggressive alpha-strike builds that can close the distance before the gunline stabilises, overwhelming the relatively fragile screen and getting into melee where the Executioners become liabilities.
554: Built around Aethon Shaan, Jump Pack Assault Intercessors, Kayvaan Shrike, Inceptors, and Vanguard Veterans with Jump Packs, this is a Shadowmark Talon list that floods the mid-board with fast FLY INFANTRY and exploits Shaan's Unparalled Tactician ability to fire off the Into Darkness Stratagem for free, enabling repeated zero-cost ingress plays. The engine is a rolling aerial threat: units drop in via ingress or charge, the Vengeful Hosts secondary detachment rewards that aggression with hit-roll re-rolls on 1s, and Centurion Devastators anchor the backline as a heavy gunline deterrent while jump units chase primaries. It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't maintain 12" range on everything, as the Shadowmark Talon cover-at-range rule makes the whole army extremely tax-heavy to shoot off objectives. Anything that can close that 12" bubble — dense melee armies or fast cavalry that flood your air space — deflates the cover bubble and exposes how relatively fragile the infantry core actually is.
556: Built around Squighog Boyz, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Beast Snagga Boyz, and Ghazghkull Thraka in the Freebooter Krew detachment, this is a midfield brawler that floods the table with mounted monsters, infantry hordes, and Trukk-delivered Boyz simultaneously. The engine is Freebooter Krew's loot objective designation combined with Sustained Hits 1 across all Mounted and Infantry attacks, letting the army generate absurd volume in melee while contesting and converting the loot marker into scoring pressure every Command phase. It punishes elite low-model armies brutally — the sheer attack count from Squighogs and Beast Snaggas overwhelms anything relying on a small number of tough units to hold the centre. Armies that can shut down the midfield approach with strong shooting or hard alpha strikes before the wave arrives will crack it open, since the build's durability depends on getting into combat, not surviving the approach.
557: Built around Beast Snagga Boyz, Beastboss characters, Squighog Boyz, Boyz, Gretchin screens, Kill Rig, Ghazghkull Thraka, Mozrog Skragbad, Painboy support, and Kommandos, this is a thundering green tide that floods the midboard with expendable bodies and hard-hitting Beast Snagga units. The plan is to plant multiple massive infantry blobs on objectives while Squighog Boyz and Ghazghkull punch through whatever is holding them, generating pressure across every lane simultaneously. It punishes elite low-model armies badly — those opponents simply cannot kill enough models fast enough to deny board control before the Orks crush them in melee. Tightly packed, high-damage shooting armies that can thin the horde before contact, combined with anti-horde area denial, are the primary threat, as losing model count early collapses the combat weight the list depends on.
558: Built around Warbikers, Deffkoptas, Deffkilla Wartrikes, Wazdakka Gutsmek, Big Mek Dakkarigs, and Trukk-delivered infantry, this Kult of Speed list floods the midboard with fast SPEED FREEKS units that can advance or fall back and still shoot and charge in the same turn. The engine is relentless positional pressure — units swing in, trade, fall back through opponents, then immediately threaten another charge, keeping scoring lanes open while grinding enemies off objectives through layered melee and dakka. It punishes static gunlines and low-mobility lists that cannot reposition fast enough to deny the constant advance-assault loop across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It struggles against armies that can reliably screen the midboard and tank the initial wave, because the Gretchin chaff is thin and losing momentum on the advance-charge chain bleeds activations the list cannot afford.
559: Built around Gretchin screens, Meks, Big Mek Dakkarigs, Boyz mobs, and a Stompa as the centrepiece, this is a mid-board brawling horde that grinds forward under the cover of cheap bodies. The Dread Mob's random-or-chosen weapon-ability table on Walkers and Mek units is the engine — players either gamble for a high-variance roll or lock in a reliable buff, letting the Stompa and Dakkarigs punch exactly where needed while Boyz flood objectives. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't clear the layered Gretchin screens fast enough, leaving objectives contested while the Walkers grind through armour. However, high-volume mortal-wound output or hard alpha strikes that drop the Stompa early collapse the list's damage ceiling and leave the horde without its primary kill piece.
560: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened, Sekhetar Robots buffed by Sorcerers (including Terminators), Scarab Occult Terminators, Rubric Marines, Daemon Princes, and Magnus the Red, this list runs the Hexwarp Thrallband detachment to project a Flow of Magic across No Man's Land whenever it controls half the midfield objectives, unlocking army-wide Psychic synergies — and pairs it with Sekhetar Cohort to grant Robots Psychic attacks and WS buffs from nearby Psykers. The win condition is layered, simultaneous pressure: Robots and Terminators brawl for midfield markers to trigger and sustain Flow of Magic while Enlightened and gunline elements delete screens, forcing opponents into no-win trades. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot contest multiple objectives simultaneously against this volume of Psychic-tagged melee and ranged threat across every zone. It cracks open against fast alpha-strike lists that can collapse midfield control early and sever Flow of Magic before the kill engine comes online.
561: Built around Scarab Occult Terminators led by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Rubric Marines, Tzaangors, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, and Sekhetar Robots, this is a mass-infantry horde that layers durable, multi-wound bodies across the table in the Rubricae Phalanx detachment, which grants Rubricae models an additional +1 to armour saves against all damage-1 attacks. The plan is to flood mid-table with bodies that are effectively unkillable by small-arms fire, using that staying power to contest objectives while Enlightened and Robots contribute ranged and melee pressure. It absolutely punishes gunlines and horde-killers that rely on high-volume, low-damage output, since the detachment ability turns their primary tool into wasted shots. Where it cracks is against high-damage multi-wound weapons — anything spiking Damage 2 or higher bypasses the detachment ability entirely and tears through Terminators faster than the numbers can compensate.
565: Built around Forgefiends, Defilers, Slaughterbounds, and waves of Eightbound and Exalted Eightbound, this Brazen Engines list fields a mass of Daemon Vehicles and Khornate infantry that hits every part of the board simultaneously. The win condition is anti-armour overload: Forgefiends and Defilers strip vehicles and heavy targets at range while Slaughterbounds and Eightbound crash into melee, with Jakhals screening and Daemon Princes of Khorne amplifying the assault, and Terror of Khorne forcing battle-shock on anything caught in the Fight phase. It punishes armies built around expensive elite units or armoured columns, where the sheer volume of mobile anti-armour threats creates impossible priority decisions. The build cracks under sustained ranged firepower that can delete daemon engines before they arrive, as losing the shooting base early leaves the melee wave unsupported and vulnerable to being isolated and ground down.
571: Built around Thulia Ghuld, Belisarius Cawl, and a core of Skorpius Disintegrators, Ironstrider Ballistarii, and Onager Dunecrawlers, all running under Cohort Cybernetica's +2" Move and boosted Objective Control on Legio Cybernetica units, supported by a deep bench of Servitor Battleclades, Tech-Priest Enginseers, and Skitarii Rangers screening the advance. The plan is to push mobile anti-armour platforms into mid-table early, leverage elevated OC from Cohort Cybernetica to contest objectives while the gunline tears apart vehicles, with Cawl and the Enginseers — hardened by Lords of the Forge's 4+ Invulnerable and Feel No Pain 5+ — keeping the repair engine running through sustained attrition. It punishes mechanised and vehicle-heavy lists brutally, combining skimmer firepower with massed Disintegrator output to overload anti-tank capacity. Pure elite melee armies that can close fast and bypass the screen will crack it open before the repair loop stabilises.
572: Built around Purestrain Genestealers, Aberrants, Abominants, and a Patriarch backed by wall-to-wall Acolyte Hybrids, Neophyte Hybrids, and Achilles Ridgerunners, this is Biosanctic Broodsurge at its most suffocating. The engine is a charge-amplified blender: Biosanctic Broodsurge's bonus Attacks on the charge turns Purestrain Genestealers and Aberrants into disproportionate melee threats, while Neophytes holding terrain regenerate wounds each Command phase to keep objectives locked and screening intact all game. It punishes low-model-count elite armies brutally — the sheer volume of charging bodies overwhelms combat attrition math, and Ridgerunners provide consistent anti-armour reach that forces opponents to split focus. Mass indirect fire, high-volume mortal wound output, or a fast alpha strike that removes the charge wave before it lands will crack this list wide open.
575: Built around Hellions, Wyches, Incubi, Reavers, and a dense Venom fleet, this is a mass-infantry Wych Cult list that floods the board with cheap bodies disembarking from skimmers. Exhibition Of Slaughter grants all Wych Cult melee attacks Lethal Hits against non-Monster/Vehicle targets, turning every chaff brawl into a delete button — Wyches and Hellions pile into screens and infantry blobs and simply erase them while Scourges handle armor from range. It punishes elite-infantry lists ruthlessly, where Lethal Hits compound across multiple units and the sheer volume of attacks overwhelms save efficiency. It cracks against heavy armored armies and anything with durable Monsters or Vehicles, since the Lethal Hits clause explicitly excludes those target types, leaving the melee engine underperforming against the hardest targets on the table.
576: Built around Warp Spiders, Howling Banshees, Swooping Hawks, Dark Reapers, Fire Dragons, and a supporting cast of nearly every Aeldari Aspect Warrior shrine, this list leans hard into the Aspect Host detachment's ability to reroll hit or wound rolls of 1 on every Aspect Warrior and Avatar each phase. The plan is overwhelming layered lethality — mobile units like Swooping Hawks and Warp Spiders harass and score while Fire Dragons and Dark Reapers strip armour and delete priority targets, with Jain Zar, Asurmen, Fuegan, and Lhykhis amplifying their respective shrines into precision kill chains. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't absorb the sheer volume of accurate, lethal attacks landing from multiple angles simultaneously. Horde armies and lists with durable screening units crack it open by absorbing its relatively thin bodies and denying the clean combat engagements and sightlines this build needs to convert its damage output into board control.
577: Built around Windriders, Warlock Skyrunners, Shining Spears, Shroud Runners, Rangers, War Walkers, Eldrad Ulthran, and Farseer Skyrunners, this list combines Path of the Outcast's detection-forcing mechanic with Windrider Host's reserve-delay rule to flood the board with fast skimmer units arriving on their own schedule. The engine is layered lethal pressure: Rangers and Shroud Runners bait enemy positioning while mounted units surge from reserves to contest objectives and stack Shining Spear lance charges against whatever is most exposed. It punishes slow, static armies that cannot reposition to answer multiple mobile threats arriving at staggered intervals across multiple flanks. However, concentrated alpha-strike lists that can delete key mounted units before they cycle through reserves, or armies with hard anti-screening tools that strip the Ranger/Shroud Runner detection layer early, leave the reserve timing engine exposed and the scoring engine stalled.
579: Built around Doomsday Arks, Canoptek Wraiths, Skorpekh Lords and Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Flayed Ones, Hexmark Destroyers, Imotekh, Canoptek Reanimators, and Technomancers operating under Awakened Dynasty's +1 to Hit for CHARACTER-led units, this is a highly mobile toolbox army that floods the board with fast, resilient threats across every phase. The win condition is multi-vector pressure — Wraiths and Ophydians contest midfield while Destroyers hunt priority targets with character-boosted accuracy, Doomsday Arks crack armour at range, and Flayed Ones punish overextension. It excels against slower, static armies that struggle to handle simultaneous threats arriving from multiple angles before they can be prioritised and eliminated. However, high-volume mortal wound output or elite melee that bypasses reanimation can dismantle the layered durability, and a true alpha strike that removes the CHARACTER leaders collapses the hit-bonus engine before it fires.
580: Built around Doomsday Arks, Flayed Ones, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, and the C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, this list plants heavy artillery in a protected backfield castle while mobile threats roam forward to threaten objectives and key targets. The Doomsday Arks anchor the firebase, layering anti-tank firepower from range while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers add concentrated armour-cracking shots, and the Nightbringer threatens anything that pushes into midfield. Flayed Ones provide aggressive board pressure and objective harassment, forcing opponents to either overcommit to chasing them or cede ground to the castle. The build punishes slow, durable armies that want to grind forward into ranged fire, but aggressive alpha-strike lists that close distance quickly can outpace the damage output and crack the firebase before the heavy guns can answer.
581: Built around Inquisitor Kroyle, massed Subductor Squads, Sisters of Battle embarked in Immolators, Imperial Navy Breachers, and a full suite of Assassins — Callidus, Vindicare, and Eversor — this is a swarming, transport-heavy gunline that floods the board with cheap bodies and skimmer-mounted firepower. The engine is threat multiplication: Assassins double up their signature abilities across the battle through Veiled Blade, while Immolators push Sisters into scoring range and Imperialis Fleet's command-phase focus amplifies hit rolls against priority targets or locks down key objectives. It punishes lists that rely on elite, low-model-count armies by drowning them in activations, layered small-arms fire, and the perpetual pressure of Kroyle's retinue contesting every corner. Against armies with high-volume, multi-damage shooting or strong combat clearance, the horde thins fast and the individually fragile units struggle to survive long enough to execute their multi-round ability cycling.
583: Built around Kasrkin, Cadian Shock Troops, and Chimeras supported by a dense officer corps of Cadian Castellans and Command Squads, this is a mechanised gunline that floods the table with Orders-buffed infantry firing from transports and dug-in positions, with Bullgryns providing a close-range anvil and Tech-Priest Enginseers keeping vehicles in the fight. The win condition is volume attrition — Officers stack Orders to trigger re-rolls on hit rolls of 1 across multiple units simultaneously, letting Kasrkin and Shock Troops punch well above their points while Chimeras project threat across mid-board objectives. It punishes horde and medium-infantry lists badly, overwhelming them with mass re-rolled fire before they can trade efficiently. However, elite low-model-count armies that can isolate and delete the officer bubble or hard-target the lightly armoured Chimeras will collapse the Order chain and gut the build's output.
584: Built around Krieg Combat Engineers, Tempestus Scions with Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Gaunt's Ghosts, Scout Sentinels, Krieg Heavy Weapons Squads, Cadian Recon Squads, Cadian Shock Troops, and Taurox transports, this is a mass-infantry gunline running the Designation Force detachment, with just over half of lists adding Siege Regiment's Creeping Barrage to punish distant enemy units with Shaken. The win condition is layering Signal Flares from Scout Sentinels and Sentinels onto priority targets, saturating them with coordinated small-arms and heavy weapons fire while a horde of cheap bodies contests objectives across the board. It punishes infantry-heavy lists through sheer volume of fire and attrition, denying movement with Creeping Barrage while Scions and Engineers apply focused pressure. It struggles against elite low-model-count armies that can methodically delete its key pieces before the numbers game overwhelms them.
585: Built around Commissars directing Bullgryn Squads, Tech-Priest Enginseers keeping vehicles operational, and Hellhounds providing mobile firepower, this list runs the Abhuman Auxiliaries detachment to let Commissars issue Orders directly to Bullgryn — turning what are normally slow brutes into a directed melee threat that can be reliably activated. The plan is to park Bullgryns on mid-table objectives under Commissar command while a heavy gunline of super-heavies and Hellhounds erases threats that try to dislodge them, with the Steel Hammer detachment enabling Titanic and Squadron units to fire into engagement range without penalty. It punishes slower, low-mobility armies that cannot escape the advance of Bullgryns or trade efficiently into a repair loop kept alive by Enginseers. Highly mobile deep-strike threats and alpha-strike lists crack it open by bypassing the gunline and isolating the Bullgryns before Commissar Orders can stabilise the midfield.
586: Built around waves of Daemonettes, Fiends, Beasts of Nurgle, Keepers of Secrets, the Contorted Epitome, the Tormentbringer, and the Masque of Slaanesh, this list weaponises both Legion Of Excess and Warptide to create a perpetual-motion assault engine: Daemonettes advance and still charge, Fell Back units re-engage the same turn, and nothing ever truly disengages. The win condition is layered combat pressure across every zone simultaneously — flooding objectives with expendable Daemonette screens while Fiends and Keepers hunt anything that contests, making it nearly impossible to hold a safe position anywhere on the board. It punishes slow, castle-style armies brutally, as the advance-and-charge loop denies breathing room and lets the list trade efficiently into anything that tries to sit on objectives. The weakness is volume of quality anti-infantry fire before the first charge lands — a list that can thin Daemonettes at range disrupts the screen math and leaves flanks exposed to counterplay.
587: Built around Infractors, Tormentors, Lord Exultants, Flawless Blades, Noise Marines, and Fulgrim delivered in Chaos Rhinos under the Court of the Phoenician detachment, this is a high-volume melee swarm that punishes opponents for letting it touch them — Sensational Performance lets charging units bypass their prior Engagement Range, effectively cycling through targets and maximising fight-phase output across multiple enemy units. The win condition is coordinating a wave of transported infantry — Infractors and Tormentors screening and threatening objectives while Flawless Blades and Lucius crack open priority targets — using mobile anti-armour threats like the Defiler and winged Daemon Prince to pin defensive lines. It punishes static gunlines and fragile elite infantry that lack sufficient screen depth, overwhelming them with sheer fight-phase volume before they can create space. Resilient mid-board brawlers and dedicated melee denial screens crack it open, because if the transports are popped before the charge lands, the Sensational Performance engine never fires.
588: Built around Flawless Blades, Infractors, Lord Exultants, Tormentors, Lucius, Daemon Princes with Wings, Defilers, Chaos Rhinos, and Noise Marines, this is a charge-hungry melee swarm running the Peerless Bladesmen detachment — every charge delivers either Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1 across the attacking unit, and Spectacle of Slaughter stacks Fights First onto Flawless Blades to punish anything that tries to swing back. The engine is mass Rhino delivery: infantry crash out of transports turn one or two, charge into scoring zones, and overwhelm defenders through sheer volume of enhanced melee attacks while Lords Exultant amplify the kill chain. It punishes static, low-model-count armies that can't screen charges, stacking enough bodies and threat vectors that any single defensive bubble gets swarmed from multiple angles simultaneously. It cracks open against fast shooting lists that strip Rhinos before the infantry disembark, stranding slow foot units in the open and defanging the charge-delivery engine entirely.
589: Built around Infractors, Chaos Terminators, Tormentors, Flawless Blades, and Lord Exultants hitting out of Chaos Rhinos, with Noise Marines and Defilers providing fire support, this is a transport-heavy melee brawler running the Elegant Brutes detachment for guaranteed +1 to Terminator charge rolls on arrival. The plan is to dump combat units from Rhinos mid-board, layer Lord Exultants to buff the subsequent brawl, and grind through scoring zones with sheer volume of attacks across multiple charging units per turn. It punishes static gunlines that lack the volume to chew through multiple waves of infantry, since the Rhino delivery system staggers threat timelines and forces opponents to prioritise poorly. It cracks open against elite melee lists or high-mobility armies that can dodge the Rhinos, isolate individual combat units before support arrives, and dismantle the charge engine piecemeal.
590: Built around the Knight Rampager, Knight Tyrant, Chaos Cerastus Knight Lancer, and Chaos Cerastus Knight Atrapos, this is a mobile heavy-armour hammer that floods the board with large, layered threats across multiple threat vectors. The win condition is anti-armour overload — the Lancer and Rampager close range aggressively while the Tyrant and Atrapos apply punishing ranged pressure, making it nearly impossible for an opponent to prioritise correctly across a single turn. Running predominantly in Lords of Dread, the improved Objective Control on Chaos Knight Characters means these monsters contest and hold primary scoring without sacrificing their combat role, punishing slower elite armies that cannot shift them. Where it cracks is against high-volume, high-accuracy anti-tank shooting that can strip individual Knights before the threat web fully develops, leaving the remaining pieces outnumbered on objectives.
591: Built around Paladin Squads, Interceptor Squads, Strike Squads, Brotherhood Terminators, and a Grand Master in Nemesis Dreadknight supported by a Brotherhood Chaplain and Brother-Captain, this is a mobile psychic melee force running Argent Assault with Banishers as a near-universal secondary detachment. The win condition is hammering high-toughness targets with Paladins whose wound rolls are boosted when outclassed by target toughness, while Interceptors flood objectives and Terminators provide additional melee weight, with Psychic Celerity and Sixty-sixth Seal supercharging key units' threat range and durability. It punishes tanky elite armies by turning toughness advantages against them, extracting extra wounds precisely where other melee lists stall out. Horde volume and ranged firepower crack it open — mass bodies dilute the Paladin hammer's efficiency, and the list has limited answers to being outshot before it closes distance.
592: Built around Purifier Squads, Castellan Crowe, Grand Master Nemesis Dreadknights, Strike Squads, and Brotherhood Terminators, this list uses the Warpbane Task Force detachment to project Hallowed Ground across the board — anchoring the deployment zone and extending it through Purifier positioning into No Man's Land. The win condition is controlling mid-board objectives to unlock the detachment's third Hallowed Ground condition while Dreadknights apply mobile anti-armour pressure and infantry flood transports to contest and score at pace. It punishes static gunlines that cede objective control early, as Dreadknight threat range combined with screened Purifier bubbles makes reclaiming mid-board ground brutally expensive. Lists that can alpha-strike the Purifier squads off objectives before Hallowed Ground expands — collapsing the detachment's spatial engine before it locks in — are the clearest way to crack it open.
594: Built around Armiger Warglaives and Armiger Helverins under the Gate Warden Lance, this is a mobile armoured swarm that layers Sustained Hits 1 across its entire model count while ignoring hit modifiers against visible targets — meaning obscuring terrain and penalty stacking simply don't apply. The win condition is grinding attrition through volume: Warglaives pressure mid-board in melee while Helverins pour out consistent ranged anti-armour, with Throne-bonded Outriders pushing Bondsman-buffed Armigers to ignore cover for clean damage lanes into fortified positions. It punishes elite-armour lists that rely on cover or hit-penalty stacking to stay alive, overwhelming them with too many durable chassis to remove efficiently. It cracks open against high-volume mortal wound output or mass indirect fire that bypasses its lack of a hard defensive bubble, leaving Knights stranded on objectives with no answer to attrition they cannot out-tank.
595: Built around Indomitor Kill Teams, Talonstrike Kill Teams, Deathwatch Terminators, Veterans, Incursors, a Gravis Captain, and the Watch Master, this is a mixed-arms infantry swarm that floods the board with Kill Team bodies across every threat band. The win condition is volume — drowning opponents in activations while the detachment's majority-Toughness wounding rule makes mixed-composition Kill Teams functionally harder to efficiently kill, forcing opponents to over-allocate firepower. It punishes horde armies and gunlines that depend on consistent wound rolls, since the Toughness-blending mechanic degrades their math against heterogeneous units. However, elite armies packing high-AP, high-damage weapons that don't care which Toughness bracket they're hitting can slice through Kill Teams efficiently, and a list this dependent on infantry volume bleeds badly to blast-heavy or mortal-wound-spam opponents.
596: Built around Librarians (both on foot and in Terminator armour), Deathwatch Veterans, Indomitor Kill Teams, Deathwatch Terminator Squads, and Sternguard Veterans operating under the Bastion Task Force and Librarius Conclave detachments, this is a heavy gunline that floods the board with elite infantry crammed into transports. The engine is Bastion Task Force's Battleline rule — Intercessors and other Battleline units shoot and perform Actions after Advancing or Falling Back, keeping the scoring machine running while the Librarius Conclave cycles psychic disciplines (Divination's re-rolls for volume shooting, Biomancy for repositioning) to maximize firepower from stationary kill teams and Veterans. It punishes static elite armies that can't threaten the transport bubble, overwhelming them with layered small-arms and special weapons before they close distance. Armies that can strip transports early or apply volume mortal-wound pressure crack it open, since the infantry inside loses both its mobility and its action-economy engine simultaneously.
597: Built around a wall of Tyranids Monsters — Norn Emissary, Norn Assimilator, Screamer-Killers, Carnifexes, Old One Eye, Maleceptor, and the Swarmlord — running Crusher Stampede, which rewards damaged monsters with stacking hit and wound bonuses and inflates their Objective Control at full strength. The plan is to advance a critical mass of high-OC monsters into scoring positions while Biovores and Zoanthropes provide backline pressure, using Neurolictors and the Neurotyrant to set up synapse chains that keep the stampede coordinated and threatening. It punishes elite-model armies that struggle to remove multiple large-wound monsters per turn, because killing enough to strip board control simply outpaces most anti-armour budgets. However, lists built around volume mortal wounds, mass multi-damage shooting, or strong screen-and-deny infantry can stall the advance and pick off monsters before Crusher Stampede's wounded-model bonuses come online.
598: Built around Tyranid Primes with lash whips, Hyperadapted Raveners, The Red Terror, Hormagaunts, and Zoanthropes operating under Subterranean Assault, this is a mobile mid-board brawler that floods the table with fast melee threats emerging from multiple angles. The engine is Tyranid Prime buffing Ravener strike packages into elite combat units while Hormagaunts screen and contest objectives, with Biovores and Hive Guard providing backline pressure that forces opponents to split attention. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot answer simultaneous multi-vector charges across the full board width, trading favorably through sheer threat density and the Swarmlord's reroll support. Blast-heavy shooting armies that clear hordes efficiently and deny board space early can dismantle the screening layer and isolate the strike units before they close.
599: Built around Genestealers, Broodlords, Neurolictors, Lictors, Von Ryan's Leapers, Raveners, and Hyperadapted Raveners, this is a deep-striking swarm that floods the midboard from multiple angles simultaneously. The engine is coordinated threat saturation — Deep Strike-capable assassins and assault units drop into scoring positions while Biovores pin screens with indirect fire and Neurotyrant/Zoanthrope psychic support amplifies the kill chain, forcing opponents to defend everywhere at once. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count armies that cannot screen the entire table, drowning them in redundant charges before they can prioritise targets. The weakness is durability — without layered saves or tough anchor units, concentrated firepower or elite combat armies can delete key pieces before they connect, and a well-placed screen collapses the entire deep-strike timing window.
600: Built around Zodgrod Wortsnagga, Ghazghkull Thraka, multiple Warbosses and Painboys, and dense waves of Boyz and Gretchin, this is a Freebooter Krew horde that floods the board with Orks Infantry. The plan is to designate a loot objective each Command phase and bury it under bodies while the Waaagh! supercharges every shooting unit with Sustained Hits 1, then grind through combat with Painboys keeping the mob alive and Tankbustas threatening armour. It punishes low-model-count lists through sheer attrition — the combination of board coverage and sustained healing makes it nearly impossible to clear objectives fast enough. It cracks under elite armies that can surgically remove Painboys early, collapsing the regeneration engine and leaving the horde vulnerable to being chipped off the loot objective before scoring.
601: Built around massed Boyz squads, multiple Warbosses, Ghazghkull Thraka, Painboys keeping bodies alive, and Big Mek Dakkarigs and Wazdakka Gutsmek rounding out the command structure, this is a War Horde list that blankets the table with green bodies and charges everything into melee, where every Ork model's weapons gain Sustained Hits 1. The win condition is simple attrition: flood objectives with sheer model count, crash Ghazghkull and Warboss-buffed Boyz into whatever is holding them, and generate extra hits in combat until the opponent runs out of ways to clear the board. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't efficiently trade into hordes — if the opposing list needs two or three attacks to kill each Boy, the math rapidly collapses in the Orks' favour. The weakness is high-volume mortal wound output or blast weapons that bypass the Painboy's healing and delete entire squads before they reach combat, cracking the mass-body engine before Sustained Hits 1 ever comes online.
602: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, Wazdakka Gutsmek, nearly two units of Lootas, almost two Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, and a wall of Gretchin screening a core of Boyz, Squighog Boyz, and Painboys, this is a layered horde that hits from every range band simultaneously. The plan is to drown opponents in threat vectors — Lootas and Flash Gitz punish anything that clusters while Ghazghkull, Mozrog Skragbad, and Squighog Boyz crash mid-board to brawl for objectives, with Gretchin and Trukks keeping the engine moving. It punishes gunlines and low-model-count armies that cannot clear the sheer volume of bodies while simultaneously trading into hard targets with Tankbustas and Shokk Attack Guns. It cracks under elite melee pressure or high-mobility alpha strikes that can bypass the Gretchin screen and delete the fragile shooting before it fires.
603: Built around Wazdakka Gutsmek, Ghazghkull Thraka, massed Tankbustas, Flash Gitz, Lootas, and Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, all ferried forward in Trukks and screened by waves of Boyz and Gretchin, this is a mid-table brawler that floods the board with bodies and guns simultaneously. The win condition is layered attrition — Trukks deliver Tankbustas and Boyz into scoring range while Lootas and Flash Gitz pour fire from behind the horde, with Painboys keeping key units alive long enough to grind opponents off objectives. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear the sheer volume of wounds, especially when those armies lack the volume of anti-infantry output to chew through multiple interlocking screens. Armies that can reliably delete Trukks before they unload, or that deploy enough board-wide mortal-wound output to bypass the horde entirely, expose how dependent the list is on getting its cargo into position intact.
604: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, multiple Warbosses, Boyz, Nobz, Stormboyz, and Breaka Boyz hauled forward in Trukks and Battlewagons, this is a War Horde list that puts Sustained Hits 1 on every Ork melee weapon in the army. The plan is to deliver overlapping waves of infantry into combat simultaneously — transports crack the midboard open while Stormboyz and Boss Snikrot's infiltrators pin or delete screens, letting the main blob swarm objectives and grind opponents into paste through sheer volume of Sustained attacks. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb the volume of melee dice, especially when Ghazghkull and Follow Me Ladz keep key units punching above their weight. Armies that can alpha strike the transports before they unload, or that have durable shooting to attrit the hordes at range, can strip the engine before it gets into contact.
605: Built around Meganobz, Nobz, multiple Warbosses, Warboss in Mega Armour, Ghazghkull, and Boyz delivered in Trukks, with Gretchin and Painboyz layering screens and feel-no-pain support across the board. The engine is Sustained Hits 1 on every Meganobz and Nobz melee attack, letting Warboss buffs stack into a kill chain that dismantles elite infantry and mid-table brawls through sheer volume of hits. This build punishes lists that rely on durable multi-wound infantry blocks, as Sustained Hits dramatically overloads saves before any opponent can trade efficiently. It cracks open against high-volume shooting that removes Trukks before the melee wave lands, stranding expensive Meganobz in the open.
607: Built around Magnus the Red, Scarab Occult Terminators led by a Sorcerer in Terminator Armour, Sekhetar Robots, Tzaangor Enlightened with fatecaster greatbows, Rubric Marines, Tzaangors, a Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings, and Sorcerer support, this Grand Coven list floods the board with layered psychic firepower and a genuine horde of bodies. The plan is to cycle Grand Coven's command abilities — extending Psychic weapon ranges and amplifying output turn by turn — while Magnus and the Daemon Prince threaten elite targets and a mass of Tzaangors and Rubrics contest primaries. It punishes armies that rely on mid-table infantry holds, drowning them in overlapping psychic attacks across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. Dedicated melee alpha-strike lists that can isolate and collapse Magnus early expose the build's dependency on its centrepiece staying alive.
609: Built around Contemptor-Achillus and Contemptor-Galatus Dreadnoughts, Telemons, Custodian Guard, and Allarus Custodians, this list floods the board with elite WALKER units that gain +2" Movement and +1 to advance and charge rolls from the Might of the Moritoi detachment, backed by Shield Host's rotating Ka'tah buffs that can spike Critical Hits on 5+ or sharpen Armour Penetration across the entire melee line. The plan is to crash enhanced Dreadnoughts into midfield early, leverage their boosted threat range to contest objectives and delete priority targets before the opponent can position away, while Guard and Allarus hold flanks and screen the scoring core. It punishes slower, static armies that cannot disengage — anything playing a castle or brickwall defence gets engulfed by a wall of elite, rapidly-closing walkers simultaneously threatening from multiple angles. It cracks when faced with heavy ranged alpha-strike pressure that can cripple Dreadnoughts before they close, since the whole threat engine depends on surviving the approach.
610: Built around Witchseekers, Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, Prosecutors, Blade Champions, and Allarus Custodians operating under the Talons of the Emperor detachment, this is a mixed-arms force that blends elite melee infantry with Anathema Psykana units whose Null Aegis aura projects Feel No Pain 5+ against psychic attacks and mortal wounds across nearby Custodes. The plan is to use mobile, layered threats across the board — Allarus dropping into flanks, Blade Champions hunting characters, and Prosecutors pressuring mid-table — while Custodian Guard and Wardens lock down objectives with exceptional durability. It punishes lists that rely on mortal wound spam or psychic damage to strip elite infantry, as the Null Aegis interaction makes those tools largely irrelevant. However, concentrated high-volume conventional shooting from gunline armies can exploit the relatively small model count and strip units before the aura network is established.
611: Built around Khorne Berzerkers, Jakhals, Eightbound, Exalted Eightbound, Slaughterbound, Khârn the Betrayer, Chaos Spawn, and Angron, this is a mass-assault engine that weaponizes the Berzerker Warband's charge bonus — every charging World Eaters unit gains +1 Attack and +2 Strength on melee weapons — to turn an already hard-hitting horde into a wall of supercharged violence. The plan is simple: deliver multiple threats simultaneously via Rhino transports, screen denials through expendable Jakhals and Spawn, and overwhelm mid-board objectives through sheer combat volume before the opponent stabilizes. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb repeated charge waves across multiple threat vectors, and the layered lethality of independent kill-pieces like Angron and Slaughterbound means no single counter-unit solves the problem. Shooting-heavy gunlines that kill units before they reach combat — particularly those with anti-horde volume fire — blunt the engine hard, since a charge bonus you never get to use is no bonus at all.
612: Built around Exalted Eightbound, Eightbound, Slaughterbound, Daemon Princes of Khorne, and Jakhals screened across the board, this Possessed Slaughterband list is a mobile melee toolbox that floods mid-table with durable, threat-dense Possessed units. The engine is Brazen Fury — every time shooting kills a Possessed model, that unit surges D6" forward, converting the opponent's shooting phase into an unintended charge setup while Vessels of Wrath sharpens Character melee to crack armour. It punishes gunline armies hardest, as heavy shooting triggers relentless surge moves that collapse the distance needed to deliver devastating combat threats across multiple units simultaneously. It cracks open against fast alpha-strike lists or elite melee that can kill entire Possessed units outright before Brazen Fury ever triggers, nullifying the reactive surge mechanic entirely.
614: Built around a dense core of Crisis Starscythe, Fireknife, and Sunforge battlesuits led by Commander Farsight, multiple Coldstar and Enforcer Commanders, Stealth Battlesuits for screening, Pathfinders for markerlight support, and The Twin Lance as a hammer unit, this is an all-battlesuit mid-table brawler running the Retaliation Cadre. The win condition is closing distance fast — every battlesuit attack within 12" gains +1 Strength, and within 8" gains +1 AP, so the list pushes aggressively onto objectives to trigger those bonuses and delete key targets before the opponent can respond. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies brutally, stacking improved AP and Strength into high-value targets while Coldstars with Starflare Ignition System reposition to keep the pressure constant and deny safe angles. Armies that can screen the midfield effectively and force engagements beyond 12" neuter the core damage bonus, and anything with strong melee that can absorb the first volley and crash into the suits will crack this list open before it recycles.
615: Built around Berehk Stornbröw, Einhyr Hearthguard, Kâhls, Cthonian Beserks, and a mechanised backbone of Hekatons, Sagitaurs, and Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, this list plays a dense mid-board brawler game backed by serious firepower. The Hearthguard Covenant's wound-reroll-of-1 aura rewards staying within 9" of targets, so the plan is to close distance fast using transports and Beserks, then lock enemies in a kill-box where the Hearthguard and Thunderkyn grind them apart while YP accumulates to fuel secondary abilities. It punishes elite-infantry armies that can't clear multiple durable threats simultaneously, as the combination of resilient melee hammers and massed mid-range shooting creates overlapping pressure no single threat-removal axis can answer. Swarm armies or anything with consistent long-range output that forces this list to advance into fire rather than dictating engagement range can erode it before the close-quarters engine comes fully online.
616: Built around Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Einhyr Hearthguard, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and Cthonian Beserks, supported by a deep bench of Kâhls, Hernkyn Pioneers, Sagitaurs, and Kapricus Carriers, this is a mid-table brawler with serious long-range teeth. The plan is to park heavy firepower on midfield objectives while Beserks and Hearthguard close for melee, using Hearthband's wound re-roll and AP bonus on closest-target attacks to grind through durable units efficiently. It punishes slow, high-toughness armies that can't avoid becoming the closest eligible target — the conditional AP improvement and wound re-rolls compound viciously against elite infantry and heavy armour. Fast, mobile lists that can dictate engagement range and attack from multiple angles strain the targeting requirements that activate the key AP bonuses, leaving the gunline exposed.
617: Built around Hernkyn Pioneers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Kapricus Carriers, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Einhyr Hearthguard, and Hekaton Land Fortresses, this is a mobile mid-board brawler running the Farseekers detachment, where every Hernkyn unit hits on 2s within 12" and the whole army closes to point-blank range to exploit it. The plan is to flood the midfield with fast Pioneers and transported infantry, generate YP through kills via Needgaârd Oathband, and use that currency to flip into Hostile Acquisition objectives while Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses provide a heavy fire base that punishes anything that tries to push back. It punishes slow, durable gunlines that cannot prevent the Hernkyn swarm from reaching close range, where the hit-roll bonus turns already-solid shooting into a removal engine. Armies that can alpha-strike the transport column before it disembarks, or elite melee threats that can kill Pioneers before they generate YP, crack this build open by denying the close-range engagement it depends on.
618: Built around Sagitaurs (Scouts 6" via Armoured Trailblazers), Cthonian Beserks, Hearthkyn Warriors, Hernkyn Pioneers, Berehk Stornbröw, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Kapricus Carriers, Memnyr Strategists, and Ûthar the Destined, this is a transport-infantry hammer that floods the midboard turn one with infantry-packed skimmers. The plan is to crash Sagitaurs forward, disgorge Beserks and Warriors into contested objectives while Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses pour heavy fire downfield, strangling the opponent's scoring engine through sheer midboard presence and layered threat saturation. It punishes slower gunline armies that can't handle simultaneous pressure from multiple transported threats and mobile anti-armour reaching their key pieces early. Highly mobile, elite melee lists that can strip transports before the infantry deploy, or armies with strong deep-strike denial that collapse the Beserks' insertion angles, crack it open hardest.
619: Built around Hekaton Land Fortresses, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Einhyr Hearthguard, and Hernkyn Pioneers, this is a mid-board brawling gunline running the Mercenary Oathband detachment, which opens the game with Hostile Acquisition active on all units before offering the option to switch to Fortify Takeover mid-battle by spending 3 Judgment Points. The plan is to flood the midfield with durable transports and heavy fire platforms, banking Judgment Points from early aggression and then flexing between offensive and defensive ability states to control scoring windows. It punishes slower elite armies that cannot clear entrenched infantry efficiently, as layered bodies in Kapricus Carriers and Sagitaurs force opponents into unfavorable trades against tough mid-table units. High model density and transport dependency mean concentrated anti-transport shooting or fast alpha-strike lists can collapse its staging before the YP engine gets going.
620: Built around Hernkyn Pioneers, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Kapricus Carriers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Memnyr Strategists, Ûthar the Destined, Hearthkyn Warriors, Einhyr Hearthguard, Sagitaurs, and Kâhls, this Farseekers list fields a mass of mobile infantry and heavy firepower across a sprawling midboard gunline. The engine is the Farseekers detachment's +1 to hit within 12", rewarding aggressive positioning to bring everything into close-range kill zones while the Needgaârd Oathband's kill-banking generates YP to fuel further abilities. It punishes slow, durable armies that try to absorb fire at range, overwhelming them with stacked accuracy once the Votann wall advances to its preferred engagement band. Armies that can deny or contest that 12" sweet spot with alpha strikes, deep strike threats, or fast melee harassment force awkward repositioning that unravels the entire shooting economy.
621: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Kâhl, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, this Hearthband list floods the midfield with heavily armoured bodies backed by a sustained firebase of vehicle-mounted and infantry heavy weapons. The win condition is forcing the opponent to engage on two fronts simultaneously: Hearthguard and Kâhl push into close combat threatening AP improvement on every melee attack against the nearest target, while Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses punish anything that tries to back off and shoot. It excels against elite low-volume armies that cannot clear wounds fast enough to stop the Hearthguard tide before the guns delete their key pieces. It struggles against high-mobility or deep-strike-heavy lists that can sidestep the closest-target wound reroll trigger, isolate the firebase, and pick apart the slower Votann elements before they converge.
626: Built around Plague Marines (infiltrating up to two squads via the Flyblown Host detachment), Poxwalkers in bulk, Malignant Plaguecasters, Biologus Putrifier, Deathshroud Terminators, Typhus, and a Tallyman support core, this is a layered mid-board brawler that floods objectives with disgustingly durable bodies. The win condition is attrition: Infiltrating Plague Marines contest primary from turn one while Poxwalkers — reinforced by the Shamblerot Vectorium's freerolling Strategic Reserve injections — drown the mid-table and deny clean scoring lanes. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear multiple waves of durable infantry and can't efficiently trade into T5 or better footsloggers. However, it cracks against mass low-AP volume shooting and fast board-wide pressure that bypasses the slow advance and collapses its threat bubbles before the attrition engine can grind.
627: Built around Mortarion, a Daemon Prince of Nurgle, Deathshroud Terminators, Lords of Contagion, Defilers, and waves of Poxwalkers screened by Chaos Spawn, this list runs Virulent Vectorium to transform every objective it touches into a plague zone — once secured at the end of your Command phase, any enemy unit contesting that objective becomes Afflicted for as long as you hold it. The win condition is layered attrition: park durable, near-unkillable bodies on objectives, force opponents to fight through Afflicted debuffs while Mortarion and the Deathshroud apply elite melee pressure, and let the Tallyman's support keep the engine grinding. It punishes mid-range brawling armies that need to physically contest objectives, since trading into Afflicted units in your plague zones is a slow, grinding death. Shooting-heavy gunlines that can clear your screens at range before Mortarion arrives, or alpha-strike lists that deny you the Command phase trigger entirely, are the hardest matchups to navigate.
628: Built around Plague Marines in Rhinos, Poxwalker hordes, Deathshroud Terminators, Malignant Plaguecasters, Biologus Putrifier, Lord of Contagion, Tallyman, and Typhus, this is a Contagion-stacking attrition engine running Champions of Contagion — with four-fifths of lists adding Paragons of Putrescence to push Character Contagion Range to 12". The win condition is layering plague debuffs across the midboard while Plague Marines and Deathshroud grind through anything that contests objectives, with the Plague switcher letting you tune your active Plague round-by-round to match whatever threatens the scoring plan. It punishes durable elite infantry lists that expect to trade efficiently, since the Contagion aura pressure and mass lethal output make every engagement costly for anything that lingers in range. However, fast armies that can threaten Characters early or deny the midboard foothold before Contagion spreads will crack it open — the whole engine stalls if the debuff bubble never gets established.
629: Built around Lords of Contagion, Deathshroud and Blightlord Terminators, Typhus, a Lord of Virulence, and screening masses of Chaos Spawn and Poxwalkers, this is a Contagion-bubble attrition list running Death Lord's Chosen alongside Paragons of Putrescence to push Characters' Contagion Range out to 12" and trigger mortal wound rolls against every Afflicted unit in the opponent's Command phase. The win condition is grinding: stack Afflicted conditions across the enemy army, then collect D3 mortal wounds per unit every Command phase while durable Terminators and expendable screens contest objectives. It punishes horde-heavy and mid-toughness armies brutally, as multiple Afflicted triggers compound fast against large unit counts. It cracks under pressure from mobile, hard-hitting lists that can isolate and delete Characters before the Contagion bubble is established, cutting off the mortal wound engine entirely.
630: Built around Mortarion, multiple Daemon Princes of Nurgle, Deathshroud Terminators, Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Foetid Bloat-Drones, and Poxwalker chaff backed by Typhus and a Lord of Contagion, this is a Virulent Vectorium list that floods objectives with durable bodies. The win condition is locking down multiple objectives simultaneously so the detachment's Afflicted mechanic degrades every enemy unit nearby while the Blight-Haulers and Drones generate relentless mobile anti-armour pressure across the board. Against low-durability elite armies that struggle to clear layers of Poxwalkers and Terminators simultaneously, this list punishes overextension brutally. However, high-volume mortal wound output or shooting lists that can efficiently pick apart the character cluster before Revolting Regeneration and Tallyman support come online will crack this list apart.
632: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, and a dense mass of Sicarian Ruststalkers, Sicarian Infiltrators, Ironstrider Ballistarii, and Skitarii Rangers, this list floods the table with layered infantry supported by fast mobile elements. The win condition is attrition through volume — Sicarians brawl into the midtable to grind opposing units off objectives while Ironstriders and Pteraxii Skystalkers apply mobile anti-armour pressure and Rangers screen to deny deep strikes and hold backfield secondaries. It punishes horde and mid-density infantry armies hard, stacking lethal close-range volleys across multiple waves of cheap bodies that are difficult to remove efficiently. It cracks under pressure from elite alpha-strike lists that can delete the Sicarian packages before they engage, as the army lacks the durability to absorb heavy focused damage without losing its melee engine entirely.
633: Built around Achilles Ridgerunners, Purestrain Genestealers, Neophyte Hybrids, Hyperadapted Raveners, Patriarch, Deathleaper, Benefictus, Acolyte Hybrids, Lictors, Atalan Jackals, and Reductus Saboteurs, this Final Day list blends native Genestealer Cult horde bodies with a massive Tyranid Vanguard Invader allotment — nearly every slot available at Strike Force. The plan is to flood every lane simultaneously, using mid-table brawlers like Raveners and Purestrains to threaten fights while Ridgerunners and Jackals apply mobile pressure and contest secondaries from range. Neophyte Hybrids healing inside terrain and Purestrain cycling via strategic reserves through Purestrain Broodswarm give the list exceptional attrition depth, punishing armies that can't sustain kill output across multiple turns. The sheer unit diversity and mixed keyword pool means it frays badly against hard alpha strikes and elite shooting that can delete key pieces before the layered threat web locks in.
634: Built around Atalan Jackals, Achilles Ridgerunners, Goliath Rockgrinders, Purestrain Genestealers, and waves of Acolyte Hybrids, this is a Outlander Claw list that floods the board with fast vehicles and expendable bodies simultaneously. The engine is objective lock: Jackals sticky-cap markers under the Outlander Claw rule while Rockgrinders and Ridgerunners push OC across the midfield, and Acolyte Hybrids with hand flamers plus Purestrains deliver close-range punishment to anything that tries to contest. It punishes slower, static gunlines that can't clear multiple threat vectors at once — the sheer volume of mounted units with boosted OC and horde bodies arriving from every angle overwhelms lists built to answer one or two kill priorities. However, high-volume mortal wound output, blast weapons, and elite melee that can trade efficiently into the swarm crack this list open, since losing key Jackal units early collapses the sticky-cap foundation.
635: Built around Land Speeder Vengances, Land Speeders, and Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes as the mobile fire platform core, backed by Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, Lion El'Jonson, and Azrael providing a durable melee anvil — all operating under Darkflight Pursuit, whose blanket Ignores Cover on every RAVENWING FLY unit's shooting strips the most common defensive buffer in the game. The plan is to use the speeder swarm to erase dug-in targets turn one while the Deathwing melee package forces the opponent to commit or cede midboard, converting skimmer pressure into primary point denial. It punishes cover-dependent gunlines and defensive objective holders hardest, since Ignores Cover turns heavy terrain into a non-factor and the Knights' layered lethality overwhelms anything that tries to trade in melee. Massed mortal-wound output, high-damage anti-vehicle shooting, or alpha-strike deep strike threats that bypass the speeder screen and hit the relatively fragile backline can crack it before the melee anvil stabilises.
636: Built around Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and a swarm of Land Speeders and Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, this list splits roughly evenly across Wrath of the Rock, Darkflight Pursuit, and Dark Age Arsenal depending on the pilot's preference. The plan is to flood mid-board with fast skimmers doing mobile anti-armour work while Azrael's leadership keeps elite melee threats — Deathwing Knights and Inner Circle Companions — pushing into objectives backed by the Lion's combat power. It punishes infantry-heavy and medium-armour lists through layered shooting and lethal close-range combat that few screens can absorb simultaneously. Armies that can alpha-strike the speeder swarm before it repositions, or that bring enough high-Strength volume to overwhelm even the wound-roll reduction from Wrath of the Rock, will crack the list open before the melee engine closes the gap.
637: Built around a swarm of Land Speeder Vengeances, Land Speeders, and a Storm Speeder Thunderstrike — all supported by Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Deathwing Knights, Scout Squads, and a Lieutenant with combi-weapon — this is a fast-moving, skimmer-heavy Dark Angels force with serious anti-armour punch. The plan is to use early board presence and mobile firepower to delete high-value targets while Scouts and Deathwing Knights contest objectives and generate OC where it matters. It punishes slow, armoured gunlines that can't respond to multi-angle skimmer threats, overloading anti-tank resources across a wide, mobile threat envelope. The weakness is staying power: without a defining detachment rule to lean on, it's fragile against fast aggressive armies that can crack the light-hulled speeders before they fire and deny the layered threat from ever materialising.
638: Built around Chaplains on Bike, Outrider Squads, Ravenwing Black Knights, and Ravenwing Command Squads, this is a fast, harassment-focused Dark Angels force running Interrogation Conclave with half the field also adding Lion's Blade Task Force's Fall Back punishment as a second detachment. The engine is Chaplain-driven battle-shock: Chaplains suppress enemy Leadership with Sower of Dread, then trigger mass battle-shock rolls on nearby units whenever they destroy something, softening the enemy midboard so Ravenwing cavalry can dictate engagement terms and farm secondary points from disrupted, penalised opponents. It punishes combat-dependent armies hardest — units fighting near a Chaplain that are already battle-shocked take compounding penalties when trying to escape Ravenwing Engagement Range. Durable, high-save shooting lists that ignore battle-shock and never need to Fall Back can simply weather the harassment and outgun the relatively fragile biker core.
639: Built around Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Hellblasters, and Deathwing Knights, with Inceptors, Ravenwing Black Knights, Scouts, and Intercessors filling out the roster under the Dark Age Arsenal detachment, which pumps all plasma weapon Strength by one across the board. The plan is to park Azrael's leadership bubble over Hellblasters and fire supercharged plasma at boosted Strength into anything with a meaningful save, while Inceptors and Ravenwing Black Knights generate mobile pressure and the Knights and Lion anchor close-range threat. It punishes MEQ and TEQ lists hard, as the Strength-buffed plasma overloads saves that would otherwise absorb shooting comfortably. Swarm lists and armies that can contest multiple flanks simultaneously expose the build's relatively low model count and a below-50% win rate suggests it struggles to close out games against faster, board-spreading opposition.
640: Built around Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and a deep bench of Librarians running the Librarius Conclave, this is a psychically-amplified elite melee-and-gunline hybrid that leans heavily on Terminator-armoured infantry moving in coordinated waves. The win condition is controlling the Vowed objective mechanic — toggling between Defensive Footing to lock down held ground and Aggressive Push to score on contested markers — while the Conclave's rotating Disciplines (Biomancy for repositioning, Divination for reliable damage output) keep each unit punching above its weight. It punishes armies that rely on volume-of-fire to chip elite infantry, since 2+ saves and layered Lethal Hits make attrition inefficient against it. Mortal wounds, high-AP anti-tank spam, and alpha-strike pressure crack it open by bypassing saves before the Vowed objective engine can fire.
641: Built around Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, Librarians in Terminator Armour, Azrael, and Lion El'Jonson, this is a heavily armoured elite infantry list running primarily under the Librarius Conclave detachment, cycling Psychic Disciplines each battle round to flex between mobility, accuracy, and firepower as the situation demands. The win condition is delivering elite melee threats — particularly the Deathwing Knights and Companions — into contact while Azrael and the Librarians stack buffs, using Intercessors and Scouts to hold ground and bleed opponent actions. It punishes lower-model-count elite armies that cannot absorb sustained pressure from multiple hard-hitting terminator-class units all benefiting from round-by-round discipline selection. Where it struggles is against fast, high-volume shooting that strips its expensive units before they engage, since losing even one or two core pieces collapses the threat density the whole engine depends on.
642:
Built around multiple squads of Deathwing Knights, Chaplains in Terminator armour, Lion El'Jonson, Azrael, an Ancient in Terminator armour, and Deathwing Terminator squads, this is a dense, elite Terminator brick army with no single detachment identity.

The plan is to crash heavily armoured, character-buffed Terminator units into the midfield, using Chaplain auras and Lion El'Jonson to amplify melee output while the Ancient's presence keeps the bricks fighting through casualties, grinding opponents off objectives through attrition rather than speed.

It punishes armies that rely on low-Strength, high-volume shooting, where its exceptional durability in armour simply absorbs the damage and keeps scoring.

What cracks it open is elite anti-armour overload — high-Strength, low-AP shooting that bypasses the toughness wall, combined with fast objective play that outmanoeuvres the relatively slow Terminator footprint before it can close.
643: Built around Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Lemartes, Sanguinary Guard, Bladeguard Veterans, and a dense support stack of Chaplains, Sanguinary Priests, and jump-pack Captains running Rage-Cursed Onslaught, this is a multi-wave melee army that floods the midboard with elite bodies from turn one. The win condition is charging everything simultaneously — Rage-Cursed Onslaught's +1 Attack on the charge (or +2 if Battle-shocked) turns already-dangerous units into kill-chain blenders, with Lemartes and Chaplains stacking fight buffs to ensure lethal output across multiple combats. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb simultaneous charges from several independent threats, and the mobile toolbox structure lets it flex scoring units into objectives while combat units create pressure. It cracks against armies that can screen out charges reliably or suppress its multi-unit assault timing, since the whole engine collapses when charges are denied or staggered apart.
644: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Lemartes, and Captain with Jump Pack under Legacy of Grace, this is an all-infantry jump pack swarm that floods the board with fast, hard-hitting melee threats. The win condition is overwhelming mid-board presence — Legacy of Grace's +1 to advance and charge rolls on CHARACTER units keeps the engine moving, with Lemartes driving Death Company into combat early while Sanguinary Guard clean up whatever survives. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count armies that can't absorb multiple concurrent melee threats across several objectives simultaneously. Where it cracks is against armies with strong overwatch, reliable screening, or high volumes of mortal-wound output that strip the jump pack units before they can land their charges.
645: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Bladeguard Veterans, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, and Sanguinary Priests providing support, this is a Liberator Assault Group list that floods the board with melee threats across multiple threat vectors — infantry on foot, jump infantry, and elite shock troops all demanding answers simultaneously. The win condition is the Liberator Assault Group's charge bonus: every charging Adeptus Astartes unit gains +2 Strength and +1 Attack on melee weapons, turning mid-tier bodies into blenders and elite units into catastrophic threats, with Lemartes pushing Death Company into overdrive and Chaplains stacking further pressure. It punishes low-model, low-armour lists that cannot absorb repeated multi-unit charges from multiple angles, quickly collapsing screening layers and taking the fight to objectives through raw combat volume. However, it struggles against gunlines with long-range anti-infantry saturation or deep-strike denial tools that prevent clean charges, since the entire damage engine requires actually connecting — forced overwatch, terrain choke, or charge-disruption mechanics peel away its teeth before the fight phase triggers.
647: Built around cultist mobs, traitor guardsmen, chaos bikers, defilers, chaos rhinos, and chaos predator destructors, this Pactbound Zealots list buries opponents under a tide of cheap bodies while sustaining meaningful firepower from its heavier platforms. The engine is a layered one: expendable infantry flood objectives and absorb attrition while bikers apply mobile mid-table pressure and predator destructors deliver sustained anti-armour shooting, all sharpened by Lethal Hits on melee attacks triggering on unmodified 5s. It punishes gunlines and low-model-count elite armies that struggle to clear multiple waves of screening chaff before the armoured elements grind them down. However, high-volume mortal wound output or blast weapons that efficiently kill horde units can collapse the screening layer and expose the mechanised core before it can dictate engagement range.
648: Built around Defilers, Chosen, Cultist Mobs, Chaos Bikers, Abaddon, Huron Blackheart, Masters of the Maelstrom, and Red Corsairs Raiders, this Pactbound Zealots list fuses a mobile gunline with a hard-hitting melee core, all unlocking Lethal Hits on unmodified 5+ melee hit rolls across the army. The plan is to flood mid-table with screening cultists and bikers while Defilers and Red Corsairs grind out ranged damage, then Abaddon and Chosen crash in with Lethal Hits-amplified melee to close out objectives and characters. It punishes elite low-model-count armies through anti-armour overload and attrition-resistant horde screening that forces opponents into unfavorable trades. High investment in melee threat means a disciplined gunline or alpha-strike list that can strip Defilers early and keep Chosen off objectives will dismantle the engine before it engages.
649: Built around Masters of the Maelstrom, Chosen, Defilers, Huron Blackheart, Cultist Mobs, Chaos Rhinos, Red Corsairs Raiders, and Vashtorr the Arkifane, this is a mid-board brawling horde that floods the table with bodies across multiple threat vectors. The plan is to drown opponents in overlapping pressure — cultists and Raiders hold and contest objectives while Chosen and Defilers grind through whatever is sitting on them, with Huron enabling strategic redeploys to tilt the board mid-game. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that lack the volume to answer simultaneous threats across multiple zones, especially when a focused re-roll target from Veterans of the Long War or AP improvement on objectives from Renegade Raiders lets the guns punch through armour that would otherwise hold. Armies with reliable board-wide blast damage or fast deep-striking units that bypass the screen and land directly on the scoring pieces can unravel the layering before the horde stabilises.
650: Built around Possessed, Cultist Mob, Chosen, Defilers, and often Abaddon, this is a Pactbound Zealots list that converts every unmodified Hit roll of 5+ into a Critical Hit across its melee units, generating a sustained engine of lethal wounds at close quarters. The plan is to flood the midboard with durable, hard-hitting bodies — Possessed and Chosen pressing into objectives while Cultists screen and soak — backed by Defilers providing mobile anti-armour punch to crack whatever sits in the way. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot efficiently trade into multiple waves of Lethal Hits melee pressure across a wide front. However, it struggles against shooting-heavy gunlines that can strip Possessed and Chosen before they reach combat, leaving the Cultist screens holding objectives without the kill power to back them up.
651: Built around Possessed, Mutilators, Chosen, Legionaries, and Cultist Mobs all buffed by Fabius Bile's augmentation system, this is a mass-infantry brawler that floods the board with enhanced Heretic Astartes Infantry, selecting or rolling for augmentations at the battle's start to stack on raw combat power. The win condition is attrition-through-volume: Cultists screen and hold ground while Possessed and Mutilators crash into midfield, with Kravek Morne and Chosen providing layered melee threat that forces opponents to trade unfavorably across multiple fronts simultaneously. It punishes elite low-model-count lists that struggle to clear a relentless tide of augmented infantry, particularly when Rhino-mounted Chosen or Legionaries threaten backfield objectives and force overextension. It cracks apart when faced with high-volume mortal wound output or blast weapons that gut hordes before they engage, and its largely foot-slogging mass can be kited by faster, shooty armies that deny the close-range brawl entirely.
652: Built around Cultist Mob screens, Defilers, Venomcrawlers, Chaos Bikers, Chosen, Vashtorr the Arkifane, and Abaddon the Despoiler, this Pactbound Zealots list layers daemon engines into a grinding melee and armour-cracking machine where every model swings with Lethal Hits on unmodified 5s in melee. The plan is to use Cultists and Bikers to contest and screen midfield while Defilers and Venomcrawlers punch holes in armoured targets and Abaddon or Chosen close the deal in combat. It punishes lists that rely on high-toughness vehicles or elite infantry clumped in the open, where the combination of sustained daemon engine shooting and Lethal Hit melee overwhelms damage thresholds fast. It cracks when faced with long-range alpha strike armies that can strip the Defilers and Venomcrawlers before they reach engagement range, leaving the infantry core without its heavy support.
653: Built around Warpsmiths, Defilers, Venomcrawlers, Chaos Bikers, Forgefiends, and Vashtorr himself operating under the Soulforged Warpack detachment, this list is a wall of Heretic Astartes Daemon Vehicles backed by cheap Cultist screens and fast Biker threats. The engine is the Dark Pact invoke mechanic — triggering contracted Daemon Vehicles to gain +1 to Wound on ranged attacks and +2 Attacks in melee simultaneously, letting Defilers and Venomcrawlers crack armour and brawl mid-table in the same activation. It punishes vehicle-heavy lists that can't handle anti-armour overload from multiple angles at once, especially when Bikers threaten flanks and contest primaries while the daemon engines do murder. Highly mobile elite infantry and screens that can tarpit the daemon engines in combat before the pact fires are the clearest crack — if the Warpsmiths can't keep vehicles alive to invoke, the whole kill chain falls apart.
654: Built around Drazhar, Lelith Hesperax, and massed Incubi and Wyches ferried in Venoms and Raiders, with Scourges providing both heavy-weapon fire support and shardcarbine harassment across every list. The kill chain runs through Skysplinter Assault's disembark trigger — units piling out of transports gain Lance on melee and Ignores Cover on ranged, while Exhibition of Slaughter stacks Lethal Hits on every Wych Cult melee swing against non-vehicles, turning each combat phase into a cascading wound avalanche. This punishes mid-density infantry armies brutally, where layered Lethal Hits and Lance combine to delete elite infantry before they can answer back.
