However, anything that collapses the transport layer early — high-volume anti-skimmer shooting or deep strike denial forcing Venoms to stall — cuts off the disembark engine and leaves the melee core stranded without its activation buffs.
655: Built around Warlock Conclaves, Eldrad Ulthran, War Walkers, Farseers, Storm Guardians, Warlocks, and Rangers under the Armoured Warhost detachment, this list weaponises the [ASSAULT] rule on Aeldari Vehicles to fire War Walkers after advancing, maintaining constant pressure while a dense psyker support network buffs and protects the core battleline. The win condition is layered attrition — the psyker stack stacks lethal output turn over turn while Storm Guardians and Rangers hold objectives cheaply, letting the War Walkers delete priority targets without sacrificing mobility. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count elite armies that struggle to answer multiple fast-moving, hard-to-shift vehicle threats across a wide frontage. Armies that can flood the board with cheap bodies to screen War Walkers out of effective range, or that bring high-volume anti-vehicle firepower to strip the mobile core early, can dismantle its scoring engine before the attrition advantage kicks in.
656: Built around Prince Yriel, Lhykhis, Kharseth, and waves of Corsair Voidreavers, Skyreavers, Shroud Runners, Warp Spiders, Rangers, Starfangs, and Howling Banshees, this Corsair Coterie list plays a fast, layered skimmer-heavy swarm across the whole board. The win condition is objective denial through attrition: the Corsair Coterie ability punishes every enemy move onto your-controlled markers with mortal wounds on a 2+, while Void Thieves steadily convert board presence into stolen secondary points, and Shroud Runners and Rangers extend detection range to strip concealment before the shooting wave lands. It punishes slower, medium-durability armies that must physically contest objectives — the combination of mass bodies, mobile anti-armour, and layered lethal fire makes trading into this list expensive. However, elite armies that can alpha strike the fragile Corsair infantry blobs before they establish objective control, or gunlines that outrange the skimmers entirely, can collapse the engine before the mortal-wound trap ever triggers.
658: Built around the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, the C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, and Ophydian Destroyers, this list uses the Pantheon of Woe detachment to wrap its Monster units in a 6" aura that degrades enemy armour saves by 1 AP on every incoming attack — then walks those same monsters directly into the enemy's face. The win condition is controlled aggression: parking multiple C'tan in the midfield forces opponents to either fight into the AP-degrading aura or cede board presence, while Ophydian Destroyers deep strike to assassinate exposed characters and hold flanking objectives. It punishes elite low-model-count armies hardest, because the aura shreds high-save infantry and the C'tan themselves are individually hard to remove. It cracks open against high-volume cheap shooting that ignores AP thresholds and can chip the C'tan to death before the aura payoff materialises.
659:
Built around the Void Dragon, Nightbringer, Deceiver, one or more Transcendent C'tan, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers, this list fields an overwhelming mass of individually powerful god-monsters and deep-striking melee threats with no single anchor that defines its identity across all lists.

The win condition is elite-unit removal and objective denial by simultaneous pressure — multiple C'tan hit different table quadrants while Flayed Ones and Ophydian Destroyers deep strike directly onto contested objectives, forcing opponents to split answers they rarely have in sufficient volume.

It punishes lists that rely on a single elite damage dealer or centralized screen, since the sheer number of independent C'tan threats guarantees at least two or three engagements the opponent simply cannot adequately answer in the same turn.

Its critical vulnerability is high-volume, point-efficient anti-tank firepower spread across the army: losing one C'tan is survivable, but concentrated shooting that degrades two or three simultaneously collapses the pressure engine before the melee threats can close distance.
661: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Cadian Shock Troops, Kasrkin, Krieg Combat Engineers, and Rogal Dorn Commanders, all ferried and supported by Tauroxes, with Gaunt's Ghosts providing elite infiltration muscle — this is a deep-order, mass-infantry gunline running Grizzled Company, which boosts Officer Order capacity and grants re-rolls of 1 to hit on all affected units. The plan is to stack multiple Orders across a wide infantry line, activate the re-roll engine on as many squads as possible simultaneously, and grind the opponent off objectives through sheer volume of accurate, mobile anti-armour and skimmer fire. It punishes armies that rely on durable mid-table units — the combination of Taurox mobility, Scion deep strikes, and Rogal Dorn firepower creates overlapping kill lanes that few medium-durability targets survive. It cracks under pressure from elite alpha-strike lists that can surgically remove Officers before Orders resolve, collapsing the re-roll engine and leaving a fragile horde with no damage amplification.
662: Built around Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Tempestus Scions, Kasrkin, Krieg Combat Engineers, Scout Sentinels, and Gaunt's Ghosts, this is a deep-striking hot-drop gunline that floods the board with elite infantry and specialist killers. The core engine is the Bridgehead Strike detachment rule: units that arrive from reserve shoot with +1 to hit, turning every drop into a concentrated burst of accurate firepower while Scions' Battleline status and boosted OC let them contest objectives immediately on arrival. It punishes slow, static armies — particularly heavy vehicle lists — by concentrating mobile anti-armour output where it hurts most before the opponent can reposition. Armies that can reliably shut down deep strike, screen aggressively, or alpha-strike the limited on-table presence before the reserves land will crack this list open.
663: Built around Cadian Shock Troops, Cadian Command Squads, Rogal Dorn Battle Tanks, Rogal Dorn Commanders, Scout Sentinels, Kasrkin, and Chimeras, this is a Combined Arms gunline that weaponizes Lethal Hits across both infantry and armour — Regiment units shredding visible infantry, Squadron vehicles burning through Monsters and Vehicles with the same efficiency. The win condition is layered firepower: mass bodies hold and screen objectives while Rogal Dorns and Sentinels hammer armoured targets with mobile anti-tank pressure, generating kills through volume and Lethal Hits rather than spike damage. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that struggle to absorb sustained shooting from multiple directions simultaneously. It cracks open against alpha-strike lists and armies that can close distance fast, stripping the shooting window before the gunline can compound its efficiency.
664: Built around Bloodcrushers, Bloodthirsters, Rendmasters on Blood Throne, Flesh Hounds, and Be'lakor, this is a Cavalcade of Chaos cavalry hammer that floods the midboard with fast, hard-hitting Khorne Mounted units backed by a shadow-wreathed daemon primarch. The engine is fall-back-and-charge: Mounted units disengage from bad matchups or overextended combats, then immediately shoot or charge again, letting Bloodcrushers and Rendmasters cycle through targets relentlessly while Be'lakor with Fade to Darkness ghosts between threats. It punishes static, low-mobility armies that can't reposition away from repeated charges, overwhelming them through layered lethal hits across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. Armies that can alpha-strike the cavalry before it engages, or stack enough anti-mounted firepower to delete key units in one turn, crack this list open before the fall-back-and-charge loop ever gets running.
665: Built around Be'lakor, a Bloodthirster, a Great Unclean One, and dense waves of Plaguebearers and Nurglings, this Shadow Legion force plays a grinding, multi-layered attrition game across every phase. Warptide lets Battleline units advance and still shoot and charge, so Plaguebearers surge into scoring positions without sacrificing combat eligibility, while Be'lakor and the Bloodthirster apply lethal pressure from deep in the opponent's half. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally — the horde volume overwhelms efficient damage trades, and layered Lethal Hits across multiple combat threats make every engagement costly for fragile high-value units. However, high-volume mortal-wound output or mass blast weaponry that degrades the screen fast exposes the heavier pieces before they can meaningfully engage, and the build lacks the raw damage ceiling to reliably crack heavily armoured targets at range.
666: Built around wall-to-wall Daemonettes, Fiends, Keepers of Secrets, the Contorted Epitome, the Tormentbringer, and the Masque of Slaanesh, this list plays Legion of Excess supported by Warptide to create a relentlessly mobile Slaanesh horde that never stops threatening combat. The engine is simple and brutal: Daemonettes advance and still charge via Warptide, while the entire army exploits Legion of Excess's fell-back-then-charge rule to stay locked into melee across multiple turns, grinding opponents off objectives through layered combat pressure rather than a single knockout blow. It punishes slower, static armies that cannot disengage from combat—any list relying on shooting from fixed positions gets swarmed, recycled back onto, and bled dry across every scoring phase. It cracks apart against high-mobility elite lists that can selectively wipe squads before they reach combat, since losing initiative against its mass of fragile bodies collapses the engine entirely.
667: Built around Lords of Change, Bloodcrushers, and Be'lakor, this list runs the Cavalcade of Chaos detachment to let its Mounted units fall back and still shoot or charge — turning every combat into a no-lose trade. The engine is relentless harassment: Bloodcrushers crash in, absorb a fight, fall back freely, then pile straight back into charges while Lords of Change and Be'lakor delete priority targets from range or melee. It punishes slow, static armies that rely on locking units in combat to neutralize threats, since the fall-back-and-charge loop completely defeats that plan. However, it struggles against high-volume anti-armour shooting or elite melee that can delete Bloodcrushers before they cycle out of danger.
668: Built around Lords of Change (averaging two per list), Screamers, Flamers, and Kairos Fateweaver, this is a hyper-mobile Tzeentch daemon force running Scintillating Legion with Warptide as its secondary detachment. The engine is Flux-token manipulation — banking re-rolls across Hit, Wound, and Damage rolls to guarantee key kill chains — while Screamers and Flamers use Warptide's Advance-and-charge and Assault-after-Advance rules to threaten every corner of the board simultaneously. It punishes slower, durable armies that rely on positioning and toughness thresholds, overwhelming them with layered lethal output from multiple threat vectors across multiple turns. It cracks open against lists that can deny its mobility windows or alpha-strike its fragile daemon bodies before Flux tokens stabilise the damage output.
669: Built around the Bloodthirster, Be'lakor, Lords of Change, Cultist Mob, Flesh Hounds, Beasts of Nurgle, and Plaguebearers, this Shadow Legion list blends elite Daemon primarchs with a sprawling, multi-god horde across a wide threat matrix. The win condition is layered pressure: Be'lakor and Lords of Change threaten from range and sky while the Bloodthirster hunts priority targets, Flesh Hounds chase down backfield threats, and Battleline units advance-and-fire via Warptide to grind objectives before the opponent stabilises. It punishes mid-range gunlines that can't simultaneously handle monstrous melee threats, skimming Battleline, and tanky Nurgle bodies clogging their lanes. However, lists that spike damage efficiently into the big characters or leverage deep strike denial collapse the engine before the multi-threat pressure can compound.
670: Built around Skarbrand, Be'lakor, a Great Unclean One, a Lord of Change, Beasts of Nurgle, Plaguebearers, and Flesh Hounds, this Daemonic Incursion list blends Chaos God keywords across a wide roster of elite monsters and screening chaff. The detachment's deep strike rule lets units arrive inside the Shadow of Chaos or within 6" of named Greater Daemons without scatter penalties, so the plan is to threaten multiple board zones simultaneously — landing Flesh Hounds and Beasts of Nurgle aggressively to contest objectives while Skarbrand and Be'lakor hunt high-value targets. It punishes armies that rely on tight bubble-wrap or single-layer screens, as the layered threat of cheap deep striking chaff followed by heavy hitters overwhelms piecemeal defensive positioning. However, lists with strong alpha-strike output or dense long-range shooting can dismantle the Greater Daemon core before the engine fully assembles, and the build's below-average win rate suggests opponents who prioritize first-turn pressure frequently crack it open before it stabilises.
671:
Built around Flesh Hounds and Skarbrand, this is a hyper-mobile melee hammer that floods the midboard with fast Khorne threats and leans on Blood Legion's surge move — triggered when enemies move within 8" — to close distance reactively and punish any repositioning the opponent attempts.

The engine is relentless forward pressure: Flesh Hounds advance and still charge thanks to Warptide's battleline ability, Skarbrand lands as a singular assassination threat, and Brazenmaw (on more than half of lists) supercharges a key character to amplify the kill chain turn after turn.

It punishes slow, infantry-heavy armies that can't avoid triggering Blood Legion surges and that fold to layered melee contact across multiple units simultaneously.

It cracks when facing armies that can consistently screen at distance, deny reactive surge triggers through careful movement discipline, or overload it with durable multi-wound targets that neutralize Skarbrand before he swings.
672: Built around Infractors, Lord Exultants, Tormentors, Defilers, Flawless Blades, Daemon Princes, Noise Marines, Chaos Spawn, and Rhino-mounted infantry, this is a mobile mid-table brawler running the Coterie of the Conceited detachment, where the Warlord pledges a kill count each round and earns Pact points by meeting it. The engine is a self-reinforcing kill loop — you commit to a number, deliver the kills through overlapping melee and shooting threats, and convert Pact points into escalating board presence that funds scoring. It punishes slower, tankier armies that cannot clear multiple elite threat vectors simultaneously, as the Rhino transports keep infantry alive to deliver pledges consistently while Defilers and Daemon Princes provide mobile anti-armour overload. High-volume chaff armies that can absorb punishment without offering clean kill counts will stall the pledge engine, leaving you Pact-starved and unable to accelerate.
673: Built around Lord Kakophonists, Noise Marines, Infractors, Tormentors, Flawless Blades, and Lord Exultants packed into Chaos Rhinos, with Lucius the Eternal, Daemon Princes of Slaanesh with Wings, and Defilers rounding out a deep, mobile infantry hammer. The plan is to surge transports into midfield, disembark and charge en masse — leaning on Sensational Performance to redirect melee swings into fresh targets each fight phase and on Coterie's pledge mechanic to convert kills into cumulative Pact point advantages. It punishes horde and mid-board brawler armies that can't weather repeated waves of high-volume, assault-focused infantry hitting from multiple transports simultaneously. However, lists built around durable elite armour or those that can screen out the charge lanes crack this army open, since the kill-engine stalls badly when units can't reach engagement range or pledge targets evaporate before the end of the battle round.
675: Built around Chaos Spawn, Infractors, Lords Exultant, Tormentors, Defilers, Flawless Blades, Noise Marines, and Lucius the Eternal, all ferried forward in Rhinos with a winged Daemon Prince providing mobile threat, this is a mid-table brawler that floods objectives with cheap, durable chaff while elite melee infantry do the killing. The core engine is Infractors and Tormentors piling out of transports to contest and fight, with Spawn soaking return fire and Lords Exultant amplifying nearby units into dangerous combat threats. It punishes infantry-heavy armies that can't clear durable chaff efficiently, letting Spawn screen key pieces while Flawless Blades and Noise Marines grind through lighter targets. Armies that pack high-volume anti-armour or elite melee that ignores its screening layer can crack the transport bubble early and strand key units before they reach engagement range.
676: Built around Bladeguard Veterans and Infernus Squads riding Land Raider Redeemers, supported by Librarians, Eradicators, Vulkan He'stan, Scouts, and Intercessors, this is a fire-heavy castle that delivers elite melee and melta assets in armoured transports while a Librarius Conclave psychic discipline buffs the whole force each round. The win condition is cracking open midfield with the Redeemer's flamecraft delivery, using He'stan to amplify flame weapons on Infernus Squads and Eradicators to antitank overload anything that survives the assault. It punishes horde armies and medium-armour lists badly, stacking high-volume flame hits and melta into targets that cannot absorb both threat vectors simultaneously. Concentrated long-range anti-tank fire or units that can strip the Redeemers early leave the Bladeguard and Infernus Squads stranded on foot and unable to project threat across the board.
677: Built around multiple Librarians buffing Intercessors, Scout Squads, and Bladeguard Veterans, this list floods mid-table with durable infantry bodies screened by cheap scouts while psyker-fuelled disciplines rotate between movement, accuracy, and firepower depending on the matchup. The win condition is objective saturation through volume — layered infantry screens hold secondaries while Bladeguard punch forward to lock enemy scoring units in melee and Librarian buffs convert mid-strength firepower into meaningful damage trades. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear numerous tough infantry blobs, particularly when Divination Discipline turns mass bolt fire into a reliable grind. However, it cracks under high-volume mortal wound output or blast weapons that make the infantry density a liability rather than a strength.
678: Built around Bladeguard Veterans, Marneus Calgar, Captain Titus, Wardens of Ultramar, Terminator Assault squads, and a Librarian cycling Psychic Disciplines each round, this list pairs the Librarius Conclave's round-by-round discipline selection with Reclamation Force's objective-linked AP bonus and defensive buff to create a durable, multi-layered melee-and-firebase hybrid. The win condition is grinding objectives through elite, hard-to-remove bodies while Calgar and Titus amplify nearby units, using whichever Discipline best fits the target — Divination for reliable damage, Biomancy for repositioning, Pyromancy for ranged clearing — and punishing anything that tries to contest in melee with the AP-boosted Reclamation Force attacks. It punishes mid-range gunlines and armies that cannot efficiently remove 2+ save elite infantry, stacking defensive objective control against volume fire. It cracks under concentrated high-AP anti-tank shooting or fast alpha-strike forces that deny it the controlled objective engagement the Reclamation Force defensive trigger demands.
679: Built around Marneus Calgar, Cato Sicarius, Victrix Honour Guard, Wardens of Ultramar, and a core of infantry screens in Scouts, Intercessors, and Incursors, this list plants itself inside terrain features and leverages the detachment's re-roll-1s-to-hit-and-wound plus the Entrenched keyword to make garrisoned units punishing to dislodge. Repulsor Executioners provide the heavy gunline backbone, firing from covered positions while screened infantry hold objectives and deny enemy movement, making points primarily through durable objective control backed by sustained, accurate firepower. It punishes aggressive melee and combined-arms lists that need to trade into infantry efficiently, because Entrenched units sitting in terrain become disproportionately costly to shift. Lists that ignore terrain entirely — deep-strike-heavy or artillery-based armies that project threat from range — can bypass the defensive bonuses and starve the engine of its core interaction.
680: Built around Caanok Var, Assault Terminators, and a supporting brick of Terminator-armoured characters, this Hammer of Avernii list uses Caanok's RECALCULATING ability to chain Oath of Moment targets together, keeping re-roll-wounds-of-1 active even as priority threats are destroyed. The engine is a relentless target-designation loop: Terminators and Ballistus Dreadnoughts hammer whatever Caanok is pointing at, while Scouts and screening bodies hold objectives and protect the advance. It punishes armies built around one or two central damage-dealers, because killing the current Oath target simply hands Caanok the next one, sustaining offensive pressure turn after turn. Where it cracks is against lists that flood the board with redundant activations and cheap bodies, forcing Oath targets onto irrelevant units and degrading the kill chain's efficiency faster than the Terminator core can compensate.
681: Built around Librarians in Terminator Armour, Terminator Assault Squads, standard Terminator Squads, Marneus Calgar, an Ancient in Terminator Armour, Bladeguard Veterans, and Scout screens, this Librarius Conclave list cycles Psychic Disciplines each battle round — Divination for hit/wound rerolls, Biomancy for mobility, Pyromancy for ranged pressure — tuning the entire force to whatever the game state demands. The win condition is controlling objectives with durable Terminator bricks that gain AP-1 in melee through Reclamation Force while the Ancient's aura keeps them fighting through attrition, with Temporal Corridor enabling aggressive repositioning to contest or flip key markers. It punishes mid-range elite armies that can't outgrind sustained melee pressure from Terminators benefiting from objective-range AP bonuses and reroll stacking. Massed low-AP shooting that strips Terminators before they engage, or high-mobility skew lists that simply avoid melee range, expose the build's dependence on staying in objective range to activate its core defensive and offensive triggers.
682: Built around Darnath Lysander, Terminator Assault Squads, Terminator Squads, Vanguard Veterans with jump packs, Bladeguard Veterans, and a Librarian, this is a dense, multi-wave melee and fire-support list running the Emperor's Shield detachment, which hands Lysander full wound re-rolls against the Oath of Moment target and gives the broader army wound-1 re-rolls on the same target. The plan is to identify a priority threat early, stack Oath of Moment wound re-rolls onto it through Lysander's enhanced version, and bulldoze it off objectives while Terminator bricks hold ground and jump infantry contest flanks. It punishes armies that rely on a single powerful anchor — monsters, vehicles, elite infantry blocks — because concentrating the re-roll engine on one target makes that unit collapse disproportionately fast. It struggles against fast, spread-out armies that deny clean Oath of Moment focus and can kite the slow Terminator core, bleeding it for points across multiple objectives before it can consolidate.
683: Built around Heavy Intercessors, Intercessors, Assault Intercessors, Librarians, Apothecary Biologis, and Iron Father Feirros, this is a dense battleline gunline that floods the mid-table with durable, self-sufficient infantry blobs operating under Bastion Task Force — meaning every unit can shoot, charge, and perform Actions after Advancing or Falling Back without penalty. The win condition is suffocating objective coverage while the detachment's post-attack debuff chips enemy units down in place, with Librarians cycling Psychic Disciplines to splice in re-rolls or speed boosts exactly where the battleline needs them and Apothecary Biologis keeping key squads alive past their natural shelf life. It punishes low-model-count elite armies through sheer volume of durable bodies — opponents struggle to trade efficiently when every wound costs resources and the infantry wall never fully clears. It cracks under coordinated alpha strikes or high-AP multi-damage output that bypasses the resilience stacking, particularly from lists that can erase full squads before the Apothecary's healing loop engages.
686: Built around Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes, Outrider Squads, Scout Squads, Intercessors, and Suboden Khan, this list leans into the Fulguris Task Force's first-turn ingress move to deploy its entire SPEEDER battlegroup aggressively forward before the opponent can react. The win condition is an early-game anti-armour overload — Hammerstrikes and Land Speeders crash into mid-board on turn one while Outriders and Khan's melee threat force the opponent to split attention, scoring through presence and attrition rather than a single alpha strike. It punishes slow, castle-style gunlines that cannot reposition fast enough to counter multiple simultaneous threats across the board. It cracks under pressure from elite close-combat armies or heavy deep-strike denial lists that either screen the ingress lanes or trade efficiently enough to strip the speeder core before it can generate sustained scoring pressure.
687: Built around War Dog Executioners, Brigands, Karnivores, and Stalkers backed by a Knight Abominant and Knight Ruinator, this is an all-armour warpack running the Helhunt Lance detachment — which extends the Abominant's aura buffs to itself whenever two or more War Dogs are in range, creating a self-reinforcing threat bubble. The win condition is layered anti-armour pressure across the whole board: War Dogs swarm objectives while the Titanic Knights punish anything heavy, with Nurglings providing cheap screen to protect the pack's flanks and scoring. It punishes infantry-light armoured lists that cannot contest multiple vectors simultaneously, using mobile threat density to force catastrophic trade decisions. Concentrated high-damage elite shooting — anything that can crack multiple T10+ targets per turn — exposes how fragile individual War Dogs are once the aura bubble fractures.
688: Built around Nemesis Dreadknights, Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, and Interceptor Squads screened by Strike Squads, this is a mobile hammer list that floods the board with heavy walkers and teleporting infantry across a detachment-agnostic framework of Immaterial Interdiction and Sanctic Spearhead. The plan is to leverage Sanctic Spearhead's 6" Advance bonus and Assault conversion on Grey Knights Vehicles to drive Dreadknights into mid-board early, then use Interceptor surge moves to threaten objectives and force unfavorable trades while the Grand Masters amplify the kill chain. It punishes slower armoured lists that cannot contest mid-board efficiently, as multiple high-damage walkers advancing at threat ranges most opponents aren't built to handle across the whole table. However, mass high-volume shooting or deep-strike denial armies that can isolate and focus individual Dreadknights before they consolidate will crack the list open, since losing even one walker early collapses the damage math significantly.
689: Built around multiple Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Purgation Squads, Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, and Castellan Crowe, this is a Brotherhood Strike list that floods the board with deep-striking infantry supported by hard-hitting walker-commanders. The win condition is a coordinated deep strike surge that uses Brotherhood Strike's re-roll-1s-to-hit-and-wound on arrival turns to crack open key targets while Purgation Squads pin enemy units and force battle-shock rolls through Fires of Purgation, disrupting the opponent's scoring and positioning. It punishes static gunlines and lower-mobility armies that cannot reposition away from the arrival wave, layering mortal pressure from multiple simultaneous deep strike threats. It struggles against armies that can screen landing zones effectively or alpha-strike the relatively fragile infantry before it gets its re-roll turns online.
693: Built around multiple Crusade Ancients babysitting waves of Crusader Squads, Execrators, Scouts, Intercessors, and the Emperor's Champion, this is a mass-horde gunline that floods the board with bodies protected by the Vindication Task Force's wound-roll subtraction on Ancient units holding objectives. The win condition is attrition through volume: Crusader Squads surge into position while Execrators and Intercessors pour fire downrange, keeping Ancients planted on objectives where they become disproportionately tough to shift. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that rely on high-Strength shooting to delete scoring units efficiently, since those attacks are taxed by the wound penalty whenever an Ancient is on an objective. Horde mirrors or armies that flood cheap bodies to contest objectives can overwhelm the screen economy, and anything that bypasses wound rolls entirely or targets non-Ancient units first will erode the infantry bubble faster than it can be replenished.
694: Built around pairs of Repulsor Executioners supported by Techmarines, an Emperor's Champion, and dense infantry blocks of Assault Intercessors, Sword Brethren, Crusaders, and Scouts, this list runs Ironstorm Spearhead to squeeze a re-roll — hit, wound, or damage — out of every Adeptus Astartes unit once per phase. The plan is to park the Repulsor Executioners in dominant fire lanes, keep them repaired and operational with Techmarines carrying Adept of the Omnissiah and The Flesh Is Weak, and grind opponents off objectives while the skimmer guns punish anything armoured. It absolutely punishes mid-table armour-heavy lists that cannot hide from sustained, re-rolled heavy firepower delivered from durable, self-sustaining platforms. The weakness is volume: cheap horde armies or elite infantry that can swamp the screen, trade efficiently into the foot troops, and get close enough to silence the guns crack it open fast.
695: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators (two squads), Logan Grimnar, Ragnar Blackmane, Arjac Rockfist, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Blood Claws, Wolf Guard Headtakers, and Wolf Scouts, this is a Saga of the Great Wolf brawler that floods the board with elite melee bodies backed by a legendary character stack. The win condition is using the Hunting Pack rotations — particularly Encircling Jaws for re-rolled Advance and Charge rolls — to crash multiple threats into midfield simultaneously, with Ragnar, Logan, and Arjac enabling kill chains that snowball into objective control. It punishes slower, static lists that can't handle multi-threat charges across multiple vectors, especially gunlines that lack the volume of shooting to strip Terminators and Wulfen before contact. It cracks open against elite armies that can pick apart the character cluster at range, since losing key synergy pieces early collapses the coordinated assault the whole engine depends on.
696: Built around Logan Grimnar, Ragnar Blackmane, Arjac Rockfist, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, multiple squads of Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Wulfen with Storm Shields, and Blood Claws screened by a Wolf Guard Battle Leader, this Saga of the Beastslayer list is a melee-first brawling horde that floods the mid-table with elite infantry and legendary characters. The win condition is activating Lethal Hits across every attack by hunting Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles to complete the Beastslayer tally, then snowballing that efficiency into cleared units and scored primaries through sheer combat volume. It punishes elite low-model-count lists by overwhelming their key pieces with Lethal Hits-fuelled attrition before they can thin the horde enough to matter. Armies that can kite, screen deeply, or drop mass mortal wounds at range from safety deny it the close-range engagements it needs to trigger its kill chain.
697: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Ragnar Blackmane, Blood Claws, Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, Wulfen with Storm Shields, and Bjorn the Fell-Handed, this is a melee-heavy brawler that floods the midboard with overlapping infantry threats across multiple unit types. The plan is to overwhelm opponents through sheer combat volume — multiple independent hammer units charge in sequence, with Ragnar and Logan amplifying nearby units while Headtakers and Wulfen punch through elite targets. It punishes slow, static gunlines that lack the board coverage to screen against simultaneous multi-angle charges from a mobile toolbox with this many independent threats. Its weakness is elite melee armies and alpha-strike builds that can isolate and delete key characters before the charge train gets rolling, since the engine depends heavily on named heroes surviving to buff their companions.
700:
Built around Cerastus Knight Lancers, Canis Rex, and Knight Destriers, this is an aggressive, mobile Knights force running the Questoris Companions detachment — which chains Oaths together turn after turn, stacking fulfilled conditions to generate continuous momentum throughout the game.

The win condition is relentless pressure: by cycling Oaths, the army sustains buffs across multiple phases and Knights, letting it dictate threat priority against the opponent while bullying them off objectives through sheer melee and shooting output from high-mobility chassis.

It punishes static armour-heavy lists that cannot reposition quickly enough to avoid being isolated and destroyed piecemeal by fast-moving Knights with overlapping lethal profiles.

Its weakness is volume firepower from horde or screen-heavy lists that can strip wounds faster than Oaths can regenerate staying power, especially if the opponent successfully staggers activations to deny clean charges.
701: Built around Deathwatch Veterans, Deathwatch Terminators, dual Librarians, and Intercessor squads, this is a mid-table shooting and brawling force that leans on Firestorm Assault Force in most lists to give its ranged weapons Assault and a Strength bump inside 12", turning aggressive repositioning into raw killing power. The plan is to push Terminators and Veterans forward behind Intercessor screens, close to within 12" to trigger that Strength bonus, and leverage Librarian psychic disciplines — Divination for re-rolls or Biomancy for movement — to crack priority targets and score through raw attrition. It punishes horde armies and gunlines hard, since the combination of high model-count screens, massed bolter volume, and close-range Strength bonuses overloads light-save and medium-save targets efficiently. It struggles against fast elite armies that can bypass the screen, isolate Terminators before they close, and avoid that 12" killzone entirely.
702: Built around Gretchin screens, Boyz, Nobz, and Bannernobs flooding the midboard, with Ghazghkull Thraka and Warbosses driving a core of Trukks and Battlewagons, all running Freebooter Krew. The plan is to designate a loot objective each Command phase and overwhelm it with a wall of bodies while Sustained Hits 1 on every Infantry, Mounted, and Walker attack — triggered when a unit is near the loot objective — pumps Flash Gitz and Boyz into lethal volume fire. Kommandos add a flanking threat that forces opponents to split attention, and the sheer model count punishes elite low-body armies that can't clear objectives fast enough under attrition. Horde-hate lists with massed high-AP blasts or combat-focused alpha-strike armies can gut the screen before the loot-objective engine gets rolling.
708: Built around Allarus Custodians, Caladius Grav-Tanks, Witchseekers, Custodian Guard, a Blade Champion, and a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, this list splits between Tharanatoi Hammerblow's ingress-then-charge threat with Terminators and Solar Spearhead's vehicle OC-boosting presence. The plan is to layer threat vectors — tanks parking on objectives at elevated OC while Allarus and the Shield-Captain ingress to threaten charges — forcing opponents to answer multiple problems simultaneously. It punishes slow, durable armies that cannot redeploy quickly, as the combination of high-OC vehicles and hard-hitting Terminator drops overwhelms static defenders. It cracks open against aggressive early pressure and elite melee armies that can strip vehicles below Starting Strength before the OC and hit-roll benefits have done their work.
710: Built around Caladius grav-tanks, Telemon and Contemptor-Achillus dreadnoughts, Contemptor-Galatuses, Venerable Contemptors, and Witchseeker and Prosecutor infantry screens operating under the Solar Spearhead and Silent Hunters detachments, this list plays a dense, mobile combined-arms game. The engine is vehicle-led objective control — Caladius tanks at Starting Strength gain +2 OC from Solar Spearhead, letting them contest and lock primaries while dreadnoughts press forward with layered lethal threat to force trades on unfavorable terms. It punishes balanced and mid-range gunline lists that can't simultaneously answer elite vehicles, multiple dreadnought bodies, and Anathema Psykana harassment, spreading anti-tank rolls too thin across too many hard targets. Pure melee alpha-strike armies or high-volume anti-vehicle spam can strip the Caladius tanks below Starting Strength early and collapse the OC engine before it pays off.
717: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, Castigators, and a dense web of Immolator-mounted infantry, Canonesses, Celestian Sacresants, Celestian Insidiants, Hospitallers, Arco-Flagellants, and Dominion Squads, this list is a deliberately attrition-hungry machine that weaponises its own casualties. The win condition is the Hallowed Martyrs detachment rule — the more units get ground down below Starting Strength or Below Half-strength, the sharper every attack becomes, so the list actively fishes for that damage threshold to punch back harder while Hospitallers slow the bleed. It punishes aggressive armies that spread damage across many units rather than deleting them cleanly, because partial casualties trigger the hit and wound bonuses without killing the unit's output. However, a precision alpha-strike that systematically erases whole units before they can drop below threshold denies the engine entirely, leaving the list performing at baseline.
718: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, Castigators, Immolators, and Dominion Squads, this is a fast, mech-heavy fire army that leverages the Bringers of Flame detachment to give every Adepta Sororitas ranged weapon the Assault ability — meaning the entire force advances and shoots without penalty, while closing to within 6" spikes Strength on every shot. The plan is to rush forward in Immolator transports, unload Dominion Squads at close range for the Strength bonus, and stack Castigator and Warsuit firepower into whatever the opponent values most, scoring through board control enabled by overwhelming short-range volume. It punishes static gunlines and low-mobility armies that can't retreat out of the 6" threat bubble before the Strength bonuses compound into vehicle-cracking damage. Tight, aggressive mobile lists and anything that forces this army to fight beyond 6" — particularly deep-striking threats or fast screens that deny advance lanes — will disrupt the close-range engine before it gets rolling.
719: Built around Repentia Squads, Arco-Flagellants, and Celestian Sacresants delivered via Sororitas Rhinos, with Hospitallers and Ministorum Priests layering buffs and the Triumph of Saint Katherine anchoring the support core, this is a Penitent Host list supplemented by Sacred Champions for +1 BS/WS on Celestian units. The win condition is wave-after-wave melee pressure — rotating Vows of Atonement to spike movement or combat output each round, flooding midboard objectives with expendable fanatics while Rhinos deliver the hardest-hitting units into knife-fight range. It punishes slow, low-body armies that cannot screen against multiple simultaneous threat vectors, drowning them in volume-of-attack melee before they can concentrate fire. Against shooting-heavy lists with reliable board control, the lack of ranged threat means Rhinos get stripped before delivering their cargo, and losing even one transport badly degrades the timing the whole plan depends on.
720: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, Celestian Sacresants, and a deep transport network of Immolators and Rhinos, this is a mobile mid-range gunline that uses the Champions of Faith detachment to designate up to three units per Command phase as Righteous, boosting their Move, Leadership, and weapon skill to create rotating threat windows across the board. The win condition is layering Castigator tank fire and Paragon anti-armour output with Righteous-buffed Sacresants threatening melee, while Hospitallers keep key pieces alive long enough to contest and score through attrition. It punishes armies that rely on mid-weight armour and exposed infantry blobs, using skimmer-mounted Battle Sisters to reposition quickly and maintain board presence across multiple objectives. It cracks under pressure from elite alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete Vahl or the Warsuits before the Righteous rotation pays dividends, leaving the support structure with nothing to anchor around.
723: Built around Sydonian Dragoons with taser lances, Ironstrider Ballistarii, Sicarian Infiltrators, Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, Skitarii Rangers, and Skorpius Disintegrators, this list floods the midboard with fast, multi-layered threats across several detachment configurations. The plan is to use Dragoons as a mobile close-combat hammer crashing into mid-table while Ballistarii and Disintegrators strip armour at range, with Infiltrators and Rangers contesting objectives and forcing opponents to split attention. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count elite armies that can't handle simultaneous pressure from multiple fast vectors across the full board width. It cracks under concentrated anti-armour overload or deep-strike denial that shuts down the Infiltrator positioning, since the kill chain depends on coordinated arrival timing rather than raw staying power.
724: Built around Acolyte Iconwards leading Hybrid Metamorphs and Acolyte Hybrids, Purestrain Genestealers as a close-range hammer, wall-to-wall Neophyte Hybrid blobs, and Achilles Ridgerunners providing mobile anti-armour punch, this Xenocreed Congregation list is a layered mass-horde assault running Characters into every combat unit to unlock re-rolls on Advance and Charge rolls and Feel No Pain 3+ on the leaders themselves. The plan is to flood the mid-table with bodies, use Goliath Trucks to deliver Metamorphs and Acolytes into charge range, and grind opponents off objectives through sheer attrition while Ridgerunners threaten armour from range. It punishes gunlines and low-model-count elite armies that cannot clear the volume of wounds fast enough, with Neophyte blobs healing 3 wounds per Command phase inside terrain to frustrate removal. However, high-damage alpha-strike armies that can strip Characters early collapse the Feel No Pain bubble and leave the horde fragile, and armies with reliable mortal-wound output or blast weapons can chew through the massed infantry faster than the list regenerates.
725: Built around Ravenwing Command Squads, Black Knights, Outrider Squads, Land Speeder Vengeances, and Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, with Sammael, Azrael, and Lion El'Jonson providing command weight, this list runs Company of Hunters to fire on the move and fall back into shooting without penalty, making every bike and speeder a perpetual threat regardless of positioning. The win condition is relentless mobile anti-armour pressure — advance, shoot, contest, repeat — using skimmer fire and mounted assault to deny opponents safe havens while Scout Squads hold backfield objectives cheaply. Darkflight Pursuit's Ignores Cover on RAVENWING FLY units punishes armies that rely on terrain to protect key pieces, stripping that defensive layer entirely for speeders already pushing up the board. Concentrated melee threat or high volumes of anti-infantry mortal wounds can crack the relatively fragile mounted bodies before the pressure engine reaches full tempo.
726: Built around Lion El'Jonson, Azrael, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and a dense Ravenwing core of Black Knights, Command Squad, and Outriders, this is a Wrath of the Rock list that floods the board with durable Adeptus Astartes Infantry and Mounted units, forcing opponents to overkill every threat. The plan is to grind through the midfield with hard-to-wound elite bodies — the detachment's -1 to Wound rolls against units where Strength exceeds Toughness turns high-powered anti-elite shooting into a tax — while the Primarch and Azrael amplify combat output and Scouts hold flanks. It punishes lists that rely on mid-Strength weapons to clear elite infantry, as those attacks are systematically degraded. However, dedicated high-AP, low-Strength-over-Toughness weapons and mortal wound output bypass the protection entirely, cracking open this otherwise tough shell.
727: Built around Chaos Terminator Squads buffed by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Kravek Morne, Mutilators, and Cultist Mobs for cheap objective bodies, this list plays Cabal of Chaos — boosting psyker shooting and melee output through Dark Pacts. The plan is to use Cultists as a sacrificial screen while the Terminator brick and Mutilators grind through the midboard, scoring through sheer attrition and objective denial rather than speed. About half of lists add Warpstrike Champions, repositioning Terminators, Obliterators, and Mutilators off the table end-of-turn to reset threat angles and deny overwatch. It punishes midrange brawler armies that can't shift T4+ multi-wound infantry in volume, but struggles against high-AP shooting lists that can crack the brick before Dark Pacts generate enough return damage.
728: Built around Chaos Terminator squads, Mutilators, Warp Talons, and Raptors led by Kravek Morne and a Sorcerer in Terminator Armour, this list leans hard into the Murdertalon Raiders detachment's re-roll-hit-1s and -1-to-hit defensive bubble on HERETIC ASTARTES INFANTRY FLY units, with the Warpstrike Champions rule cycling up to two Terminator, Obliterator, or Mutilator units back onto the table at the end of each opponent's turn. The win condition is a mid-board brawl where flying infantry pressure enemies into half-strength or battle-shocked thresholds, then exploit the re-roll trigger to snowball combat and score through sheer attrition. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that bleed to half-strength quickly, stripping their offensive output with the -1-to-hit debuff while a cultist mob holds secondary objectives. Spread-out horde lists that never dip below half-strength deny the key re-roll trigger and can screen out the deep-striking Terminators and Mutilators before the repositioning engine gets going.
729: Built around Chaos Bikers, Cultist Mobs, Traitor Guardsmen, Defilers, and Chaos Rhinos operating under Pactbound Zealots, this list floods the board with cheap bodies while parking Daemon Engine firepower at range. The plan is to drown opponents in screening chaff — Cultists and Guardsmen holding flanks and objectives — while Defilers and Bikers threaten mobile anti-armour pressure and melee aggression backed by Lethal Hits on 5+ in combat. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that struggle to clear waves of expendable infantry before the Daemon Engines grind them down. However, it cracks under high-volume mortal wound output or strong anti-horde shooting that strips the chaff screens efficiently, leaving the heavier engines exposed and unsupported mid-table.
738: Built around Immortals, Technomancers, Plasmancers, Canoptek Wraiths, Tomb Blades, Ophydian Destroyers, Scarab Swarms, and the Void Dragon — all scaffolded by the Cryptek Conclave and Hand of the Dynasty detachments — this is a highly mobile shooting force that flexes its weapon type mid-phase, picking Anti-Infantry, Anti-Mounted, Heavy, or Ignores Cover on its Crypteks each turn while Immortals and Warriors advance and still shoot. The plan is to pressure every quadrant simultaneously, scoring through board control rather than a single kill chain, with the Void Dragon and Wraiths threatening flanks while screens of Scarabs and Warriors hold primary. It punishes mid-range gunlines that struggle to clear multiple overlapping threats across the board before action runners complete secondaries. It cracks open against armies that can delete Crypteks early, collapsing the adaptive-shooting engine and leaving the Immortals with baseline output.
739: Built around the Skorpekh Lord, Technomancer, Canoptek Wraiths, C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, Skorpekh Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Illuminor Szeras, Nekrosor Ammentar, Imotekh the Stormlord, and Canoptek Reanimator, Awakened Dynasty is a mobile, character-stacking elite army that uses its detachment's +1 to Hit on led units to sharpen every combat and shooting threat simultaneously. The win condition is threat saturation — flood multiple lanes with hard-to-kill, hitting-reliably units while Reanimators and Technomancers recycle bodies, forcing opponents to choose what they let score. It punishes armies that rely on evasion or low-volume high-quality attacks, since the blanket accuracy bonus and layered resurrection make trading inefficient. It cracks under high-volume mortal wound output or mass screening that denies its melee units clean charges before they can be healed back.
740: Built around Deathwatch Kill Teams, Subductor Squads, Imperial Navy Breachers, Watch Masters, and a dense supporting cast of Inquisitors, Navigators, Rogue Trader Entourages, Sisters of Battle squads, and Immolators delivered in Rhinos, this is a mass-horde gunline running Imperialis Fleet with Veiled Blade doubling up Assassin abilities as a secondary threat layer. The win condition is flooding objectives with durable, cheap infantry blobs while Imperialis Fleet's Eliminate At All Costs focuses the army's firepower to surgically delete priority targets each Command phase, keeping the scoring lanes clear. It punishes low-model-count elite armies by overwhelming them with sheer bodies, layered skimmer fire from Immolators, and transport-delivered pressure that makes trading efficiently nearly impossible. It cracks open when opponents bring high-volume, high-AP output that chews through infantry faster than the horde can restock, collapsing the screening network and exposing the relatively fragile midfield control structure.
741: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Kasrkin, Gaunt's Ghosts, Ursula Creed, Scout Sentinels, Cadian Shock Troops, Cadian Command Squads, and Krieg Combat Engineers, this is a dense infantry gunline that deep strikes elite kill units while flooding the board with expendable bodies. The plan is to use Scions dropped via deep strike for mobile anti-armour and skimmer fire while the horde of Shock Troops, Kasrkin, and Engineers holds objectives and bricks midfield under Command Squad orders. It punishes armies that cannot clear bodies efficiently, trading cheap infantry for scoring turns while elite units pick apart key targets from unexpected angles. Concentrated high-damage shooting or strong melee that can crack through the screening infantry and suppress the Command Squad order chain before the Scions land will expose how fragile individual units are once isolated.
743: Built around Flawless Blades, Noise Marines, Tormentors, Lord Kakophonists, and a winged Daemon Prince, this list runs the Spectacle of Slaughter detachment to give Flawless Blades Fights First, then ferries the bulk of its infantry forward in Chaos Rhinos to hit the midboard as a coordinated melee wave. The win condition is crashing charge-enabled units into contested objectives — Peerless Bladesmen rewards charging units with Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1, so the list scores by winning fights, holding ground, and denying the opponent's ability to trade efficiently. It punishes slower combat armies and horde infantry that can't survive Fights First pressure backed by high-volume melee output. It struggles against gunlines and alpha-strike lists that strip the Rhino transports before the charge lands, leaving the melee core exposed and reactive.
744: Built around Daemon Princes of Slaanesh with Wings, Maulerfiends, Defilers, Lords Exultant, Infractors in Rhinos, Tormentors, Noise Marines, and Flawless Blades, this Coterie of the Conceited list drives a wall of mobile threat into the mid-board every turn. The win condition is the Pact points engine: pledge an achievable kill count each round, cash it in consistently, and weaponize the accumulating Pact points to amplify the army's already punishing melee and anti-armour output. It punishes slower gunline and armour-heavy lists that cannot thin the wave of Maulerfiends and Princes before they hit combat, and the transported Infractors deny opponents clean objective holds. Lists that can alpha-strike the Princes and Maulerfiends off the board early disrupt the pledge math, leaving the slower infantry elements stranded without their kill-generating vanguard.
746: Built around Chaos Rhinos ferrying Infractors, Tormentors, and Noise Marines into position, supported by Lords Exultant, Daemon Princes with wings, Flawless Blades, Defilers, and walls of Chaos Spawn absorbing punishment at the front. The list wins by flooding mid-table with bodies, using the Spawn as disposable screening and threat-saturation while transported infantry delivers the real damage — primarily through the Coterie of the Conceited's Pact point engine, which rewards consistently destroying enemy units each round. This build punishes infantry-heavy and low-vehicle lists that cannot strip multiple tough mid-board units simultaneously, exploiting the Rhino-delivery speed and melee threat density to force bad trades. It cracks against elite armoured lists that can selectively delete key transport vectors before infantry disembark, stalling the kill-pledge engine and bleeding Pact point generation.
747: Built around War Dog Stalkers, Karnivores, and Brigands — six to eight fast, aggressive light Knights swarming the board with overlapping threat vectors. The plan is to pick apart opposing armies piece by piece using mobile anti-armour pressure across multiple activation windows, with Infernal Lance's Malefic Surge or Houndpack Lance's Sustained Hits 1 focus-fire funneling concentrated damage onto priority targets each turn. The sheer volume of durable, fast chassis punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot answer eight separate threat sources simultaneously, forcing unfavorable trades across the entire field. The build cracks under high-volume anti-tank lists that can efficiently strip individual War Dogs before they activate, since losing even two early collapses the activation economy the entire engine depends on.
748: Built around Knight Despoilers and War Dog Karnivores, this is a hard-hitting Chaos Knights force that leans on the Infernal Lance detachment's Malefic Surge mechanic — risking mortal wounds each Command phase to push its engines into an Empowered state that unlocks additional offensive options. The plan is straightforward aggression: use the Karnivores' mobility to crack open armour and isolate high-value targets while Despoilers deliver layered firepower and melee pressure across multiple threat axes simultaneously. It punishes slower, armour-heavy lists that can't spread damage efficiently, overwhelming them with multi-vector charges before they can trade economically. The central weakness is self-inflicted: failed Leadership tests bleed wounds off already fragile big models, and any opponent who can force attrition from range before the engines engage will exploit the build's dependence on surviving long enough to get Empowered.
749: Built around War Dog Karnivores, Executioners, Brigands, Stalkers, and a Knight Abominant, this is a fast, all-armour Chaos Knights swarm operating under the Hunting Warpack detachment, which lets War Dogs strip enemy concealment at close range to unlock full shooting. The plan is to flood the board with mobile firepower and melee threat simultaneously — Executioners and Brigands pour ranged damage into armoured targets while Karnivores crash into combat, using layered lethality across multiple activation windows to grind opponents off objectives. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally, where every War Dog activation trades efficiently against expensive units and there are no cheap screens to absorb the pressure. Horde armies and dense terrain crack it open, since the detection mechanic requires visibility within 12" and the list carries no real infantry to contest tight midboard pockets.
750:
Built around packs of War Dog Karnivores and Stalkers screened by dense Cultist Mob chaff, this is a mobile anti-armour swarm running Iconoclast Fiefdom to field DAMNED infantry that hold ground while the Knights hunt.

The win condition is layered lethality: Karnivores close and rip through vehicles in melee while Stalkers provide ranged threat, and Cultist screens deny enemy deep strikes and contest objectives cheaply, freeing the Knights to kill rather than babysit.

It punishes armour-heavy lists through anti-tank overload — too many fast, hard-hitting chassis to focus-fire efficiently — and the Cultist mass makes clearing screens a tax that delays pressure on the Knights themselves.

Where it cracks is against elite infantry armies that can ignore the Cultist screen and lock down individual War Dogs in unfavourable combat before the pack concentrates, and lists packing high volumes of AP mortal-wound output can degrade the Knights faster than the swarm can generate pressure in return.
753: Built around Castellan Crowe, multiple Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, and Brotherhood Terminators, this Warpbane Task Force list uses Purifier positioning to physically extend Hallowed Ground across the midboard, layering objective control with a mobile elite infantry core. The win condition is map domination through Hallowed Ground saturation — Purifiers push into No Man's Land to unlock additional detachment benefits while Dreadknights provide fast-moving anti-armour punch and Crowe enables Purifier synergies. It punishes slow or static armies that cannot contest multiple midfield objectives simultaneously, as the combined threat range of Dreadknights and Terminators forces an opponent to defend everywhere at once. Highly mobile elite forces that can collapse individual Purifier squads — breaking Hallowed Ground coverage — and armies with sufficient long-range firepower to strip Dreadknights before they engage will crack this list open.
754: Built around a mass of Nemesis Dreadknights led by Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, with Interceptor Squads and Strike Squads screening and contesting, all anchored to the Sanctic Spearhead detachment whose core trick adds 6" to Vehicle Advances and grants Assault on their ranged weapons. The plan is to surge Dreadknights deep into the opponent's half early, threatening lethal melee and shooting without sacrificing mobility, while Interceptors use Immaterial Interdiction surge moves after shooting to creep onto objectives and deny space. This build punishes slower elite armies that cannot outpace the Dreadknight threat vectors or clear the wave of infantry screening in front of them. It cracks open when faced with sufficient anti-tank overload that can strip Dreadknights before they close distance, leaving the infantry core without its hammer.
756: Built around multiple Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Purgation Squads, Purifier Squads, and Castellan Crowe, this list runs either Fires of Purgation or Warpbane Task Force to layer psychic shooting pressure across the board. The plan is to pin enemy units with Righteous Persecution, forcing battle-shock rolls at -1, while Dreadknights threaten mobile anti-armour and Purifiers extend Hallowed Ground to contest mid-table objectives under favorable conditions. It punishes horde-heavy armies hardest, where massed psychic firepower and battle-shock cascades can strip bodies and deny actions simultaneously. It cracks open against elite low-model-count armies that shrug off battle-shock and can surgically remove Purgation Squads before the pinning engine comes online.
759: Built around Logan Grimnar, multiple squads of Wolf Guard Terminators, Arjac Rockfist, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, and a Land Raider Redeemer, this is a Saga of the Great Wolf elite-melee hammer that floods the mid-table with heavily armoured bodies. The plan is to deliver Terminators and characters into the heart of the opponent's army via the Redeemer, using the detachment's rotating Hunting Pack buffs — particularly Encircling Jaws for free re-rolls on Advance and Charge — to ensure the assault connects every turn while Scout screens push early board control. It punishes elite and armoured lists that cannot generate enough high-AP volume to chew through multiple Terminator bricks before the characters compound the damage. Armies that can screen the Redeemer out of charge range, or that bring enough mortal-wound or mass-fire output to strip the Terminators before they engage, will crack the tempo this list depends on.
760: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Terminator Assault Squad, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, and Arjac Rockfist, this is a transport-heavy terminator hammer that floods the mid-table with armoured bodies. The win condition is delivering multiple terminator squads into melee through transports while Saga of the Great Wolf's rotating Hunting Packs — chiefly Encircling Jaws for re-rolled charges — guarantee the contact that turns elite infantry into scrap. It punishes lists that rely on expensive characters, monsters, or vehicles, since Saga of the Beastslayer arms the entire force with Lethal Hits against those target types, turning every swing into a deletion event. Lists that can screen the mid-table aggressively, deny transport lanes, or flood the board with cheap wounds stretch the terminator brick thin and exploit its low model count.
761: Built around swarms of Armiger Warglaives and Armiger Helverins, this list pairs the Throne-bonded Outriders detachment — granting Ignores Cover to Armigers under a Bondsman ability — with Valourstrike Lance, which converts Advances into Assault-mode shooting across the entire army. The win condition is relentless mobile anti-armour pressure: Advance freely, shoot without penalty, and strip saves from dug-in vehicles and monsters through guaranteed cover denial while the Bondsman chain keeps Armigers buffed every turn. It punishes static armoured lists brutally, denying the defensive value of terrain and overloading opponents who rely on cover saves to survive Knight-tier firepower. The build cracks open against armies that can screen flanks and force unfavourable charges early, since losing Armigers before Bondsman triggers come online collapses the buff chain and leaves the list trading inefficiently at range.
767: Built around near-infinite Boyz blobs, multiple Painboys, Ghazghkull Thraka, Gretchin screens, multiple Warbosses, Wazdakka Gutsmek, Kommandos, and Zodgrod Wortsnagga's supercharged Gretchin, this is a layered meat-grinder horde that floods every zone with bodies. The plan is to overwhelm the midboard through sheer volume of melee attacks sustained across multiple turns, with Painboys keeping blobs fighting well past their natural lifespan while Kommandos threaten backfield objectives to force overextension. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally — opponents simply cannot generate enough attacks to clear the wave before the next one crashes in. However, concentrated high-AP shooting that bypasses Feel No Pain-style healing, or powerful alpha-strike armies that can decapitate Ghazghkull and the Warboss stack before the Orks engage, can collapse the engine before it ever gets going.
768: Built around Squighog Boyz, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Ghazghkull Thraka, Beast Snagga Boyz, and Boyz packed into Trukks, this is a Freebooter Krew horde that plays as a relentless mid-board brawler — designating a loot objective each Command phase to funnel pressure onto a single priority marker while the mass of bodies contests everywhere else. The win condition is sustained melee attrition: Ghazghkull activates the Waaagh!, Squighog Boyz and mounted Beastbosses crash into the most valuable target, and Sustained Hits 1 on every attack turns volume into a kill chain that dismantles elite infantry and exposed monsters. It punishes slow or fragile armies that can't clear mid-board presence fast enough, drowning them under layers of cheap Gretchin screens, Trukk-delivered threats, and relentless scoring on the loot objective. It cracks against armies that can strip Trukks before disembarkation or hold the mid-board with durable, high-damage units that trade up efficiently against Ork squads.
771: Built around Sorcerers in Terminator Armour leading Scarab Occult Terminators, supported by Sekhetar Robots, Rubric Marines, Tzaangors, and Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, this list plays a layered, mass-horde castle that floods the board with durable Psychic units across multiple tiers of toughness. The win condition is attrition and objective suffocation — the Enlightened provide mid-range Psychic skimmer fire to soften targets while the Terminators and Robots form a resilient central brawling core that grinds through scoring turns. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot clear multiple durable screening layers fast enough, trading efficiently across all phases. Mortal-wound spam and high-volume anti-horde shooting crack it open by bypassing invulnerable saves and thinning the screens that protect the expensive Terminator anchor.
772: Built around Magnus the Red, a winged Daemon Prince, multiple Sorcerers, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Tzaangor Enlightened, Tzaangors, Chaos Spawn, and Sekhetar Robots, this Grand Coven list is a layered psychic-firepower machine wrapped in a deep infantry shell. It wins by cycling the detachment's rotating command-phase abilities — extending psychic weapon ranges or amplifying psychic lethality — to project kill power across the board while Rubrics and Terminators, buffed by Sorcerers, grind objectives under transport protection. It punishes mid-density elite armies that lack the volume to strip multiple durable, psychic-enhanced infantry bricks simultaneously, exploiting the Eldritch Vortex and Umbralefic Crystal enhancements to overload specific threat corridors. Armies that can alpha-strike Magnus or flood the board with enough bodies to drown the psychic output before the ability rotation matters crack it open early.
773: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened, Scarab Occult Terminators, Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Rubric Marines, and supporting Sorcerers, this is a transport-heavy infantry phalanx that floods mid-board with bodies while maintaining a layered psychic support structure across multiple detachment configurations. The win condition is attrition-through-volume: Scarab Occult Terminators and Tzaangor Enlightened crack open mid-table objectives while Sorcerors fuel Ritual chains that continuously heal psyker units back to fighting strength, making the list punishingly expensive to grind down. It excels against elite low-model-count armies that struggle to generate enough attacks to chew through stacked invulnerable saves and the Rubricae's built-in damage-1 armour save bonus simultaneously. It cracks open under sustained high-damage, multi-vector pressure — anything that bypasses invulnerables with mortal wounds or spikes consistent Damage 2+ attacks can outpace the healing engine before it stabilises.
774: Built around Defilers, Forgefiends, Sekhetar Robots, a winged Daemon Prince, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, and half the time Magnus the Red, this is a Hexwarp Thrallband list that floods the board with Daemon Engines and Psychic-tagged melee threats. The win condition is controlling No Man's Land objectives to extend the Flow of Magic across the midfield, then leveraging the Sekhetar Cohort's +1 WS aura from nearby Psykers to crash boosted Sekhetar Robots into whatever the Forgefiends and Enlightened have already softened at range. It punishes mid-density armoured lists badly, stacking mobile anti-tank from multiple angles while the layered Psychic shooting strips screens before the melee wave arrives. Armies that can deny its midfield objective control early collapse the Flow of Magic engine, and elite hordes with strong alpha-strike capability can gut the Daemon Engines before the aura synergy goes online.
776: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Tzaangor Enlightened with fatecaster greatbows, Sekhetar Robots, and a deep Sorcerer support stack, Grand Coven floods the board with layered psychic lethality across multiple unit types and ranges. The engine rotates Grand Coven's Command phase ability each turn to amplify whichever threat axis is most punishing — extending psychic weapon range to stretch the kill bubble or stacking mortal output — while Rhinos push Rubrics and Tzaangors onto objectives and Magnus and the Daemon Prince create unsolvable priority problems. It punishes elite low-model-count armies by drowning them in psychic mortal wounds from too many vectors simultaneously. Armies that can strip screens fast and close into melee before Grand Coven cycles its abilities will crack the tempo, and the build's footprint makes it vulnerable to concentrated alpha strikes that remove key Sorcerer support before the engine activates.
777: Built around Rubric Marines and Scarab Occult Terminators behind a dense character package — a Daemon Prince of Tzeentch, an Infernal Master, a Sorcerer in Terminator Armour, and in half the lists Ahriman and an Exalted Sorcerer — with a Mutalith Vortex Beast, a Chaos Rhino, and a Chaos Vindicator, this Hexwarp Thrallband list played the slow, durable Thousand Sons game. The Rubrics anchored objectives while the Terminators and the Daemon Prince committed into whatever the character stack had softened, with the Mutalith supplying the mobile threat the infantry lacked and the Vindicator answering armour. It punished armies that had to grind through resilient multi-wound infantry without efficient volume. It collapsed against alpha-strike lists that removed the characters early, since so few units carried the plan. Six games survive under current rules, so no win rate is published.
780: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Sorcerers, and Chaos Spawn screening in mass numbers, this Grand Coven list uses the detachment's rotating Command phase abilities — including extended Psychic weapon range and enhanced Psychic shooting — to project overwhelming firepower while flooding the board with bodies. The win condition is layering Psychic shooting from Magnus and Rubric Marines behind a thick Chaos Spawn and Tzaangor screen, using mobile pieces like the winged Daemon Prince and Exalted Sorcerer on Disc to threaten flanks and pressure secondaries. It punishes static gunlines that struggle to chew through horde bodies before the Psychic payoff units get range-extended and into position. It cracks open against elite melee armies that can punch through the screen cleanly and close into Magnus before the Psychic abilities cycle through their one-per-battle uses.
781: Built around Khorne Berzerkers and Masters of Executions piling out of Chaos Rhinos and Chaos Land Raiders, with Eightbound, Exalted Eightbound, Slaughterbound, and Goremongers flooding the midboard alongside Daemon Prince of Khorne and Khârn the Betrayer as character muscle. The gameplan is a coordinated disembark-charge engine: Goretrack Onslaught grants +1 to Charge rolls and Lance on melee weapons the turn units exit transports, so Rhinos drive deep, dump Berzerkers into the face of whatever threatens the objectives, and Eightbound variants clean up anything left standing. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't screen every lane, where the sheer volume of charging bodies — amplified by Vessels of Wrath's Cleave or AP boost on characters — overwhelms targeted defenses. Armies with strong overwatch, high-volume shooting, or deep-strike denial that keeps the Rhinos honest can bleed it out before the charge engine ever fires.
782: Built around Mortarion, Deathshroud Terminators, a Daemon Prince of Nurgle, Foetid Bloat-Drones, and a deep roster of supporting characters running Virulent Vectorium, this list plants Poxwalkers and Chaos Spawn on objectives to trigger the detachment's Afflicted condition while a slow-rolling wall of elite infantry and Defilers grinds forward. The win condition is suffocation: lock down objectives early to Afflict anything that contests them, then use Mortarion and Deathshroud as a hammer to dismantle whatever the opponent commits to clear your screening units. It absolutely punishes gunline armies that need to hold static firing positions, because those units spend most of the game Afflicted while being worn down by heavy blight launchers and Defiler firepower. The critical weakness is speed — a fast, deep-striking or hyper-mobile opponent can bypass the screen entirely, flip objectives before Afflicted triggers, and race ahead on secondaries before the slow Death Guard centre can respond.
783: Built around Plague Marines (Infiltrating forward via Flyblown Host), Nurglings, Plaguebearers, Poxwalkers, Beasts of Nurgle, Rotigus, Malignant Plaguecasters, Biologus Putrifier, and Deathshroud Terminators, this list floods the board with Nurgle bodies across both Death Guard and Plague Legions keywords, exploiting the Tallyband Summoners synergy to extend Contagion Range by 3" while granting Nurgle's Gift to Daemon units camping nearby. The win condition is layered attrition — Infiltrating Plague Marines threaten objectives from turn one while the Contagion bubble steadily degrades enemy durability, letting the horde grind opponents off midfield through sustained lethal-rate pressure rather than burst damage. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear multiple overlapping screening layers before the Contagion engine comes fully online. Fast, high-volume shooting lists that can outrange the bubble and pick apart the horde piecemeal before the screens lock down the midfield will crack this list open.
785: Built around Rotigus, Deathshroud Terminators, a Lord of Contagion, and waves of Beasts of Nurgle, Nurglings, Poxwalkers, Plaguebearers, and Chaos Spawn, this Tallyband Summoners list exploits the detachment's core synergy: Plague Legions daemons sitting within 7" of Death Guard units gain Nurgle's Gift, while Death Guard within 7" of those daemons extend their Contagion Range by 3", creating an interlocking web of attrition across the entire midboard. The win condition is drowning opponents under layered lethality — stacking Contagion Range bubbles to corrode enemy durability while bodies flood objectives and Deathshroud punch out anything that survives the grind. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot trade efficiently against the sheer volume of durable wounds and cannot escape the expanding contagion aura. Concentrated high-damage shooting or alpha-strike lists that delete key synergy pieces before the web forms can unravel the whole engine before it gets going.
787:
Built around Commander Dante, Sanguinary Guard, multiple Captains and Chaplains with jump packs, Assault Intercessors, Death Company, and Vanguard Veterans — all airborne — this is a Stormlance Task Force army that chains the advance-and-charge rule into a relentless aerial assault, with Vengeful Hosts layering hit-roll re-rolls onto every unit that ingresses or charges in the same turn.

The win condition is coordinated multi-unit charges from deep strike or rapid repositioning, crashing waves of FLY INFANTRY into priority targets each turn while Scouts and Intercessors babysit home objectives.

It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't screen effectively against multiple simultaneous airborne threats, stacking enough bodies and re-rolls to overwhelm overwatch-dependent defenses.

It cracks under pressure from armies with robust deep strike denial, high-volume shooting that strips cheap chaff screens early, or enough durable melee counterplay to absorb the charge and grind back — its hitting power is spread across many medium-strength units rather than one knockout blow.
788: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, a Captain with Jump Pack, Lemartes, Commander Dante, Bladeguard Veterans, a Sanguinary Priest, and Gladiator Lancers backed by Scout and Intercessor screens, this is a wall-to-wall jump pack assault list running the Liberator Assault Group detachment. The win condition is the charge bonus — every charging Adeptus Astartes unit gains +2 Strength and +1 Attack on melee weapons — so the list floods mid-board early, forces favourable charges across multiple units simultaneously, and lets Lemartes amplify Death Company into a blender while Gladiator Lancers handle armour at range. It punishes MSU infantry lists and anything that can't survive several high-volume, high-Strength charge phases hitting from multiple angles at once. However, elite melee armies that can weather the initial charge and fight back, or gunlines with enough volume to whittle the jump pack units before they close, can crack it open — the list lives and dies by getting the charge, and anything denying that or trading efficiently in the subsequent fight phase exposes how little it has left.
789: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs led by Lemartes, Sanguinary Priests, and a supporting core of Assault Intercessors and Bladeguard Veterans, this list runs primarily under the Liberator Assault Group detachment, which adds 2 Strength and 1 Attack to all melee weapons on any unit that charged that turn. The plan is to deliver multiple elite melee threats simultaneously — Priests buffing durability and fight-back, Lemartes supercharging Death Company, and charged Sanguinary Guard hitting at boosted stats — while Baal Predators and Intercessors hold ground and apply fire support. It punishes medium-armour infantry lists that can't absorb multiple high-Strength charging units across several fronts at once.
