Opponents who screen effectively to deny charges, or who pack enough anti-infantry firepower to strip the jump pack units before they land, can dismantle the engine before it swings.
791: Built around Death Company Dreadnoughts, Death Company Marines with jump packs, Sanguinary Guard, Lemartes, a jump pack Captain, Intercessors, and Commander Dante, this is a flying melee sledgehammer that exploits charge-triggered attack bonuses — either re-rolling wound rolls of 1 with extra attacks on the charge, or piling on Strength and Attacks simultaneously depending on detachment — to delete priority targets in a single activation. The win condition is using Lemartes to supercharge Death Company Marines into catastrophic charge turns while Sanguinary Guard and Dreadnoughts simultaneously threaten multiple flanks, overwhelming opponents who can only answer one assault vector at a time. It punishes slower melee armies and low-model-count elite lists that cannot screen charge lanes or trade attrition across multiple fronts. It cracks open against heavy shooting armies that can strip the jump pack units mid-approach before the charge lands, neutering the entire attack-bonus engine before it fires.
792: Built around Corsair Voidscarred, Prince Yriel, Corsair Voidreavers, Corsair Skyreavers, Warp Spiders, Striking Scorpions, Lhykhis, Rangers, Shroud Runners, and the Avatar of Khaine, this Eldritch Raiders list weaponizes the detachment's core rule — Anhrathe, Rangers, and Shroud Runners units can Advance and still charge — to flood the board with fast, multi-layered lethal threats from turn one. The win condition is momentum: advance screens and flankers into scoring positions while the Avatar and Voidscarred punch into priority targets, creating kill chains the opponent can't fully address in a single turn. It punishes slower, static armies that can't reposition to meet simultaneous threats from multiple angles, with layered Lethal Hits across the roster amplifying damage output even on glancing attacks. Its weakness is concentrated firepower — elite shooting lists that can delete key pieces before the advance-charge engine engages leave it exposed, and losing Prince Yriel early strips the leadership glue that keeps the assault coherent.
793: Built around Eldrad Ulthran, multiple Warlock Conclaves, individual Warlocks, a Farseer, Storm Guardians, Rangers, Warp Spiders, Howling Banshees, Fire Dragons, the Avatar of Khaine, Jain Zar, and Fuegan under the Seer Council detachment, this is a dense psychic-and-elite castle that generates a pool of Fate dice at game start to fuel its Stratagems throughout the match. The win condition is layered attrition — using Fate dice to efficiently trigger Stratagems at critical moments while Howling Banshees and Fire Dragons crack armour and elite infantry, Warp Spiders harass midfield, and Rangers anchor scoring. It punishes slower, lower-model-count lists that can't match the sheer breadth of threats across every unit slot, forcing anti-tank overload decisions at every turn. It cracks open against aggressive alpha-strike armies that can disrupt the castle's positioning before the Fate dice engine pays dividends.
794: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, and Vindicators operating under the Saga of the Great Wolf detachment, this list blends armoured firepower with elite melee infantry. The Vindicators supply mid-table anti-armour punch while the Terminators and Headtakers deliver transported shock assaults, cycling the Hunting Pack selections each Command phase to keep the entire force adaptable across the game's shifting demands. It punishes slower gunlines that struggle to screen against multi-vector threats, overloading them with Vindicator blasts and simultaneous melee pressure from Terminator bricks. Where it cracks is against hyper-mobile or deep-strike-heavy armies that can strip its infantry transports early, leaving the assault core exposed and unable to close without reliable re-roll support.
795: Built around Pathfinder Teams guiding multiple Crisis suit variants (Starscythe, Sunforge, Fireknife), Riptide Battlesuits, The Twin Lance, and Commanders in Coldstar and Enforcer frames alongside Commander Farsight, all operating under Mont'Ka — which grants [ASSAULT] on all ranged weapons for the first three battle rounds and [LETHAL HITS] to Guided units. The plan is to move-and-shoot aggressively from turn one, stacking Lethal Hits through the For the Greater Good Guided mechanism onto high-volume, multi-role Crisis platforms to delete priority targets before the opponent can stabilise their midboard. It punishes armour-heavy and elite lists badly, as the combination of mobile anti-tank output and Lethal Hits on Guided units strips expensive models faster than they can be screened. However, it struggles against armies that deny or disrupt the Guided chain early, collapsing the Lethal Hits engine and leaving its suits trading at unimpressive efficiency.
796: Built around Pathfinder Teams, Stealth Battlesuits, Ghostkeels, Vespid Stingwings, Coldstar Commanders, and Riptides operating under the Advanced Acquisition Cadre detachment, which lets Pathfinders and Stealth Battlesuits shoot without breaking hidden status — keeping key units perpetually concealed while still projecting firepower. The gameplan is to exploit that hidden-while-shooting interaction to screen forward aggressively, deny midboard space, and then flip the engine with Kauyon in rounds three through five, when Sustained Hits 1 across the army turns already-mobile anti-armour platforms into legitimate threat multipliers. This build punishes slower, heavy-armour lists that can't clear concealed units efficiently before the Kauyon window opens. It struggles against armies that can alpha-strike the exposed screening layer early, collapse hidden coherency, or out-score it on objectives before the late-game shooting surge arrives.
798: Built around Breacher Teams in Devilfish, Stealth Battlesuits, Crisis Sunforges, and a dense commander suite running both Experimental Prototype Cadre and Kauyon, this is a patience-rewarding gunline that turns into a buzzsaw after turn three. The win condition is straightforward but punishing: survive the early game with mobile screening and transport play, then detonate with army-wide Sustained Hits 1 and full modifier-ignore on Guided targets, stacking Pathfinder spotting into overwhelming late-round firepower. It punishes high-armour lists brutally — the mobile anti-armour profile of Sunforges and Coldstar Commanders with extended 6" range reaches targets other T'au builds can't touch. The hard counter is fast, high-damage aggression that forces trades before round three activates the Kauyon payoff, leaving the army's relatively fragile infantry exposed with nothing to show for it.
799: Built around Krootox Rampagers, Kroot Lone-Spears, Krootox Riders, Kroot Carnivores, Crisis Sunforge Battlesuits, The Twin Lance, Kroot Trail Shapers, Vespid Stingwings, and Kroot Farstalkers, this list pairs the Experimental Prototype Cadre's extended Battlesuit range with the Kroot Hunting Pack's conditional hit-and-wound bonuses to field an enormous, multi-layered horde. The plan is to flood every zone with cheap Kroot infantry while Rampagers and Lone-Spears crack open weakened units — the Hunting Pack bonuses trigger on targets below Starting Strength, so chipping enemies first then piling in to finish them is the core kill chain. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally, overwhelming their ability to screen or hold objectives against sheer body count while the Sunforge and Twin Lance elements handle armour. Concentrated firepower that deletes full squads before they get chipped, or fast melee threats that bypass the horde's screen, can deny the conditional bonuses and unravel the entire engine.
800: Built around Riptide Battlesuits, Sky Ray Gunships, Pathfinder Teams, Stealth Battlesuits, Ghostkeels, and the Twin Lance, this list runs the Advanced Acquisition Cadre alongside Kauyon to create a layered shooting platform that stays hidden while it spots and guides targets. The engine is a Markerlight-driven kill chain: Pathfinders and Sky Rays designate Spotted units, Kauyon's late-game Sustained Hits 1 then amplifies every guided shot from Riptides and Crisis Starscythes into a volume of high-strength fire that dismantles armoured lists. It punishes heavy-vehicle spam hard — the mobile anti-armour profile means it can efficiently strip tanks and monsters that slower lists cannot dodge. The weakness is early pressure: the payoff is rounds three through five, so aggressive alpha-strike armies or deep-strike denial builds that force scoring before Kauyon activates can leave this list outpaced on primaries.
801: Built around Riptide Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams, Sky Ray Gunships, Stealth Battlesuits, Crisis Starscythes, The Twin Lance, Piranhas, Ghostkeels, Vespid Stingwings, and an Ethereal, this is a Mont'Ka mobile fire-superiority list that floods the board with T'au Empire units across every point cost. The engine is Pathfinders marking targets so Guided units fire with Lethal Hits, while Assault on all ranged weapons across the first three battle rounds lets the entire army advance and shoot without penalty, enabling aggressive objective pressure backed by concentrated kill volume. It punishes slow, high-armour forces through anti-armour overload — multiple Riptides and Sky Rays generating Lethal Hits shred heavy vehicles and monsters before they can stabilise. Aggressive alpha-strike lists that neutralise the Markerlight-Guidance chain early, or elite screening that denies the advance lanes, cut the scoring engine off at its knees.
803: Built around Pathfinders, Stealth Battlesuits, Crisis Sunforge and Fireknife teams, Broadsides, Coldstar Commanders, Riptides, Commander Farsight, and Ghostkeels, this is a mid-to-late game mobile gunline that earns its power spike in rounds three through five when Kauyon unlocks Sustained Hits 1 across every ranged weapon and lets Guided units ignore modifiers when targeting Spotted enemies. The plan is to spend early rounds screening with Vespid Stingwings and Stealth suits, establish Spotting links through Pathfinders, then unleash a massive accuracy-and-volume swing once the detachment rule activates — stacking Crisis Sunforge melta into heavy armour while Fireknife and Broadside shooting clears mid-board. It punishes slow, durable lists by removing the saves-through-cover and modifier stacking those armies rely on to survive sustained fire. Aggressive alpha-strike builds that force decisive combat before round three arrive — or armies that screen out Spotting entirely — shut off the engine before it ever fires.
804: Built around Hammerhead Gunships, Pathfinder Teams, Stealth Battlesuits, The Twin Lance, Ghostkeels, Crisis Starscythes, Fireknifes, Riptides, Coldstar and Enforcer Commanders, Commander Farsight, and Vespid Stingwings, this is a mobile all-arms T'au force that spreads firepower across nearly every chassis in the faction. The plan is to use Pathfinders to establish Guided units early, then pour Lethal Hits-boosted tank fire and battlesuit volleys into high-value targets while Hammerheads and Riptides crack armor from range and Crisis suits threaten the mid-table. It punishes slow, heavily armored lists that cannot close distance quickly, as the combination of Railguns, plasma, and multi-threat vectors creates an anti-tank overload that forces impossible save decisions. Aggressive alpha-strike armies or lists with strong deep strike denial that can collapse the screening layer of Stealths and Ghostkeels early will disrupt the Guided network before it pays off.
807: Built around Belisarius Cawl, massed Kataphron Breachers and Destroyers, Tech-Priest Manipuli, Servitor Battleclades, and Sicarian Infiltrators flooding mid-board with Skitarii Rangers and Vanguard screening, this is a layered horde-gunline running primarily Lords of the Forge, which gives Tech-Priests a 4+ invulnerable save, Feel No Pain 5+, and the Baffling Data Screed ability to strip enemy vehicle actions. The plan is to swarm objectives with expendable bodies while Kataphrons and Cawl pump out concentrated fire from close-mid range, using Technoarcheologists and Thulia Ghuld to sustain and reposition the gun platforms. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear waves of cheap screening infantry before the Kataphron killboxes come online. It cracks open when faced with aggressive alpha-strike pressure that collapses the screening layer early, exposing the slow, expensive Kataphrons before they can fire effectively.
808: Built around double Forgefiends, Defilers, Warpsmiths, and Cultist Mob screens, this is a Daemon Engine gunline that leans on Dark Pact-fueled shooting to grind opponents off the board from range. The core engine is the Soulforged Warpack contract: Forgefiends and Defilers invoke their pact to add 1 to Wound rolls on ranged attacks, while Warpsmiths keep the machines operational and Cultists absorb punishment on forward objectives. It punishes low-armour, infantry-heavy armies that have to advance into its kill zones, where stacked Wound bonuses and volume of fire become overwhelming. Against elite melee armies that can close distance fast and tank the shooting phase, the build struggles — its Dark Pact Leadership risk and limited melee threat leave it exposed once engines are locked in combat.
809: Built around Eldrad Ulthran, multiple Warlock Conclaves, Rangers, Storm Guardians, War Walkers, Fire Dragons with Fuegan, and a spread of Farseers and Farseer Skyrunners, this Seer Council list generates a Fate dice pool at the start of the game and spends those dice to trigger detachment Stratagems at predetermined values, layering psychic buffs and lethal keyword saturation across a mass of cheap bodies. The win condition is overwhelming opponents with volume — Rangers holding ground under Path of the Outcast's detection bubble, Storm Guardians screening forward, and Fire Dragons with Fuegan delivering concentrated anti-armour kills while Fate dice guarantee the key Stratagem triggers when it matters most. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that cannot contest every corner simultaneously, drowning them in activations and lethal-stacked shooting from War Walkers and skimmer-mobile Skyrunners. It cracks under pressure from fast alpha-strike forces that can delete the psychic support characters early, collapsing the Fate dice engine before it pays out.
810: Built around Troupes mounted in Starweavers, Troupe Masters, Skyweavers, a Solitaire, Rangers, and Falcons, this list runs Armoured Warhost and Serpent's Brood to fuse skimmer firepower with disembark-fuelled melee murder. The engine is a two-phase kill chain: Starweavers shoot on the move with Assault, then Troupes disembark with Sustained Hits 1 and carve through whatever survived, letting Troupe Masters and the Solitaire clean the flanks while Rangers hold backfield objectives. It punishes static gunlines and fragile elite infantry hard, burying them under repeated layered lethality from units that threaten at range and in combat simultaneously. Anything with durable screens, high-volume anti-skimmer fire, or the reach to strip Starweavers before the disembark turn cracks this open, leaving exposed Troupe squads with nowhere to safely land.
811: Built around Wraithlords, Wraithguard, Wraithblades, Spiritseers, and usually Eldrad Ulthran and a Farseer Skyrunner, this Spirit Conclave list weaponizes its own casualties: every time a Psyker dies, the killer earns a Vengeful Dead token, and every subsequent Wraith Construct attack against that unit gains +1 to hit and +1 to wound. The plan is to deliberately bait the opponent into killing Spiritseers or Eldrad, then stack Vengeful Dead tokens and crash Wraith Constructs into the marked unit with surgical precision. It punishes lists that must engage and kill efficiently — heavy melee or elite MSU — because every kill they score on a Psyker flips a switch that makes their own unit dramatically easier to delete in return. Spread damage and Psyker-avoidant shooting crumbles the engine, since a token never generated is a token that never fuels the retaliation chain.
812: Built around massed Windriders, War Walkers, Farseer Skyrunners, Warlock Skyrunners, Shroud Runners, Warp Spiders, and the Avatar of Khaine, this Armoured Warhost list runs Windrider Host as its second detachment to hold Asuryani Mounted units in Reserves and deploy them a round earlier than normal, flooding mid-board objectives from unexpected angles. The win condition is layered attrition — Assault-enabled Vehicle shooting lets War Walkers advance and fire freely while Windrider blobs contest and score, with psykers and the Avatar providing the melee teeth to punish anything that moves up to clear them. It punishes infantry-heavy lists brutally, stacking mobile anti-armour and skimmer fire across multiple threat vectors that overload target priority. Durable elite armies with hard-hitting melee or strong anti-vehicle firepower crack it open by stripping the War Walkers early and leaving the Windrider blobs without the damage output to defend their own objectives.
813: Built around Windriders, Farseer Skyrunners, Shining Spears, Fire Prisms, and the Avatar of Khaine, with Howling Banshees and Jain Zar cracking open elite infantry alongside Warp Spiders and Shroud Runners screening the flanks — running either Warhost's Battle Focus token engine for supercharged Agile Manoeuvres or Windrider Host's early Strategic Reserves entry to flood midfield from turn one. The plan is to layer skimmer shooting from Fire Prisms and Windriders onto priority targets while the assault package of Banshees, Jain Zar, and the Avatar cleans up whatever survives, scoring through board control generated by constant high-speed repositioning. It punishes static gunlines and low-mobility armies that cannot redeploy to contest, as the combination of deep-striking mounted units and mobile anti-armour overloads their threat prioritisation. However, armies that can screen midfield effectively or deny the early Agile Manoeuvre bonuses — forcing the list into suboptimal positioning — blunt its tempo and expose how fragile the individual units are without momentum.
814: Built around the Silent King, Imotekh the Stormlord, and Ophydian Destroyers backed by an Overlord, this list runs the Obeisance Phalanx detachment, locking in a target each Command phase so Nobles, Lychguard, and Triarch units wound it more easily. The plan is to designate a priority threat — typically a tough character or vehicle — funnel multiple hard-hitting units into it with the wound bonus, and snowball off eliminated anchors to collapse the opponent's scoring engine. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that struggle to protect individual key pieces, as stacking wound bonuses on a single target overwhelms even resilient units. However, it cracks under pressure from fast, multi-threat armies that force the wound-bonus selection onto something irrelevant while the real damage comes from unexpected angles.
817: Built around Hellhounds, a Doomhammer, Scout Sentinels, Bullgryns, and Tech-Priest Enginseers supported by Lord Solar Leontus and Cadian Command Squads, this list runs Abhuman Auxiliaries and Steel Hammer to combine a mobile armoured fist with a grinding super-heavy gunline. The win condition is pushing Hellhounds and Bullgryns aggressively into midboard to contest objectives while the Doomhammer — benefiting from Steel Hammer's ability to fire into engagements without penalty — hammers anything that tries to screen or tie it up, with Enginseers keeping the vehicle core repaired and operational throughout. It punishes elite melee threats and mid-density infantry screens hard, as Bullgryns absorb punishment on the push while the Squadron rule lets titanic firepower fire freely through the scrum. Highly mobile, high-damage lists that can alpha strike the Hellhounds off the board or deny the Doomhammer clear lanes will crack it open, since losing either the mobile vanguard or the super-heavy anchor collapses the two-layer pressure the build depends on.
818: Built around Scout Sentinels, Rogal Dorn Battle Tanks, Hippogriff AFVs, Lord Solar Leontus, Kasrkin, Hellhounds, and blobs of Cadian Shock Troops supported by Gaunt's Ghosts, this is a layered gunline that uses Designation Force to spotlight priority targets, extending detection range and enabling the rest of the army's considerable firepower to punish anything trying to hide or screen behind terrain. The plan is to hold the midfield with cheap infantry waves while Dorns and Hippogriffs crack armour and Hellhounds clear screens, with Leontus and command assets coordinating order-stacking across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It punishes elite low-model-count armies through sheer volume of wounds across mixed weapon profiles — anti-armour and anti-infantry fire coming from every corner of the board. It cracks open when faced with fast, high-mobility armies that can isolate and overwhelm individual gunline elements before the designation-and-fire loop gets rolling, or drown it in bodies faster than the horde clearance tools can respond.
819: Built around Rogal Dorn Commanders, Hellhounds, Leman Russ Battle Tanks, Gaunt's Ghosts, Bullgryns, and Lord Solar Leontus operating under Grizzled Company, this is a mechanised gunline that floods the table with armour, elite infantry screens, and officer-stacked Orders that let every attacking model re-roll hit rolls of 1 while increasing the number of Orders each officer can issue. The win condition is layered attrition: Rogal Dorn Commanders and Leman Russ tanks grind through armour at range while Hellhounds flush out light infantry and Bullgryns bodyblock key pieces long enough for the gunline to dismantle threats systematically. It punishes slow, static enemy lists that cannot close distance quickly, as sustained heavy firepower with consistent hit re-rolls overwhelms low-mobility armies before they establish board presence. The list cracks under pressure from fast melee or alpha-strike builds that can punch through the infantry screens early, exposing the armour to close-range engagements where the gunline's range advantage collapses.
820: Built around multiple squads of Plaguebearers, Great Unclean Ones, Poxbringers, Beasts of Nurgle, Rotigus, Nurglings, and Sloppity Bilepipers, this is a suffocating Nurgle horde running primarily the Plague Legion detachment to blanket midfield in diseased bodies. The win condition is grinding attrition through layered lethality — forcing Battle-shock tests on anything within 9" of a Nurgle unit each Command phase while Plaguebearers and Beasts contest and hold objectives under punishment, letting the list outscore opponents who cannot efficiently clear durable, self-reinforcing chaff. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to efficiently trade into T5+ masses with high wound counts and degraded combat effectiveness from persistent Battle-shock pressure. It cracks open against high-mobility lists that can skirt the 9" aura entirely, denying Battle-shock triggers and bypassing the slow defensive bubble to cherry-pick isolated scoring units.
821: Built around Maulerfiends, Infractors, Lords Exultant, Defilers, and Tormentors — with Daemon Princes, Rhino-mounted Noise Marines, and Flawless Blades rounding out the core — this is a wall-to-wall mobile melee army running primarily the Coterie of the Conceited detachment, pledging enemy unit kills to Slaanesh each round to bank Pact points. The win condition is an aggressive mid-board collision: flood the table with fast threats, make accurate kill-count pledges to stack Pact points, and use Lords Exultant to drive the damage engine while Rhinos deliver infantry safely into the fight. It punishes slower gunlines that can't handle simultaneous multi-vector charges from durable, mobile monsters and transported infantry. Lists that can alpha-strike the Maulerfiends or screen out charges before the pledge resolves deny the Pact economy entirely, leaving this army scoring far below expectation.
823: Built around Bladeguard Veterans, Infernus Squads, Eradicators, and Adrax Agatone delivered inside a Land Raider Redeemer, with Vulkan He'stan amplifying flame weapons and multiple Librarians cycling Psychic Disciplines each round. The plan is to advance aggressively while the detachment's Assault rule lets every ranged weapon fire on the move, with the +1 Strength within 12" turning melta and flamer profiles into close-range delete buttons against any durable target. Dense infantry screens and massed mid-board MSU units punish armies that rely on light infantry blobs or low-Toughness hordes, as the short-range Strength spike shreds them efficiently before they can contest objectives. The build cracks under pressure from long-range alpha strikes and hard terrain denial — anything that keeps it beyond 12" negates its core damage bonus and forces the advance engine to fight uphill.
825: Built around Marneus Calgar escorted by Victrix Honour Guard, a wall of Repulsor Executioners, and a forward screen of Scout Squads backed by Intercessors and Bladeguard Veterans, this list runs the Gladius Task Force detachment to cycle Combat Doctrines — most critically Devastator Doctrine, which lets units shoot after Advancing and keeps the Repulsor Executioners mobile without sacrificing firepower. The plan is to flood midfield with durable infantry screens while Calgar anchors a protected firebase, using the Executioners' heavy guns to eliminate priority targets from range and grind opponents off objectives through attrition. It punishes slower, low-mobility gunlines that can't contest the midfield screen early, as the combination of Bladeguard durability and Repulsor volume fire simply outgrinds them. However, lists that can surgically remove the screening layers through deep strike or massed high-AP output leave the Executioners exposed and the whole structure collapses.
827: Built around Terminator Assault Squads (nearly two units on average), a supporting Terminator Squad, an Ancient in Terminator Armour, and Scout squads for cheap board coverage, this is a heavily armoured melee-and-gunline hybrid that floods the table with resilient, high-threat units across multiple ranges. The plan is to use Scouts to screen objectives and deny deep strike while the Terminator mass closes distance and crashes into mid-table, with the Ancient's aura keeping squads fighting through attrition. It punishes lists that lack high-volume anti-elite firepower by presenting multiple durable, high-damage threats simultaneously — an opponent who over-commits to killing one Terminator brick often loses board control to the others. However, focused mortal-wound output or mass high-AP shooting that bypasses armour saves can crack the expensive, low-model-count core before it reaches engagement range.
828: Built around Aethon Shaan, multiple Librarians in Terminator Armour, Centurion Devastators, Terminator squads, and dense infantry screens of Scouts, Incursors, and Intercessors, this Librarius Conclave list leans heavily on the Shadowmark Talon's ranged cover bubble — forcing opponents to close within 12" before their shots land cleanly — while the Psyker discipline rotation (Divination for re-rolls, Pyromancy for burst, Biomancy for repositioning) tunes the army's output each round. The win condition is Aethon's free Into Darkness Stratagem triggering once per battle round to keep Terminators and mobile elements pressing objectives while the Centurion Devastators grind from behind a virtually permanent cover save. This setup punishes mid-range gunlines hard, since the cover denial threshold forces enemies to overextend or shoot through the screen at penalty, and the sheer model count across Inceptors, Scouts, and Intercessors makes objective denial expensive to crack. Elite melee alpha-strikers who can reliably close within 12" early bypass the cover bubble entirely and expose how slowly the Terminator core repositions under pressure.
829: Built around Inceptor Squads, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Vanguard Veterans with Jump Packs, and Scout Squads backed by a core of Intercessors, this is a mobile combined-arms force that floods the table with fast infantry across multiple threat vectors. The win condition is board saturation — Inceptors deliver heavy firepower at range while jump pack units charge into objectives, forcing opponents to prioritize targets they cannot all answer simultaneously. It punishes slower gunline armies that struggle to clear multiple waves of advancing infantry, particularly lists that lack the volume of fire to handle both aerial and ground threats at once. However, it lacks a true hammer unit capable of cracking elite armor or high-toughness monsters, and any list that can efficiently concentrate lethal firepower — or screen against charges — will repeatedly blunt its momentum.
831: Built around Outrider Squads, Assault Intercessors, Bladeguard Veterans, a Librarian, and Suboden Khan, this list runs the Librarius Conclave detachment and leans heavily into a mobile close-combat brawl backed by a surprisingly dense gunline. The win condition is Psychic Discipline buffed charges — Divination's reroll-1s on hits and wounds keep the combat units reliable, while Spearpoint Task Force (present in just over half the lists) lets Outriders and Assault Intercessors charge after Advancing, turning the whole army into a threat on turn one. It punishes slower, low-model-count armies that can't screen their flanks, as multiple fast melee threats arriving simultaneously create impossible split-decision moments for the opponent. The build struggles against dense shooting that can strip the exposed cavalry and infantry before they engage, and with no single dominant enhancement or secondary detachment, its toolkit feels scattered rather than locked in.
833: Built around Intercessor Squads and Redemptor Dreadnoughts, with a significant bloc of heavy firepower from Ballistus Dreadnoughts and Heavy Intercessors backing them up, this is a static or semi-static bolter-and-cannon gunline that plants itself in terrain and grinds opponents down at range. The win condition is sustained firepower pressure — Redemptors and Ballistus Dreadnoughts do the heavy lifting against armour and elite infantry while Intercessors hold ground and score, with Lieutenants and Techmarines keeping the big walkers functional turn after turn. It punishes slow, durable armies that want to walk into its guns, converting multi-turn shooting into attrition advantage against lists that cannot avoid the engagement. However, anything with strong alpha-strike capability, deep strike threats, or fast melee access can bypass the gunline entirely and crack it open before it establishes optimal positioning — this build gives ground poorly and struggles to reclaim objectives once displaced.
834: Built around Librarians (including one in Terminator armour), Outrider Squads, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Terminator Assault Squads, Sternguard Veterans, Land Speeders, Scout Squads, Kor'sarro Khan, Suboden Khan, and Intercessors, this is a Librarius Conclave list that uses the Spearpoint Task Force detachment to let units charge after Advancing or Falling Back, creating relentless multi-wave pressure. The Librarians rotate Psychic Disciplines each battle round — cycling Biomancy for movement, Divination for reroll stacking, or Pyromancy for firepower — while Suboden Khan repositions 6" after wiping a unit in melee, chaining kills across the board. It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't peel fast-moving assault threats off multiple objectives simultaneously. Armies with strong overwatch, high-AP shooting, or deep strike denial tools can pick apart the advance before the charge-after-Advance engine comes online.
835: Built around Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes, Scout Squads, and Intercessor Squads, this list floods the board with fast, skimmer-based firepower backed by cheap infantry holding ground. The plan is to park Hammerstrikes and Speeders in dominant firing positions while scouts and intercessors sit on objectives, using mobile anti-armour output to strip heavy targets and skimmer movement to reposition threat after threat. It punishes gunline armies and armour-heavy lists that cannot force it off advantageous angles, as the sheer volume of mobile anti-tank overloads static defensive screens. However, it struggles against aggressive melee alpha strikes that can reach the speeder platforms early, since the infantry core lacks the raw durability to absorb a hard punch and protect the skimmers simultaneously.
836: Built around the Emperor's Champion, High Marshal Helbrecht, Sword Brethren, Repulsor Executioners, and a Land Raider Redeemer, this is a terrain-hugging gunline that keeps elite infantry and armour planted inside cover from turn one. The Ceramite Sentinels detachment rewards staying put — units entrenched in terrain re-roll hit and wound rolls of 1, so Repulsor Executioners and the Execrator blast at full efficiency while Sword Brethren and Bladeguard hold the line in melee. It punishes mobile mid-range lists hard: anything forced to walk into the guns eats re-rolled shooting from armour that's also difficult to shift out of fortified positions. The weakness is alpha-strike or deep-strike pressure that forces units off terrain early, stripping the Entrenched keyword and collapsing the re-roll engine before it can grind the opponent down.
837: Built around Sword Brethren Squads (with +1 OC from Marshal's Household), Repulsor Executioners, Marshals, Helbrecht, the Emperor's Champion, Chaplain Grimaldus, Castellans, and Crusader and Scout screens, this list blends a dense infantry horde with a heavy skimmer gunline. The win condition is controlling objectives through sheer body count and elevated OC on Sword Brethren while Repulsor Executioners hammer priority targets from range, with Helbrecht and the Emperor's Champion threatening lethal melee follow-up. It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't clear the volume of infantry quickly enough to contest objectives before the OC advantage locks scoring. However, elite alpha-strike lists that can strip the Repulsors early and precision-delete the Sword Brethren undercut both the firepower engine and the OC swing simultaneously.
838: Built around Terminator Assault Squads, Wolf Guard Terminators, Arjac Rockfist, Logan Grimnar, and Bjorn the Fell-Handed, this is a heavily armoured melee freight train operating under Saga of the Beastslayer, which grants Lethal Hits against Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles across the entire army. The win condition is smashing into the midboard with multiple terminator units, using Lethal Hits to efficiently strip enemy elites and heavy targets while accumulating kills toward the Beastslayer tally for army-wide Lethal Hits on everything. It punishes lists built around expensive Characters, Monsters, or Vehicles — precisely the targets where Lethal Hits compounds the most damage output — and Logan Grimnar provides mobile command flexibility to redirect threat vectors. Heavy shooting lists that can weather the advance and delete terminators before they close distance will crack this open, since the build lacks durable long-range answer units to trade back efficiently.
839: Built around multiple squads of Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Terminator Assault Squad, Arjac Rockfist, and Bjorn the Fell-Handed, this Saga of the Great Wolf list is a wall of terminator armour crashing into the midboard. The plan is to use the Hunting Pack system — especially Encircling Jaws' re-roll Advance and Charge rolls — to deliver multiple terminator units into combat simultaneously, generating kill chain pressure across several objectives at once rather than committing to a single point. It punishes slower, durable elite lists that lack the volume of attacks to chew through repeated waves of 2+ save bodies before the terminators rip their scoring pieces apart. Fast, high-damage melee threats that can reach terminators before they engage — and armies with enough anti-tank overload to strip Bjorn and any Land Raider support early — can blunt the charge timing this list depends on.
840: Built around Thunderwolf Cavalry, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, and Wulfen with Storm Shields, this Stormlance Task Force list plays a relentless mid-table brawl, using the detachment's ability to charge after Advancing or Falling Back to keep elite melee units constantly threatening. The gameplan is to crash multiple hard-hitting hammers into the opponent's midfield simultaneously, denying them safe scoring positions while Logan and Arjac stack into Terminator blobs to grind out kills in the fight phase. It punishes elite low-model-count lists that can't absorb repeated charges from Thunderwolves and shielded Wulfen across consecutive turns. However, high-volume shooting that picks apart the cavalry before they reach combat, or fast-moving screens that collapse the charging lanes, exposes how much the engine depends on actually making contact.
841: Built around Thunderwolf Cavalry, Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, and Ragnar Blackmane, this is a hero-hammer brawler running Saga of the Beastslayer, which grants Lethal Hits to all attacks targeting Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles. The plan is to crash a wall of elite melee threats into the opponent's key pieces — named characters and heavy support units — converting hits into wounds efficiently enough to trade up on premium targets while Thunderwolves threaten midboard objectives. It punishes elite armies leaning on Characters, Monsters, or Vehicles as their win condition, since Lethal Hits across the entire roster turns every combat into a threat multiplication problem for those lists. However, against horde infantry or armies that can screen out the melee core and force piecemeal engagements, the list's below-average win rate suggests the brawler toolkit struggles to find clean charges and score consistently.
842: Built around Trygons, Raveners, Hyperadapted Raveners, The Red Terror, Lictors, Neurolictors, Zoanthropes, Biovores, Neurotyrant, The Swarmlord, Hormagaunts, and Maleceptor, this is a Subterranean Assault list that floods the board from underground, with Trygons (frequently upgraded to Trygon Prime characters) and Burrower-keyword units emerging mid-game to collapse opponent positioning. The win condition is board-state suffocation — Lictors and Neurolictors pre-position to deny deep strike and screen flanks while Ravener waves crash into the midfield, forcing the opponent to fight on multiple fronts simultaneously rather than contesting objectives cleanly. It punishes static gunlines and elite low-model-count armies that cannot absorb the volume of bodies arriving from unexpected vectors each turn. It cracks open against fast, high-damage lists that can destroy emerging units before they activate, erasing the tempo advantage that subterranean arrival is designed to create.
843: Built around Norn Emissaries, Maleceptors, Neurotyrant, Tyrannofex, Norn Assimilator, Exocrine, and Biovores operating under Synaptic Nexus, this is a flexible combined-arms swarm that rotates Synaptic Imperatives each round to shift between offensive, defensive, and utility modes as the game demands. The win condition is accumulating points through multi-threat pressure — heavy ranged platforms like the Tyrannofex and Exocrine strip armour while Norn Emissaries and Assimilators threaten melee, forcing opponents to split attention rather than focus down one axis. This broad toolkit punishes lists that are optimised against a single threat type, since no one counter fully neutralises the roster's range of delivery mechanisms. Its weakness is consistency: cycling Imperatives and coordinating synapse bubbles creates mechanical overhead, and focused, fast armies that collapse the synapse network early leave the swarm fragmented and underperforming.
844: Built around Norn Emissaries and Norn Assimilators carrying Protean Purpose under Talons of the Norn Queen, supported by Maleceptors, Neurolictor screens, Biovores, Pyrovores, and a Hive Tyrant, this is a flexible, toolbox-heavy swarm that morphs its threat profile each game. The win condition is dictated threat saturation — Protean Purpose lets the Norns adapt their role on the fly, while Biovore indirect fire forces opponents off objectives and Neurolictor harassment disrupts key positioning. It punishes static gunlines that can't reposition, overwhelming them with mobile multi-vector pressure that no single defensive formation can fully address. Its weakness is elite close-combat armies that can isolate and delete Norns before Protean Purpose pays dividends, cracking open the list's identity unit before the threat web is established.
845: Built around Beast Snagga Boyz, Squighog Boyz, Beastboss, Painboy, Boyz, Gretchin, Ghazghkull Thraka, Wazdakka Gutsmek, and Kommandos, this is a thundering mid-board melee horde running Equatorial Hordes for Scouts 6" on key MOB units and Freebooter Krew's Sustained Hits 1 across virtually every model in the army. The plan is to flood the midfield on turn one with screened Beast Snagga blobs backed by Ghazghkull's aura, then bury opponents under sheer attack volume amplified by Sustained Hits 1 while holding the loot objective for consistent Command phase pressure. It brutally punishes elite low-model-count lists that can't absorb the raw number of Sustained Hits attacks pouring out of multiple full hordes simultaneously. Armies with strong shooting that can pick apart blobs before they make contact, or anything with durable screens that denies the initial charge, will erode the momentum this build depends on.
846: Built around Scarab Occult Terminators led by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Sekhetar Robots buffed by Psyker auras, and a deep horde of Tzaangors, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, and Rubric Marines, this list plays a dense, layered mid-table game with Ahriman directing the psychic engine. The plan is to flood the midfield with bodies across multiple unit types, using Psyker Infusion auras to push Robots into melee and Rituals to sustain key characters through the Ritual of Regeneration, generating attrition advantage while contesting every objective simultaneously. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that cannot clear the sheer volume of threats without being overextended, as each wave removed simply exposes another. It cracks open against high-volume mortal wound output or anti-horde shooting that collapses multiple cheap screens before the Terminator hammer can close.
847: Built around Chaos Terminators (averaging over two squads), Jakhals, a Daemon Prince of Khorne, Khorne Berzerkers, and Exalted Eightbound, this is a mass-horde melee army running Butchers of Khorne — a detachment that generates an additional Blessing of Khorne at the start of the Fight phase whenever an engaged Terminator squad triggers the Blessings of Khorne roll. The plan is to flood mid-table with bodies early, use Jakhals as cheap screening fodder to protect the kill-pieces, then crash Terminators and Exalted Eightbound into the enemy's front line and stack Fight-phase buffs to shred whatever they contact. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb the sheer volume of attacks across multiple horde waves hitting simultaneously. However, armies that can reliably shoot off the Terminator squads before the Fight phase fires — or deny the charge with deep-strike denial and long-range firepower — shut down the core engine and leave the list without its buff-generation.
848: Built around Breacher Teams riding Devilfish, Pathfinders marking targets, Cadre Fireblades stacking volume fire, Riptides and Broadsides providing heavy punch, and Stealth Battlesuits and Piranhas running interference, this is a mobile firing line that floods the board with bodies and guns simultaneously. The engine is Mont'Ka's Assault keyword on all ranged weapons for the first three rounds combined with Lethal Hits on Guided units — Pathfinders mark a priority target, Breachers disembark and unload at close range with Lethal Hits converting wounds directly, while Riptides and Broadsides delete armour in the same activation window. It punishes infantry-heavy and medium-armour lists brutally, as the combination of mass Assault shots and Lethal Hits on Guided units overwhelms saves through sheer conversion efficiency. However, elite melee armies that can close fast and wreck the Devilfish transports strand the Breachers in the open and collapse the entire kill chain.
850: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Krootox Rampagers, Vespid Stingwings, Crisis Fireknives, Kroot Carnivores, Riptides, Ghostkeels, and twin Commanders, this is a hybrid Kroot-and-battlesuit force running Auxiliary Cadre alongside Kauyon that uses the Kroot's hidden status to screen and contest while its battlesuits ramp into a late-game ranged crescendo. The win condition is patience: hold the midboard with expendable Kroot bodies and Rampager brawlers, then detonate Kauyon's Sustained Hits 1 and ignore-modifier rules in rounds three through five to obliterate armour with Riptides, Broadsides, and Fireknives. It punishes slow, high-armour lists that struggle to clear cheap screens before the Kauyon window opens, leaving hard-hitting suits free to operate. Aggressive alpha-strike armies that can collapse the Kroot screen in rounds one or two deny the Kauyon payoff entirely, leaving the ranged engine exposed before it can fire at full effect.
851: Built around krootox riders, krootox rampagers, kroot carnivores, kroot lone-spears, kroot hounds, kroot farstalkers, kroot war shapers, kroot flesh shapers, vespid stingwings, and kroot trail shapers, this is a mass-horde brawler that floods the board with cheap Kroot bodies and hammers home with heavy cavalry. The win condition is attrition through volume — weathering return fire with expendable screens while the detachment's hit-and-wound bonus triggers against depleted units, turning already-damaged squads into easy kills that cascade across the game. It punishes elite low-model-count armies hardest, since opponents constantly sitting below Starting Strength or Below Half-strength hand this list permanent offensive upgrades on nearly every attack. Armies that can delete entire squads in one activation before those units get to fight back, or that project enough ranged lethality to prevent the brawl from ever closing, can deny the Below Half-strength trigger and leave Kroot punching without their teeth.
852: Built around Obliterators, Chaos Terminator Squads, Cultist Mob, Kravek Morne, Sorcerer in Terminator Armour, and Mutilators, this list runs Devotees of Destruction to give Obliterators and Havocs the Heavy keyword, with most lists also taking Warpstrike Champions to redeploy Terminators, Obliterators, and Mutilators at the end of the opponent's turn. However, high-volume mortal wound output or armies that can alpha-strike the Terminator blobs before Warpstrike Champions fires will shred the expensive core before the redeployment engine ever pays off.
853: Built around Defilers, Venomcrawlers, and Warpsmiths supported by Vashtorr the Arkifane, Cultist Mobs, Warp Talons, Chaos Bikers, and a jump-pack Lord, this list runs Soulforged Warpack's Dark Pact engine to supercharge its Daemon Vehicles — invoking contracts to gain +1 to wound on ranged attacks — while Murdertalon Raiders' Warp Talons punish weakened or battle-shocked units with re-rolled hit rolls and impose -1 to hit on return fire. The plan is to grind opposing armour off the board through layered vehicle shooting and Dark Pact-boosted wound rolls, using Cultist screens and mobile infantry to contest objectives while the engines do the killing. High-volume, low-AP shooting that targets vehicles before Dark Pacts resolve — combined with clearing the cheap screens early — exposes how dependent this list is on keeping its engines alive long enough to fire.
854: Built around Venoms, Raiders, Ravagers, Incubi, Wyches, Scourges, Mandrakes, Lady Malys, Drazhar, and the Archon corps running Exhibition Of Slaughter, this is a mass-skimmer horde list that floods the board with cheap transports and infantry across multiple layers. The win condition is disembark-and-delete: Incubi and Wyches pile out of Venoms and Raiders with Lethal Hits on every melee attack against non-vehicles, while Ravagers and Scourges punish anything armoured from range, and Mandrakes threaten objectives from unexpected angles. It punishes mid-range infantry-heavy armies badly — the sheer volume of Lethal Hit melee pressure combined with skimmer mobility means clustered foot lists get dismantled piecemeal before they can consolidate. However, anything that can crack transports at range before the disembark payoff triggers — heavy anti-tank overload or long-range blast spam — shuts the engine down, leaving expensive melee units stranded with no delivery.
855: Built around Archons leading Kabalite Warriors and Incubi packed into Venoms and Raiders, with Ravagers, Scourges, and Lelith Hesperax alongside Drazhar and Lady Malys providing command support, this list runs Kabalite Agonysts giving all Kabal and Blades for Hire ranged attacks Sustained Hits 1 against non-Monster/Vehicle targets, layered with Skysplinter Assault so disembarking units punch through cover and hit melee with Lance. The plan is to surge transports forward, dump infantry out with Ignores Cover shooting and Lance melee, then saturate mid-board objectives with a mass of Sustained Hits bodies while Ravagers and Scourges handle hard targets from range. It punishes infantry-heavy armies brutally — Sustained Hits 1 across multiple units stacks into overwhelming volume against foot lists with no place to hide. It cracks when opponents force it to fight from static positions or strip transports early, since the whole engine collapses without the disembark trigger.
856: Built around Spiritseers, Wraithguard, Wraithblades, and Wraithlords, this list plays a dense wall of Wraith Constructs guided by Asuryani Psykers whose deaths become fuel — when enemy units destroy a Psyker, they earn Vengeful Dead tokens that cause every subsequent Wraith attack against them to hit and wound on improved rolls. The plan is to bait or absorb Psyker losses, then redirect the buffed Wraith Constructs into the offending unit to grind it off objectives through layered, punishing close-range pressure. Vehicle units attacking with Assault across the board keep the force mobile and threatening even while pushing into mid-board, punishing static gunlines that can't reposition away from the Wraith tide. Aggressive alpha-strike lists that kill the Psykers too fast and too spread out prevent tokens from concentrating, and elite melee that simply outfights Wraithblades in a straight trade can collapse the close-range anchor before the token engine kicks in.
857: Built around Spiritseers, Wraithguard, Wraithlords, Wraithblades, Eldrad Ulthran, Rangers, and the Avatar of Khaine, this list leans on the Spirit Conclave's Vengeful Dead engine — baiting the opponent into killing Asuryani Psykers, then unleashing Wraith Constructs with stacked +1 to hit and wound against marked targets. The plan is to force efficient trades: sacrifice Spiritseers to charge up Vengeful Dead tokens, then deliver Wraithguard and Wraithblades into priority targets with dramatically improved kill probability while Wraithlords apply long-range layered pressure. Rangers and Shroud Runners provide screen-and-deny utility with extended detection range, keeping enemy infiltrators honest. The list cracks open against aggressive alpha-strike armies that can delete Wraith Constructs before tokens are spent, and struggles when opponents refuse to kill Psykers in the desired order, starving the wound-buff engine entirely.
858: Built around the Nightbringer, Void Dragon, Deceiver, and Transcendent C'tan alongside Flayed Ones and Ophydian Destroyers, this list fields a murderer's row of near-unkillable demigods backed by elite melee infiltrators. The plan is to flood the mid-table with Flayed Ones and Ophydian Destroyers applying relentless close-range pressure while the C'tan constellation bulldozes whatever threatens to hold ground, converting raw combat power into primary and secondary scoring simultaneously. It punishes armies built around elite, high-value targets by overloading threat saturation — no opponent can remove four C'tan-tier pieces in the same turn, making efficient sequenced killing nearly impossible. It cracks against armies with hard board presence early enough to deny the infiltrators their positioning, or high-volume chip damage that grinds the C'tan down before they can deliver.
859: Built around Lord Kakophonists leading Noise Marines and Infractors forward in Rhinos, supported by Lord Exultants, Tormentors, Daemon Princes, Flawless Blades, Lucius, and Defilers, this is a transport-heavy infantry hammer running Coterie of the Conceited — the detachment that rewards you with Pact points each round you hit or exceed your own kill pledge. It punishes horde armies and infantry-dense lists that offer easy pledge targets, letting the kill-counting engine run at full efficiency. However, it struggles when facing elite low-model-count forces that deny easy pledge fulfillment, stalling the Pact economy and leaving this list without its core payoff.
861: Built around Land Raider Redeemers carrying Bladeguard Veterans and Intercessors, a brace of Librarians running Librarius Conclave disciplines, Vulkan He'stan, Adrax Agatone, and Scout and Lieutenant support, this is a heavy short-range gunline that delivers elite infantry by transport into the mid-board. Armies with strong anti-tank overload or long-range shooting can strip the transports before they deliver, leaving elite but slow infantry stranded in the open.
862: Built around Marneus Calgar, Captain Titus, Bladeguard Veterans, Wardens of Ultramar, Vanguard Veterans with jump packs, Victrix Honour Guard, Intercessors, and Scout screens operating under the Reclamation Force detachment, this list blends a durable melee core with ranged gunline pressure. It punishes static elite armies that park on objectives, using stacked AP improvement to crack armour saves that would otherwise hold. Aggressive mobile forces that contest objectives before you establish control, particularly anything that can strip your objective grip in the command phase, expose how many pieces this list needs to function simultaneously.
863: Built around Darnath Lysander, multiple Terminator Assault and Terminator Squads, Librarians in Terminator Armour, and an Ancient in Terminator Armour, this is a dense, armoured-infantry list running Emperor's Shield with Librarius Conclave support in seven-in-ten lists. The win condition is grinding through Oath of Moment targets with full wound re-rolls on Lysander and wound-roll-of-1 re-rolls across the wider army, while the Ancient sustains the blob's durability and Librarius Conclave layers in Divination or Biomancy turn-by-turn to shift between threat projection and mobility. 864: Built around Repulsor Executioners, Execrators, Sword Brethren, Crusader Squads, the Emperor's Champion, Castellans, and Scout Squads, this is a Companions of Vehemence gunline that floods the board with re-rollable Advance and Charge rolls to keep pressure on objectives while heavy skimmer fire does the real damage. It punishes slower, lower-model-count armies that can't match the sheer volume of bodies and firepower, overwhelming them before they stabilize their objective game. 865: Built around Armiger Helverins and Armiger Warglaives as the chassis core, this list floods the table with cheap Knight bodies supported by Skitarii Rangers screening objectives roughly half the time, with the Questor Forgepact detachment stitching wounds back onto damaged Knights each Command phase. 866: Built around the Neurotyrant, Norn Emissaries, Screamer-Killers, Maleceptors, Neurolictors, and Deathleaper operating under Synaptic Nexus Synaptic Imperatives, this is a mobile, psyker-heavy swarm that pressures the entire board through fast, multi-threat positioning. 867: Built around Genestealers, Broodlords, Neurolictor, Lictors, Raveners, Hyperadapted Raveners, Von Ryan's Leapers, and Hormagaunts flooding every angle, this is a pure Vanguard Onslaught swarm that uses Deathleaper as its Warlord — freed from the Hunter Organism restriction — to anchor an aggressive multi-threat infiltration package. It punishes slow, low-model-count armies that can't clear multiple independent threats per turn, particularly grinding down elite lists through sheer layered lethality and objective denial. It cracks open against armies that can alpha-strike key pieces off the table before engagement, or that hold enough efficient board-wide shooting to thin the swarm before it can pile into melee range.
868: Built around Neurolictors, Lictors, Psychophages, Von Ryan's Leapers, Pyrovores, Haruspex, Hive Tyrant, Neurotyrant, and Biovores operating under Ambush Predators, this list floods the board with Deep Striking assassin-class units that materialize wherever the opponent is most vulnerable. It punishes elite, character-heavy lists that can't screen every angle, as the Deep Strike pressure forces poor positioning decisions and opens kill lanes. 869: Built around Rubric Marines, Exalted Sorcerers, Tzaangors, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, Sekhetar Robots, Scarab Occult Terminators, Mutalith Vortex Beasts, and Tzaangor Shamans, this list floods the board with layered infantry waves running the Ritual Of Regeneration detachment, which heals Psyker units D3 wounds each time they successfully manifest a Ritual — making the caster core nearly impossible to grind out. 870: Built around Chaos Terminators, Exalted Eightbound, Daemon Prince of Khorne, Goremongers, and Slaughterbound, all operating under Vessels of Wrath, with Jakhals and Chaos Rhinos providing cheap bodies and transport capacity to push the brawlers upfield. It cracks apart against fast armies that can dictate engagement range, strip the Jakhal screens efficiently, and kite the slow core before it ever gets its fights off.
871: Built around Celestian Sacresants, Hospitaller support, Immolators, Paragon Warsuits, Seraphim, Zephyrim, and a dense command structure of Morvenn Vahl, Canonesses, and Junith Eruita, this is a mobile infantry swarm that floods the board from transports and the air. 873: Built around Doomsday Arks, Canoptek Wraiths, Skorpekh Destroyers led by a Skorpekh Lord, Technomancers, Canoptek Reanimators, Flayed Ones, Necron Warriors, Hexmark Destroyers, and Imotekh the Stormlord, all operating under Awakened Dynasty — whose CHARACTER-led units add 1 to every Hit roll. 874: Built around Beasts of Nurgle, Rotigus, Great Unclean Ones, Nurglings, Poxwalkers, Deathshroud Terminators, a Lord of Contagion, Plaguebearers, and Defilers, this list runs Paragons of Putrescence alongside Tallyband Summoners to stack Contagion Range extensions from both detachments simultaneously, pushing the debuff aura to maximum reach across the entire mid-table. It punishes armies relying on clustered mid-board infantry and tightly grouped support characters, where the Contagion overlap becomes almost impossible to escape. It struggles against fast, spread-out forces that can isolate individual aura nodes before the Contagion bubble fully overlaps, cracking the synergy before it matures.
875: Built around Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Foetid Bloat-Drones, Deathshroud Terminators, Lord of Contagion, Lord of Virulence, and Poxwalker screens, this is a mid-range attrition machine that layers Contagion across the board to tag enemies as Afflicted, then punishes that status with mortal wound triggers and elite melee pressure. It punishes durable infantry and monster-heavy lists that park on objectives, since those multi-wound units accumulate Affliction tokens and bleed mortals every command phase while struggling to remove tanky Death Guard bodies. Highly mobile, elite, single-unit armies — particularly those that avoid combat and pick apart the advance from range — crack it open before Contagion can spread far enough to matter.
876: Built around Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Foetid Bloat-Drones, Plagueburst Crawlers, and Poxwalker screens, supported by Deathshroud Terminators, Lord of Virulence, Lord of Contagion, Tallyman, and Plague Marines across Mortarion's Hammer and Paragons of Putrescence detachments. It punishes durable multi-wound infantry and medium armour lists that clump or advance slowly, where layered lethality and persistent Contagion pressure compound into unavoidable attrition. Faster aggro armies that can collapse your Poxwalker screens early and deny Contagion range — forcing Characters into the open before Deathshroud can protect them — crack this list wide open.
877: Built around Purestrain Genestealers, Patriarch, Benefictus, Reductus Saboteurs, massed Acolyte and Neophyte bodies, Atalan Jackals, and Achilles Ridgerunners, this is a sprawling horde that floods every quadrant of the board from turn one. The Purestrain Broodswarm detachment's ability to pull unengaged Purestrains into strategic reserves at the end of the opponent's Fight phase turns the cult's signature melee hammer into a near-unkillable threat that can be recycled repeatedly, while Ridgerunners and Reductus Saboteurs provide mobile anti-armour pressure across the mid-table. It punishes elite low-model-count armies through sheer volume of bodies — screens die to replace screens, and the Purestrains keep threatening re-engagement every cycle. Blast weapons and high-volume mortal output that can delete units wholesale before the Fight phase triggger crack this list open, since it relies on survival long enough to exploit the reserve bounce.
878: Built around multiple Librarians (including a Terminator-armoured variant), Azrael, Inner Circle Companions, Deathwing Knights, Sternguard, and Hellblasters, this list runs the Librarius Conclave to pulse a chosen Psychic Discipline across every psyker each round — Divination for re-rolls into hard targets, Pyromancy for volume damage, Biomancy to reposition.
