It excels against slow, heavy-armour lists that can't contest the buff rotation before the shooting dismantles them piece by piece. Armies that apply early pressure across multiple flanks crack it open, forcing suboptimal discipline choices and exposing how expensive and relatively immobile the core is.
879: Built around Venomcrawlers, Forgefiends, Defilers, Obliterators, and Vashtorr the Arkifane, this is a daemon-engine heavy list running Devotees of Destruction to give Obliterators and Havocs the Heavy keyword, supplemented in roughly three-quarters of lists by the Soulforged Warpack detachment to supercharge Dark Pact activations on Heretic Astartes Daemon Vehicles — boosting wound rolls on ranged attacks and raw melee Attacks in the same phase. The plan is to apply layered anti-armour pressure from multiple angles simultaneously: Forgefiends and Obliterators grind out shooting while Venomcrawlers and Defilers crash into the mid-board, forcing opponents to answer threats from every direction or bleed secondaries. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb multi-vector daemon engine aggression or trade efficiently into vehicles. It cracks under elite shooting armies that can delete engines before Dark Pacts fire, as Cultist chaff and loose screening leave daemon vehicles exposed to alpha-strike overload.
880: Built around Possessed in double-plus squads and a screen of Cultist Mobs, this list runs a dual-detachment shell pairing Cabal of Chaos with Fellhammer Siege-host to combine offensive Dark Pact buffs with a durable defensive layer that subtracts 1 from wound rolls whenever attackers outstrip the unit's Toughness. The plan is to flood mid-board with bodies, use Cultists as a cheap denial wall, then crash Possessed into whatever survives — soaking damage through Fellhammer's wound-roll suppression while Cabal of Chaos supercharges Psyker shooting and Daemon Prince melee output via Dark Pacts. It punishes shooting-heavy armies that rely on high-Strength, low-volume anti-infantry fire, since Fellhammer makes those wounds statistically fail more often against the mass. Armies that bypass the wound-roll reduction through volume of low-Strength attacks, or that pressure multiple flanks simultaneously, can stretch the horde thin and collapse the objective hold before Possessed reach combat range.
881: Built around Legionaries and Chosen delivered in Rhinos, Chaos Lords empowering melee, Cultist Mobs screening objectives, and a heavy armoured core of Defilers, Predator Destructors, and Chaos Bikers, all running Pactbound Zealots for Lethal Hits on unmodified 5s in melee. The plan is to grind mid-board with Lethal Hits-boosted infantry while the Predator Destructors and Defilers punish anything with an armour value from range, layering mobile anti-armour firepower over an objective-squatting cultist base. This build punishes slow, infantry-heavy gunlines that cannot reposition away from the advancing Rhino transports and bikers threatening multiple angles simultaneously. It cracks open badly against elite armies that can ignore the cultist screen and delete the armoured vehicles before the melee infantry make contact, stripping both its scoring base and its damage engine in one sweep.
882: Built around Cultist Mobs, Noise Marines, Chosen, Legionaries, and Huron Blackheart leading a Masters of the Maelstrom command staff, all riding Chaos Rhinos forward, this is a mass-horde gunline that floods every corner of the board with cheap bodies and mid-range firepower. The plan is to saturate objectives with expendable Cultist screens while Noise Marines and Legionaries pour high-volume shooting into whatever the opponent needs to keep alive, using Rhinos to deliver Chosen and other elites directly into contested midfield fights. It punishes low-model-count lists badly — the sheer number of activations overwhelms armies that rely on precise sequencing or thin screens to protect key assets. It cracks against elite close-combat armies that can punch through the Cultist chaff quickly and reach the fragile firepower units before they cycle through enough shooting to matter.
883: Built around Drazhar, Incubi, Lady Malys, Skyweavers, Solitaire, Troupes, Cronos, Scourges, Ravagers, and a full skimmer fleet of Venoms and Raiders, this is a Reaper's Wager list that fuses Drukhari and Harlequins into a single layered-lethality engine. The win condition is chaining kills to maintain wager advantage, then crashing Incubi and elite melee threats off transports into softened targets while Ravagers and Scourges strip armour from range. It punishes slower, durable armies that can't cover multiple threat vectors simultaneously — the combination of skimmer mobility, massed bodies, and precise melee delivery overwhelms lists that rely on positional attrition. However, anything that can crack the transports early or weather the initial kill chain breaks the wager loop and leaves the relatively fragile infantry exposed with no recovery mechanism.
884: Built around Skorpekh Lords, Skorpekh Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, the Nightbringer, the Void Dragon, and Nekrosor Ammentar under Cursed Legion, this is a multi-vector assault force that floods every approach with Destroyer Cult muscle backed by C'tan anchor pieces. The Cursed Legion ability stacks Strength on Destroyer Cult weapons — and escalates further when a unit kills or cripples something — so the plan is to chain kills each turn, converting early contacts into snowballing melee lethality while the C'tan soak return fire and hold ground. It punishes slower, tankier lists by overwhelming their durability with high-Strength melee spam across multiple independent threat vectors simultaneously. Tight, elite combat armies that can alpha-strike key Destroyer units before the kill chain ignites, or shooting lists that can isolate and delete C'tan before they stabilize the line, will crack this build open.
885: Built around Immortals and Necron Warriors led by characters under Awakened Dynasty — adding 1 to every Hit roll while a Character leads — and backed by Imotekh, the Nightbringer, Skorpekh Lord, Plasmancers, Royal Wardens, Technomancers, Canoptek Reanimators, and Lokhust Heavy Destroyers. The plan is to grind opponents off objectives through layered reanimation sustained by Reanimators and Technomancers while the Nightbringer and Lokhust Heavy Destroyers provide a credible kill threat that forces opponents to react rather than simply race for points. The boosted Hit rolls across multiple infantry blobs punish medium-armour armies that can't efficiently clear tough, self-repairing blobs before the score gap opens. However, dedicated alpha-strike lists and high-volume high-AP shooting can crack the reanimation loop before it stabilises, and the build's below-par win rate suggests it struggles to close games against top-tier elite armies.
886: Built around Immortals, Necron Warriors, Plasmancers, Flayed Ones, and Overlords, this list weaponizes the Hand Of The Dynasty detachment's core perk — giving Immortals and Warriors the Assault rule so they can advance and still shoot at full effect, keeping pace with objectives without sacrificing firepower. The win condition is layered board control: advance-and-shoot infantry blocs grind out primary while Flayed Ones pressure flanks, with Hypercrypt Legion's end-of-turn teleport (in over half of lists) repositioning units to contest or deny late. It punishes slow, static gunlines that struggle to shift massed reanimating bodies across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It cracks under pressure from elite alpha-strike armies that can delete infantry blocs before Reanimation Protocols trigger, since the build lacks concentrated heavy hitting to deter aggressive early engagement.
888: Built around Doomsday Arks, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Skorpekh Destroyers, Flayed Ones, a Skorpekh Lord, and Ophydian Destroyers under the Cursed Legion detachment, this list pairs long-range heavy firepower with a feral melee strike force. The Cursed Legion's Strength buff stacks onto Destroyer Cult units mid-turn, so the kill chain runs: Arks and Lokhust soften or kill a target to trigger the bonus, then boosted Skorpekh and Ophydian Destroyers crash in to finish whatever survives. It punishes slower, durable armies that expect to weather one phase at a time, since the escalating Strength values let the melee wave crack targets that should have been safe. However, aggressive alpha-strike lists that can eliminate the Destroyer Cult units before the combo fires, or screens that deny the melee ingress lanes, will dismantle the engine before it ever triggers.
889: Built around the Nightbringer, Void Dragon, Deceiver, Flayed Ones, and Tomb Blades operating under Hypercrypt Legion, this is a maximum-mobility threat-stack army that floods the board with elite bodies that teleport in and out of danger every single turn. The engine is relentless positional pressure: Hypercrypt's end-of-turn repositioning keeps C'tan and Flayed Ones perpetually threatening objectives and assassinations, while Tomb Blades arrive via deep strike with boosted accuracy through Skyshroud Spearhead to clean up wherever the C'tan soften targets. It punishes armies that rely on static defensive positioning or fragile elite screens, since no single threat vector can be neutralised without leaving another angle completely exposed. It cracks against armies that can alpha-strike one or more C'tan before Hypercrypt saves them, collapsing the threat density the entire plan depends on.
890: Built around Lokhust Lords buffing Lokhust Destroyers and Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers as a melee threat, Nekrosor Ammentar as a force multiplier, and Canoptek Reanimators keeping the killing units alive, with the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon as a durable mid-table anchor. The list wins by pushing Destroyer firepower into contested objectives — roughly a third of lists run Starshatter Arsenal to add +1 to hit on objectives and grant Assault to vehicle and mounted ranged weapons, turning the mobile Destroyer core into a scoring engine that punishes opponents for holding ground. It excels against mid-weight elite infantry and vehicle lists that can't trade efficiently into Reanimation-backed Destroyers, especially when Ophydians pin down backfield threats. Armies with high-volume mortal wound output or enough anti-tank overload to strip the C'tan and heavy Destroyers before Reanimation triggers will crack the attrition engine apart.
891: Built around War Dog Huntsmen, Executioners, Stalkers, and Karnivores flooding the board with 8–12 small Knights, this list runs across multiple detachments — most commonly Hunting Warpack, which lets a nearby War Dog expose an enemy unit within 12" for amplified targeting. The win condition is overwhelming anti-armour pressure through sheer model count and layered lethality: each War Dog threatens independently, so there is no single unit to isolate and kill while the pack contests every objective simultaneously. It punishes transport-heavy infantry armies hardest, as its mobile anti-armour suite strips transports and then grinds exposed passengers under Knight melee. Tight screening and hard-hitting elite single-model units crack it open, since each War Dog is individually fragile and losing tempo early leaves the pack too thin to threaten across the whole board.
892: Built around Repulsor Executioners, Sword Brethren, the Emperor's Champion, and a dense infantry core of Marshals, Castellans, Assault Intercessors, Crusaders, and Scouts, this Stormlance Task Force list plays like a grinding advance that never truly stops moving. The engine is Stormlance's core ability — every unit can charge after Advancing or Falling Back — letting Repulsor Executioners lay down punishing skimmer fire while the infantry swarm flows into combat on the same turn, threatening objectives and attrition simultaneously. It punishes slower, melee-averse armies that lack the screens to keep Sword Brethren and Assault Intercessors at arm's length, as the constant charge threat taxes positioning without relief. However, it struggles against elite shooting that can delete key pieces before contact, since the list's combat payoff collapses if its infantry blobs are thinned before they can close.
893: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Vindicators, and Scout screening units running the Saga of the Great Wolf detachment, this list plays a grinding mid-table brawl backed by heavy demolisher fire. The win condition is simple brutality: push the Terminator and character blob forward under Grimnar's leadership while Vindicators erase anything holding the mid-board, letting the melee hammer score through elimination and durable objective hold. It punishes elite infantry-light lists that cannot absorb repeated demolisher blasts and lack the bodies to trade into Terminator blobs efficiently. It cracks open against high-volume mortal-wound output or long-range anti-tank that can suppress the Vindicators before the melee core closes distance.
894: Built around Logan Grimnar, Wolf Guard Terminators, Terminator Assault Squads, Librarians in Terminator Armour, Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, Wolf Guard Headtakers, and Bjorn the Fell-Handed, this is a heavy infantry brawler that cycles detachments — Librarius Conclave, Champions of Fenris, Saga of the Great Wolf, and Veterans of the Fang among them — to flex its psychic buffs, charge threat, and movement each round. The core engine is crashing a wall of terminator-armoured elites and characters into the mid-table, using Librarius Conclave's rotating Psychic Discipline to patch whatever the matchup demands — Divination for reliable damage output, Biomancy to extend charge threat. It punishes elite low-model-count lists that can't absorb repeated multi-unit charges from durable Terminator blobs led by named characters stacking buffs. However, it folds to boards that deny the engagement — ranged attrition gunlines that strip characters before they arrive, or armies that out-speed it and contest objectives before the terminator wall makes contact.
895: Built around Gretchin screens, Stormboyz, Deffkoptas, Warbikers, Boyz, and Wazdakka Gutsmek, this is a Taktikal Brigade list that floods the table with cheap bodies and fast melee threats across every wave. The plan is to use Gretchin to lock down midfield objectives while Stormboyz — granted Battleline by the detachment — and Warbikers crash into the enemy lines, keeping infantry eligible to start actions even after advancing or falling back to stack primary score relentlessly. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that can't realistically kill through the sheer replacement volume of a multi-wave horde running layered lethality in melee. High-mobility alpha lists and anything that generates enough mortal wounds or blast weapons to thin screens before the swarm arrives will crack it wide open.
896: Built around Scarab Occult Terminators led by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, supported by Forgefiends, Sekhetar Robots, Rubric Marines, Chaos Spawn screens, and Tzaangor bodies flooding the midboard, this is a mass-horde brawler with a heavy gunline backbone. The plan is to saturate objectives with expendable Tzaangors and Spawn while the Terminators and Forgefiends threaten from range and punch through anything that contests, using sheer volume of bodies and psychic firepower to grind opponents off the board. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that lack the volume to clear multiple waves of cheap screening units while simultaneously answering the ranged threat of the Robots and Forgefiends. It struggles against fast aggressive lists that can isolate and overwhelm the Terminator brick before the screen re-establishes, since the build's midrange durability trades poorly into concentrated alpha-strike pressure.
897: Built around Hernkyn Pioneers, Kapricus Defenders mounted in Kapricus Carriers, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Einhyr Hearthguard, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and Hernkyn Yaegirs, this list plays a dense midboard brawl with layered transport infantry and heavy firepower across the whole table. The engine is the Farseekers detachment's +1 to hit within 12" on Hernkyn units, rewarding aggressive positioning that stacks kill pressure through the Needgaârd Oathband's YP generation per destroyed unit, converting battlefield attrition into a compounding resource engine. It punishes slow, durable gunlines that can't disengage from the midboard — the combination of mobile transports, hard-hitting Thunderkyn, and Ûthar delivering elite melee means overextended anchor units get isolated and dismantled for YP. Lists that can reliably deny the 12" Hernkyn threat bubble through high mobility or long-range alpha strikes, or flood cheap screens to slow the YP engine, will blunt its scoring before it reaches full momentum.
898: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and Kâhls operating under Hearthguard Covenant, this list layers elite close-range infantry with heavy armoured vehicles and a dense supporting cast of Pioneers, Thunderkyn, and Sagitaurs across the midfield. The engine is point-blank attrition: Hearthguard Covenant's wound-reroll-1 triggers inside 9", so the whole army is incentivised to push up, park on objectives, and grind enemy units off the table while accumulating YP through the Needgaârd or Mercenary Oathband secondaries. It punishes slower gunlines and elite low-model-count armies that cannot trade bodies fast enough to clear the sheer volume of durable infantry and vehicles contesting every midfield objective. Aggressive, fast-moving threat density — skimmers, transports, and screening infantry — can overwhelm the positioning requirements of the 9" wound reroll bubble, collapsing the build's damage output before it reaches optimal range.
899: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Hernkyn Pioneers, Kapricus Defenders riding Kapricus Carriers, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Hernkyn Yaegirs operating under the Needgaârd Oathband, this is a mid-table brawler that keeps mobile firepower humming across all phases. The engine is attrition through Kyn Points — every enemy unit destroyed feeds the Oathband's YP engine, while the Farseekers detachment (present in most lists) sharpens Hernkyn ranged attacks to +1 hit within 12", rewarding aggressive forward positioning that stacks kills. It punishes low-model-count elite armies brutally, converting each destroyed unit into compounding resource advantage while layered vehicle bodies absorb return fire. It cracks under alpha-strike pressure or mass volume shooting that deletes Carriers and Fortresses before the YP engine can generate meaningful tempo.
900: Built around Typhus, four squads of Poxwalkers, the Noxious Blightbringer, Malignant Plaguecasters, Deathshroud Terminators, a Lord of Contagion, the Tallyman, and often Mortarion, this is a Paragons of Putrescence list that weaponises the extended Contagion Range to blanket the mid-table in overlapping debuff auras from turn one. The engine is attrition-through-presence: Poxwalker bricks deny objectives by being effectively unkillable under layered Lethal buffs while Deathshroud and Mortarion apply lethal pressure to anything that tries to contest. It punishes low-volume, high-investment armies that cannot generate enough attacks to chew through bloated infantry and elite bodyguard screens simultaneously. It cracks when faced with high-mobility alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete Typhus or Mortarion before the Contagion bubble reaches critical coverage.
901: Built around Plague Marines in Chaos Rhinos, Deathshroud Terminators, Typhus leading Poxwalker hordes, Lords of Contagion, Foul Blightspawn, and Foetid Bloat-Drones, this Death Lord's Chosen list pairs a sprawling infantry mass with the Paragons of Putrescence detachment's extended Contagion Range to blanket the midfield in pestilence. The win condition is attrition through layered lethality: enemy units inside Contagion Range are constantly rolling against the Death Lord's Chosen passive, bleeding D3 mortal wounds on a 6-or-less each Command phase, while characters like the Biologus Putrifier and Lord of Virulence stack additional punishment on anything that survives. It punishes durable, multi-wound infantry lists that expect to trade efficiently, grinding them down through unstoppable chip damage before Deathshroud Terminators close and finish the job. Lists that alpha-strike from range or deny the midfield entirely can shut off the Contagion engine before it activates, leaving a slow army with no pressure lever to pull.
902: Built around Deathshroud Terminators, Lords of Contagion, Rotigus, the Great Unclean One, Beasts of Nurgle, Poxwalkers, Nurglings, Plaguebearers, Typhus, and Myphitic Blight-Haulers under the Tallyband Summoners detachment, this list fuses a Death Guard infantry core with a full Plague Legions daemon contingent to stack Contagion Range bonuses — the cross-faction proximity rules from Tallyband Summoners extend Contagion Range on Death Guard units while granting Nurgle's Gift to daemon units simultaneously. The plan is to flood mid-table with cheap chaff and durable daemons, letting stacked Contagion Range turn the entire board into a layered attrition engine that bleeds opponents off objectives while Deathshroud and Greater Daemons hammer anything that over-commits. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't survive sustained lethal toughness checks across multiple turns of scoring. However, high-mobility lists that avoid the Contagion bubble and pick off support characters early collapse the synergy chain before it becomes oppressive.
903: Built around Myphitic Blight-Haulers, both Foetid Bloat-Drone variants, Deathshroud Terminators, and a Lord of Contagion and Lord of Virulence command core, this is a mobile armour-cracking swarm that uses the Contagion Engines detachment to give every Blight-Hauler and Drone [ASSAULT] on their ranged weapons — letting them advance and shoot without penalty while Poxwalkers flood objectives. The win condition is layered attrition: Blight-Haulers and Bloat-Drones strip armour from range while advancing into scoring positions, Deathshroud provide a punishing melee threat, and Poxwalkers deny space and contest. It punishes slow, low-model-count elite armies that can't clear chaff fast enough before the armoured core closes and unloads. Armies that generate high volumes of anti-infantry at range can strip the Poxwalker screen early and expose the vehicles to alpha focus-fire before the ASSAULT move advantage pays off.
904: Built around multiple squads of Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Deathshroud Terminators, Lords of Contagion, Typhus leading Poxwalker blobs, and Plague Marines, this list runs Champions of Contagion to flex between Nurgle's Gift Plagues each battle round, with most lists also adding Paragons of Putrescence to push Character Contagion Range out to 12". The plan is to layer Contagion debuffs across the midfield while the Hauler packs apply mobile anti-armour pressure and the Deathshroud terminate anything that wanders into range, scoring through attrition and objective presence behind a wall of bodies. It punishes slower melee armies that can't strip wounds efficiently, because the stacking Lethal interactions and durable multi-wound models make straightforward trade-fighting enormously costly. Fast shooting lists that can kite the Haulers and ignore Contagion range entirely will crack this open before the debuff engine ever comes online.
905: Built around Plague Marines, Deathshroud Terminators, Poxwalkers, Malignant Plaguecasters, Lord of Contagion, Biologus Putrifier, Tallyman, Typhus, and Myphitic Blight-Haulers, this list layers Contagion Range pressure across the board using Characters to push the debuff bubble out to 12" via Paragons of Putrescence, while Flyblown Host drops Plague Marines into Infiltrator positions at deployment to immediately threaten mid-table objectives. The win condition is grinding attrition through stacked lethal conditions — using Poxwalkers as cheap objective holders and screens while Deathshroud and Plague Marines in Rhinos deliver high-damage melee into anything Afflicted or within Contagion Range. It punishes slow, high-toughness infantry lists that can't escape the Contagion bubble or outpace the screen-and-grind pressure. However, fast-moving armies with strong alpha-strike capability or long-range mortal wound output can strip the Character support staff before the Contagion engine comes fully online, collapsing the synergy the entire list depends on.
906: Built around Rotigus, a Great Unclean One, Beasts of Nurgle, Plaguebearers, Nurglings, Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Foetid Bloat-Drones with Heavy Blight Launchers, Deathshroud Terminators, a Lord of Contagion, and a Lord of Virulence, this list runs both Contagion Engines and Tallyband Summoners to stack Plague Legion units with Nurgle's Gift while extending Death Guard Contagion Ranges by 3" — a dual-detachment synergy that turns the entire army into a spreading lethality engine. The win condition is layered attrition: flood mid-table with durable Nurgle bodies, stack Contagion debuffs across as many enemy units as possible, and grind opponents off objectives through accumulated lethality rather than a single kill spike. Blight-Haulers and Bloat-Drones with Assault ranged weapons give the list surprising mobile anti-armour reach, punishing vehicle-heavy lists that expect to sit outside contagion range safely. It cracks when faced with fast, high-volume shooting that deletes key bubble-wrap screens before Contagion can spread — strip the Beasts and Nurglings early and the synergy engine collapses inward.
907: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, multiple Skorpius Disintegrators, Servitor Battleclades, and Skitarii Rangers screening under Lords of the Forge, with most lists also adding Ironstrider Ballistarii, Sicarian Infiltrators, and Pteraxii Skystalkers for aggressive board pressure. The plan is to park durable Tech-Priests — benefiting from 4+ Invulnerable Saves and Feel No Pain 5+ — behind massed firepower while Rad-zone Corps punishes static castle armies at game start, forcing opponents into a lose-lose decision between battle-shock and mortal wounds before a shot is fired. The layered infantry screens, mid-board brawlers, and skimmer guns punish elite low-model-count armies that lack the volume to clear screens while simultaneously threatening armour through mobile anti-tank. Against fast melee or deep-strike-heavy lists that can bypass the screen and isolate the gunline, the whole structure becomes fragile fast.
908: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, Sicarian Ruststalkers, Sicarian Infiltrators, Skitarii Rangers, Ironstrider Ballistarii, Pteraxii Skystalkers, and Servitor Battleclades, this is a mass-infantry swarm that floods the midboard with layered bodies across multiple unit types. The win condition is attrition through volume — Ruststalkers and Infiltrators brawl for midboard primaries while Ironstriders and Skorpius Disintegrators (in half of lists) suppress armour, with Cawl anchoring durability through his buffing presence. It punishes light-to-medium infantry lists that can't kill through sheer model count across multiple activations, overwhelming screens and contesting every objective simultaneously. Concentrated high-damage output that deletes whole units in single activations cracks this build open, since losing chunks of the swarm faster than it can trade collapses the board presence it depends on.
909: Built around Achilles Ridgerunners, Purestrain Genestealers, Neophyte Hybrids, Hyperadapted Raveners, Benefictus, Patriarch, Deathleaper, Acolyte Hybrids, Von Ryan's Leapers, and The Red Terror, this is a hybrid GSC/Tyranids Vanguard Invader swarm running the Final Day detachment to flood the board with both cultist bodies and fast Tyranid killers. The plan is to drown opponents in threat saturation — Raveners, Leapers, and Purestrains force impossible priority decisions while Neophyte Hybrids entrench in terrain and recover wounds through Xenocult Masses, locking down objectives for the long game. It punishes low-model-count lists that can't clear volume, overwhelming them across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It cracks under elite shooting armies that can efficiently delete chaff before the melee wave lands, collapsing the objective hold before the healing engine matters.
910: Built around Purestrain Genestealers, Achilles Ridgerunners, Neophyte Hybrids, Acolyte Hybrids, Reductus Saboteurs, Benefictus, Atalan Jackals, and Leman Russ Battle Tanks in the Brood Brothers Auxilia detachment, this is a mass-horde gunline that floods the board with cheap bodies backed by serious mobile anti-armour. The plan is to drown opponents in volume — Neophytes and Acolytes screen and contest objectives while Ridgerunners and Leman Russes pour firepower into whatever matters most, with Purestrain Genestealers threatening lethal melee counterattacks on anything that overextends. It punishes armies that rely on elite low-model-count units, overwhelming them with more targets than they can efficiently clear while Xenocult Masses (in roughly 40% of lists) regenerates Neophyte screening units sitting in terrain. Concentrated high-damage alpha strikes and elite melee units that ignore the horde and go straight for the backline armour crack it open, since the tanks are few enough that losing one hurts badly.
911: Built around Sanctus, Reductus Saboteurs, Purestrain Genestealers, Neophyte Hybrids, Benefictus, Acolyte Hybrids, and Achilles Ridgerunners operating under Heroes of the Uprising, this is a sprawling horde list that layers elite assassins over a tide of cheap bodies. The Killer rule on Sanctus and Reductus Saboteurs — rerolling 1s to hit and wound — turns Gene-tailored Toxins into a precision kill engine, while Ridgerunners and Purestrain Genestealers provide mobile anti-armour and threat saturation across every angle. It punishes elite armies that can't clear volume, drowning them in activations while the assassin core deletes key targets. Dense, high-volume armies that can efficiently clear Neophytes and screen out the Purse Genestealers before they engage will expose how fragile the scoring backbone really is.
913: Built around Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Sanguinary Guard, and Lemartes supported by Jump Pack Captains, Chaplains, and Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, this is a Rage-Cursed Onslaught list that floods the board with fast-moving melee threats from multiple angles. The win condition is charging with everything simultaneously — Rage-Cursed Onslaught's bonus attack on the charge, plus re-rolls to wound on 1s, creates a kill chain where multiple units punching in the same turn overwhelm a single defending unit at a time. Scouts, Intercessors, and Gladiator Lancers provide the objective-hold and anti-armour scaffolding that lets the jump infantry ignore attrition long enough to deliver decisive combat rounds. The build struggles when opponents can screen efficiently or stagger activations to absorb charges piecemeal, since the entire output model depends on actually getting the charge — anything that denies, disrupts, or absorbs the alpha swing deflates the engine.
914: Built around Sanguinary Priests buffing waves of Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Assault Intercessors, Chaplains with Jump Packs, Lemartes, Outriders, and Librarians, this is a Legacy Of Grace and Stormlance Task Force list that floods the board with fast, hard-hitting melee infantry. The engine is advance-and-charge: Legacy Of Grace hands Infantry Characters +1 to both rolls while Stormlance lets the whole force declare charges after Advancing or Falling Back, enabling relentless multi-turn pressure that scores through controlling board space and drowning opponents in combat. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count elite armies that cannot handle simultaneous threat vectors from multiple charging units across the whole table. It cracks under concentrated shooting that removes key characters before they can trigger the charge chain, and it struggles against armies that can screen wide and deny the advance-charge window entirely.
915:
Built around Baal Predators, Sanguinary Priests, Librarians, Assault Intercessors, and a jump pack Captain supported by Sanguinary Guard, this is a Bastion Task Force list that weaponises its Battleline units as a mobile gunline — Advance and Shoot, Advance and charge, Advance and perform Actions all in the same activation, letting infantry contest objectives without surrendering firepower or tempo.

The engine is flooding midfield with Assault Intercessors and Intercessors who never stop shooting, while Baal Predators pour anti-infantry fire downrange and Priests chain-buff combat survivability, scoring primaries through pure board presence backed by threat saturation.

It punishes slower, static armies that can't clear multiple coordinated threats simultaneously, as the combination of mobile Battleline screening and armoured skimmer fire forces opponents into bad prioritisation decisions.

It cracks open against elite alpha-strike armies that can surgically remove Priests early, collapsing the buff chain and leaving Battleline units exposed without their support scaffolding.
916:
Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, and Captains with Jump Packs, with Scout Squads providing board presence, this is a mobile assault force that floods the midfield with elite melee threats while Baal Predators and Vindicators deliver heavy fire support from armoured anchor points.

The plan is to use jump pack units to pressure enemy scoring pieces and key threats early, forcing reaction moves that bleed opponents off objectives while the armoured vehicles punish anything that clusters or advances into range.

It punishes slower, durable gunlines that can't quickly disengage — the combination of fast melee reach and armoured firepower creates two simultaneous threat vectors that overload defensive positioning.

It struggles against elite close-combat armies or heavy alpha-strike lists that can delete the jump pack core before it engages, and spreading forces across two distinct threat types means concentration of force is rarely achieved cleanly.
917: Built around Terminator Assault Squads, Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Bladeguard Veterans, and a Chaplain in Terminator Armour running Liberator Assault Group, this is a wall-to-wall melee army that floods every angle with charging bodies. The engine is simple: every unit that charges gains +2 Strength and +1 Attack on all melee weapons, so the Chaplain buffs Terminators into a brick that threatens anything while jump pack elements threaten every flank simultaneously. Scouts and Intercessors provide the cheap screen-and-hold layer that frees the combat units to charge rather than babysit objectives, punishing gunlines and low-model-count armies that can't absorb multi-threat charges from multiple vectors. The list cracks open against armies that can deny or survive the charge — durable, high-volume overwatch or units that simply weather the alpha and grind back, since outside the charge bonus the melee output drops sharply and the list has limited staying power in a protracted attrition fight.
918: Built around multiple Baal Predators, Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with jump packs, a Captain with jump pack, Commander Dante, Lemartes, and Chief Librarian Mephiston, this list runs the Liberator Assault Group detachment to blend fast armour with a charging elite infantry package. The Baal Predators apply mobile, high-volume firepower to soften targets while the jump pack assault elements — buffed on the charge to +2 Strength and +1 Attack on all melee weapons — crash in to finish units and contest objectives simultaneously. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't handle both the armoured shooting threat and the supercharged melee wave arriving in the same turn. Horde lists that absorb the charge buffs across masses of cheap bodies, or any build with strong anti-armour overload that can strip the Predators early, will expose how dependent this list is on both halves of its engine staying alive.
919: Built around Chaos Terminators, Obliterators, Mutilators, Kravek Morne, a Sorcerer in Terminator Armour, and Cultist Mobs, this is a heavily armoured midfield brawler that grinds forward on foot and dares the opponent to shift it. The plan is to park Terminators and Mutilators on mid-board objectives while Obliterators flex as mobile anti-armour, using Cultists as cheap screens and action-runners to free the hard bodies for pure attrition. It punishes low-volume elite armies that can't generate enough wounds to clear through multiple waves of high-toughness infantry before the Obliterators delete their key pieces. Against fast, high-AP shooting lists that can crack Terminator armour at range from turn one, the lack of consistent mobility and resilience to sustained overload damage leaves it scrambling for primaries.
920:
Built around Wyches, Incubi, Drazhar, Lelith Hesperax, Lady Malys, Succubi, Archon, Mandrakes, and Reavers delivered by wall-to-wall Venoms and Raiders, this Skysplinter Assault list is a mass-horde skimmer force that floods the table with elite melee infantry inside fast transports.

The plan is to use layered threat saturation — multiple independent kill-threats disembarking from skimmers simultaneously — forcing opponents to prioritize incorrectly while Drazhar and Lelith lead Incubi and Wyches into high-value targets, Scourges strip armor at range, and Mandrakes contest mid-board.

It punishes slow or low-model-count lists that can't answer simultaneous multi-vector melee charges without spreading their anti-horde tools fatally thin.

Concentrated shooting from armies that can strip transports before the infantry disembark collapses the entire engine, as stranded foot-sloggers rarely survive long enough to reach combat.
921: Built around Lady Malys, Hellions, Wyches, Incubi, Reavers, Mandrakes, and walls of Venoms ferrying infantry across the board, this is a high-volume, skimmer-heavy swarm that floods the table with cheap, fast bodies backed by elite close-range threats. The engine is relentless board saturation — Venoms project poison fire while Lady Malys enables unpredictable repositioning, Scourges suppress key targets with heavy weapons, and Incubi backed by Drazhar threaten to gut anything soft on an objective. It punishes low-model-count elite armies brutally, trading layered lethality and mass screening to overwhelm threat saturation while scoring through sheer presence on primary. Armies that can blank the skimmer-fire trade economy with durable multi-wound chaff or hard anti-horde blast weapons will crack this open, as losing Venoms early collapses the transport-infantry delivery engine the whole plan depends on.
922: Built around Wyches, Lelith Hesperax, multiple Succubi, Hellions, Mandrakes, Incubi, and a swarm of Venoms and Raiders delivering bodies at speed, this is a mass-horde melee assault army running Kabalite Agonysts with Spectacle of Spite as its most common secondary detachment. The plan is to flood the board with cheap, fast infantry delivered by skimmers, overwhelm objective zones through sheer volume and layered lethal hits, and use Scourges with heavy weapons plus Ravagers to punish anything that tries to hold ground at range. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't answer simultaneous threats across multiple board sectors, where Lelith and Succubi (commonly carrying Morghenna's Curse and Periapt of Torments) shred through small units faster than they can be replaced. However, high-volume shooting that can strip transports before disembarkation cracks the delivery system open and leaves expensive melee units stranded without their threat range.
923: Built around the Silent King, Imotekh the Stormlord, Nekrosor Ammentar, Triarch Praetorians, Triarch Stalkers, and Ophydian Destroyers, this list runs the Obeisance Phalanx to concentrate wound-roll bonuses from its Noble, Lychguard, and Triarch units onto a single priority target each Command phase. The win condition is surgical threat removal — designate a dangerous enemy unit, pile in with buffed Triarch Praetorians and Stalkers to delete it efficiently, while Ophydian Destroyers tunnel up to threaten flanks and backfield objectives. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies by stacking wound bonuses against hard targets that lack the volume to absorb repeated nominated-target kills. Horde screens and durable infantry blobs dilute the single-target focus, and losing the designation chain early through character sniping collapses the entire offensive engine.
924: Built around Scout Sentinels, Rogal Dorn Commanders, Leman Russ Exterminators, and Hellhounds, this is a fully mechanised armoured column that overwhelms opponents with layered vehicle firepower at every range band. 928: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Gaunt's Ghosts, Krieg Combat Engineers, Cadian Shock Troops, Cadian Command Squads, and Kasrkin, this Grizzled Company list drops elite infantry from reserve while flooding objectives with cheap bodies. 933: Built around Tech-Priest Enginseers keeping Baneblades and Hellhounds operational, this is a heavy armour gunline that floods the board with Astra Militarum Titanic and Squadron firepower under the Steel Hammer detachment, which lets those vehicles blast enemies even in Engagement Range without penalty. 935: Built around Tormentors, Infractors, and Lord Exultants flooding forward in Chaos Rhinos, supported by Flawless Blades, Lucius the Eternal, Defilers, Noise Marines, winged Daemon Princes, Chaos Spawn, and Maulerfiends, this is an aggressive, transport-heavy melee swarm running the Frenzied Host detachment. 937: Built around Librarians projecting Psychic Discipline buffs across the force, Redemptor Dreadnoughts as durable mid-field anchors, Gladiator Lancers as mobile anti-armour, and Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs backed by an Apothecary Biologis, this is a multi-threat gunline with genuine close-combat teeth. 957: Built around twin Hekaton Land Fortresses pumping Sustained Hits 1 onto embarked or nearby Leagues of Votann Infantry via Firebase Control, with Einhyr Hearthguard, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Hernkyn Pioneers, and a dense supporting cast locking down the midfield. The win condition is attrition through volume — screen opponents off primary with disposable Cultists, push Legionaries and Chosen forward in Rhinos to contest and trade, and leverage Dark Pact-boosted ranged attacks to punch above their weight class in the shooting phase. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that struggle to clear waves of cheap bodies and can be overloaded by the sheer number of scoring units across multiple zones. However, high-output anti-infantry spam — anything that clears hordes efficiently at range — collapses the screen before the Rhinos can deliver, stranding Chosen and Legionaries in the open with no cushion.
966: Built around Noise Marines, Chosen, Legionaries, and Chaos Bikers transported in Chaos Rhinos, with Cultist Mobs flooding objectives and Huron Blackheart alongside Masters of the Maelstrom providing command support, this list plays a broad mid-board pressure game across multiple detachment frameworks. The win condition is drowning opponents in overlapping threat vectors — Noise Marines hose infantry with volume fire while Bikers and Red Corsairs Raiders skirt flanks for mobile anti-armour kills, forcing opponents to address too many angles simultaneously. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't absorb the sheer number of activations, using Cultist screens to protect the shooting core while Rhinos deliver melee threats into the midfield. However, it struggles against concentrated high-damage output that can blast through screens early, cracking the Rhino delivery system and isolating Noise Marines before they can fire.
967: Built around Possessed, Chosen, Cultist Mobs, Mutilators, and Huron Blackheart himself, this is a Heretic Astartes infantry horde that floods the table with bodies while cycling a rotating buff through the Huron's Marauders detachment — granting enhanced abilities to every eligible unit, upgraded further for anything in Huron's line of sight. The win condition is objective saturation through sheer volume: Cultists screen and hold, while Possessed and Chosen push into mid-table fights backed by Mutilators providing a slow-grinding third wave. It punishes elite-infantry lists that lack the volume of attacks to clear multiple cheap screens before the Possessed and Chosen close in for layered melee punishment. Ranged alpha-strike armies and anything with consistent high-damage shooting can strip the screening layer early and isolate the expensive combat units before Huron's buff engine ever gets rolling.
968: Built around Talos, Cronos, Incubi with Drazhar, Scourges with heavy weapons, Ravagers, and Venoms ferrying Kabalite Warriors and Mandrakes, this is a layered skimmer-fire army running Kabalite Cartel with the Tools of Torment secondary detachment. The plan is to flood the midboard with tough, regenerating Talos and Cronos as objective anchors while Ravagers and Scourges delete armour from range, then Venoms deliver Incubi and Kabalites to contest or clear whatever survives. It punishes lists that rely on single large threats or static gunlines, piling mobile anti-armour into one target while Mandrakes and infantry bleed secondaries dry. Armies with durable, spread-out bodies and board-wide lethality crack it open by overwhelming the skimmer screen before the pain-engine core can stabilise.
969: Built around Skorpekh Lords, Skorpekh Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, Ophydian Destroyers, the C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, and Flayed Ones, this is a melee-heavy assault force that floods multiple threat vectors simultaneously across the table. The win condition is attrition through multi-wave contact: Ophydian Destroyers dig up behind screens while Skorpekh units crash forward supported by Nekrosor Ammentar, forcing the opponent to answer dangerous charges from multiple angles every turn. It punishes slow, low-mobility armies that cannot reposition to avoid the staggered assault waves, as the sheer volume of melee threats overloads defensive screens and targeting priority. However, it struggles against elite shooting lists that can isolate and delete individual assault packages before they close, as losing key pieces early unravels the coordinated multi-prong pressure the build depends on.
970: Built around Technomancers shepherding Canoptek Wraiths, dual C'tan shards (Nightbringer and Void Dragon), Illuminor Szeras, Skorpekh Lords, Ophydian Destroyers, and Canoptek Scarab Swarms, this is a mobile threat-overload list running Awakened Dynasty — whose detachment ability adds 1 to Hit rolls for every unit led by a Necrons Character. The plan is to flood the board with independently dangerous pieces that all benefit from Technomancer-led reanimation support, forcing opponents to triage while Canoptek Reanimators sustain key units and C'tan apply unblockable pressure on priority targets. It punishes gunline and low-model-count elite armies that can't kill fast enough across multiple fronts simultaneously, turning the attrition game firmly in Necrons' favour. Its vulnerability is concentrated alpha-strike aggression or high-volume mortal-wound output that races ahead of the reanimation engine before it can stabilise.
971: Built around Necron Warriors, Immortals, and a deep bench of characters — Technomancer, Plasmancer, Orikan, Imotekh, Royal Warden, Illuminor Szeras, and Skorpekh Lord leading Skorpekh Destroyers — all operating under Awakened Dynasty, which adds 1 to Hit rolls whenever a CHARACTER leads a unit. The plan is to stack leaders onto Immortals and Warriors to generate reliable, buffed shooting while Canoptek Reanimators sustain casualties, keeping scoring bodies on objectives long enough to grind out primary points. Awakened Dynasty's hit bonus punishes mid-toughness infantry armies that can't clear buffed, reanimating blobs before the points haemorrhage. However, elite low-model armies or high-AP volumetric damage can bypass reanimation efficiency and collapse the scoring base faster than the support characters can compensate.
972:
Built around double Immortals squads, Plasmancers, Warriors, and Flayed Ones, this list runs the Hand of the Dynasty detachment to give Immortals and Warriors the Assault rule, letting them advance and shoot without penalty while still performing actions.

The plan is to flood mid-table objectives with durable, mobile infantry that score while shooting, using Plasmancers to boost lethality across multiple threat layers rather than relying on a single kill piece.

It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't clear volume efficiently, because the Assault-advance interaction means the infantry never stop contesting ground or scoring.

The weakness is raw damage output — 40% win rate signals that lists with heavy elite firepower or elite melee simply delete the infantry blocks faster than Reanimation can compensate.
973: Built around Skorpekh Destroyers, Skorpekh Lord, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Necron Warriors, Immortals, Ophydian Destroyers, Flayed Ones, and Lychguard — all operating under Cursed Legion, with Hand of the Dynasty layered on top in three-quarters of lists — this is a multi-threat toolkit army that floods the board with Destroyer Cult pressure across every phase. The engine is the Cursed Legion buff chain: Destroyer Cult weapons gain +2 Strength baseline, and the first kill or Below Half-Strength trigger each turn escalates that bonus further, so Skorpekh and Lokhust units that draw first blood become exponentially more dangerous as the game progresses. Warriors and Immortals with Assault on their ranged weapons, courtesy of Hand of the Dynasty, keep the midboard contested while the melee destroyers punish any opponent who presents soft or medium targets without screens, overwhelming them before they can consolidate. The build cracks when facing durable, high-toughness armies that can tank the initial kills and deny the cascade trigger, leaving the Strength bonus on ice and the army fighting at base efficiency across the mid-game.
975: Built around Doomsday Arks, Canoptek Wraiths, Technomancers, Canoptek Reanimators, Skorpekh Lords, Ophydian Destroyers, Skorpekh Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, and Flayed Ones under Awakened Dynasty, this list pairs long-range Doomsday Ark firepower with a deeply mobile melee threat package. The Awakened Dynasty's +1 to Hit on Character-led units sharpens the Skorpekh and Wraith combat elements, while Technomancers and Reanimators keep bodies cycling back into the fight to contest objectives turn after turn. It punishes mid-range gunlines that expect to trade efficiently — the reanimation engine means every attrition calculation is wrong, and the multi-vector assault from Ophydian deep strikers and Flayed Ones forces opponents to defend everywhere at once. Tightly-wound elite shooting lists that can bypass reanimation with mortal wounds or high-volume high-AP attacks, or armies that simply out-range the Arks, will crack this castle before it can fully establish board control.
976: Built around Doomsday Arks, Ophydian Destroyers, Flayed Ones, Technomancers, and Canoptek Wraiths, this list blends a backfield heavy-weapons platform with an aggressive melee delivery system. The Doomsday Arks sit back generating anti-armour pressure while the Destroyers and Flayed Ones threaten midfield and close-quarters zones, with Technomancers providing repair support to keep key pieces on the table. It punishes static gunlines that can't strip layered threats simultaneously — the opponent must answer both the long-range Ark firepower and multiple melee flanks at once, creating genuine decision paralysis. However, the list runs a fragmented detachment spread across four options with no dominant choice, and its below-average win rate signals it struggles against highly mobile armies that can isolate and overwhelm the Arks before the melee elements arrive to relieve pressure.
977:
Built around the Nightbringer, multiple Transcendent C'tan, the Deceiver, the Void Dragon, Ophydian Destroyers, Flayed Ones, Canoptek Wraiths, and Technomancer support, this is a C'tan-heavy mobile toolbox army with no fixed detachment identity.

The win condition is threat saturation — fielding so many dangerous independent models that opponents cannot neutralise all of them, then letting surviving C'tan and Destroyers delete priority targets while Flayed Ones and Wraiths contest and hold objectives.

It punishes armies that lack the volume of quality anti-monster shooting needed to address six-plus high-wound threats simultaneously, leaving at least one C'tan free to rampage through backlines.

It cracks open when a shooting-heavy opponent brings enough AP-ignoring volume to efficiently chew through every model in sequence, or when tight board control collapses the army's reliance on positional flexibility.
978: Built around Lokhust Destroyers led by Lokhust Lords, Nekrosor Ammentar, Skorpekh Destroyers led by Skorpekh Lords, Ophydian Destroyers, Canoptek Wraiths, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, and Canoptek Reanimators in Awakened Dynasty — a detachment that adds 1 to Hit rolls for every attack made by a unit led by a Necrons Character. The plan is to deliver multiple independent kill threats simultaneously: Lokhust Lords stack the Awakened Dynasty hit bonus onto Lokhust Destroyers for reliable ranged damage, while Ophydian Destroyers and Skorpekh units crash into melee, all screened and sustained by Reanimators keeping key pieces alive. This punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't weather coordinated multi-angle pressure from both shooting and close combat in the same turn. It cracks under volume-attrition lists that can strip characters before the hit bonus fires and overwhelm Reanimator coverage across too many units at once.
980: Built around Cadian Shock Troops, Scout Sentinels, Kasrkin, a Cadian Command Squad, Leman Russ Vanquishers, and Tech-Priest Enginseers, this is a layered gunline that mixes massed infantry screens with hard-hitting armour. The plan is to hold the backfield with waves of Guardsmen while Vanquishers crack heavy targets and Kasrkin punch priority units at range, keeping the Enginseer alive to maintain key vehicles under fire. It punishes slow, expensive armies that want to trade efficiently — stacking bodies and anti-armour volume overwhelms lists that can't deal with multiple threat types simultaneously. It cracks open badly against aggressive mid-table brawlers and fast alpha-strike threats that can bypass the screens before the gunline establishes lanes, and the list's below-average results suggest it consistently struggles to close out scoring games against top-tier competition.
981: Built around Victrix Honour Guard, Marneus Calgar, Bladeguard Veterans, and a Repulsor Executioner core, supported by Librarian-powered Psychic Discipline rotations and Scout-led screening, this list leans hardest into Librarius Conclave — cycling Divination for re-rolls into Biomancy for mobility as the situation demands. The plan is to park Repulsor Executioners as a sustained firepower platform while Calgar and the Honour Guard bodyguard bubble push onto midfield objectives, using Scout screens to deny deep-strike lanes and protect the gunline's flanks. It punishes slower elite armies that can't clear durable, multi-layered screening before the Executioners and Bladeguard bleed them dry in attrition. It cracks against high-volume alpha-strike lists that can strip screens early and isolate Calgar's bubble, leaving the Honour Guard's protection investment stranded without the characters it's built to keep alive.
982: Built around a dense core of Terminator Assault Squads, Terminator Squads, and Heavy Intercessors led by an Ancient in Terminator Armour, a Librarian in Terminator Armour, a Captain in Gravis Armour, Caanok Var, and Iron Father Feirros, this list runs Bastion Task Force to let its Battleline units shoot and charge after Advancing or Falling Back, keeping a thick wall of bodies perpetually threatening objectives. The win condition is attrition through volume — the Terminator brick absorbs punishment while Heavy Intercessors flood midfield, and the Librarius Conclave's rotating Psychic Disciplines sharpen output round by round to grind down whatever stands in the way. It punishes horde armies and low-AP spam lists that struggle to crack 2+ saves across a mass of wounds, wearing them down through sheer durability and counter-punch. It cracks against elite anti-tank overload lists or anything with high-volume high-AP output that can strip the brick faster than the Ancient's aura can sustain it.
983: Built around Redemptor and Ballistus Dreadnoughts holding terrain alongside Heavy Intercessors and Intercessor Squads, this is a Ceramite Sentinels gunline that plants itself in cover and refuses to move. The engine is Entrenched — by stationing durable infantry and dreadnoughts inside terrain features from turn one, every unit gains re-rolls on 1s to hit and wound while also earning the Entrenched keyword, generating sustained firepower and defensive resilience simultaneously. It punishes slow, durable armies — elite infantry and heavy vehicle lists that can't clear terrain-hugging units fast enough before the cumulative volume of re-rolled shooting grinds them down. Its weakness is mobility and board control: an opponent who seizes mid-table early forces this castle to either abandon cover and lose its core rule, or cede objectives and bleed points.
984: Built around Ballistus and Redemptor Dreadnoughts, Hellblasters, Intercessors, Terminators, and Lieutenants operating under the Gladius Task Force, this is a layered heavy gunline that uses the Devastator Doctrine to advance and shoot without penalty, extending its threat range while keeping guns hot. The win condition is sustained firepower attrition — Hellblasters and Ballistus Dreadnoughts strip armour at range while Terminators and Intercessors hold objectives to force the opponent into the killzone. It punishes slow, durable elite armies that must walk into concentrated fire, rewarding patient positioning and doctrine timing. It cracks open against fast assault or deep-strike pressure that collapses the firing line before doctrines can be cycled, leaving individual units isolated and unable to mutual-support.
985: Built around War Dog Executioners, Karnivores, Brigands, and Stalkers — a full pack of mobile armoured hunters — with Cultist Mobs providing cheap screening bodies under the Houndpack Lance detachment. The gameplan is to nominate a single high-value enemy unit each Command phase for Sustained Hits 1 across the entire pack, then funnel overwhelming ranged and melee output into that target to delete it before rotating to the next, all while Cultists sit on home objectives. This list punishes armour-heavy and elite-unit armies that present obvious priority targets, letting the Sustained Hits focus multiplier shred expensive models efficiently. It cracks open against horde lists that dilute the targeting mechanic and swarm the War Dogs before they can cycle through enough units to clear objectives.
986: Built around the Knight Tyrant — a towering centerpiece appearing in nearly nine out of ten lists — this build uses the Bastions of Tyranny detachment to squeeze extra accuracy out of every swing against battle-shocked targets, layering that bonus onto an already punishing mobile anti-armour threat profile. The plan is to bully opponents into battle shock through sheer pressure and then exploit the hit bonus to compound kills, while a flexible supporting cast of War Dogs and medium Knights floods objectives and maintains board presence. It punishes slower, elite armies that can't screen efficiently or recover from battle-shock cascades, burying them under layered high-damage attacks from multiple angles simultaneously. However, it struggles against fast, resilient forces that can avoid battle shock, deny the hit bonus, and trade efficiently against its expensive individual models — one unanswered alpha strike on the Tyrant can gut the list's damage ceiling entirely.
987: Built around the Knight Despoiler, packs of War Dog Karnivores, and the Knight Rampager, this is a mobile armoured assault list that floods the board with heavy melee threats across multiple threat vectors. The win condition is overwhelming the opponent's damage priority — Karnivores hunt flanks and tie up key pieces while Despoilers and Rampagers crash into the centre, generating kills that convert into scored primaries through sheer board presence and OC tonnage. The Infernal Lance's Malefic Surge empowerment rewards aggressive positioning, giving the list burst-damage spikes that can delete mid-tier armour and elite infantry in a single activation. It struggles against armies that can reliably force battle shock early, concentrate high-AP firepower onto individual Knights to trade efficiently, or screen the flanks well enough to deny the Karnivores clean charge lanes.
989: Built around Repulsor Executioners, Sword Brethren, Assault Intercessors (both foot and jump pack), and a dense command stack of Marshals, Castellans, Emperor's Champion, and High Marshal Helbrecht, this is a Gladius Task Force list that fuses a heavy gunline core with a mass of cheap objective-holding infantry. The Devastator Doctrine's advance-and-shoot rule lets the Repulsor Executioners reposition without sacrificing firepower, while the infantry flood — Scout Squads, Crusader Squads, and Intercessors — saturates objectives and forces opponents into unfavorable trades. It punishes horde and mid-tier mechanized lists by combining high-volume shooting with a wall of bodies that is genuinely difficult to clear off points in a single turn. However, elite alpha-strike armies or high-damage anti-tank overload can strip the Repulsors early, collapsing the shooting engine before the infantry mass can compensate.
990: Built around Gladiator Lancers, Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Headtakers, and Iron Priests running Saga of the Great Wolf, this list blends heavy armour with elite melee in a flexible mid-board package. The Lancers provide long-range anti-tank pressure while the Terminator blocks and Headtakers push forward to brawl on objectives, with Logan's command presence and Iron Priests' repair utility keeping the machine-war engine online. It punishes slow, durable gunlines that can't simultaneously deal with heavy vehicles and charging elite infantry threatening multiple angles at once. However, lists that can screen the mid-board efficiently or deliver concentrated alpha-strike damage early will overwhelm the build before its flexible Hunting Pack selections can compound advantage across the game.
992: Built around multiple Librarians (including Terminator-armoured variants), Deathwatch Veterans, Terminator squads, Intercessors, Fortis Kill Teams, and Rhino transports, this list runs the Bastion Task Force with most lists also taking the Librarius Conclave to cycle psychic disciplines each round. The engine is wave-after-wave of Battleline infantry that can shoot and charge after Advancing or Falling Back, keeping pressure on objectives while Librarians flex between Biomancy, Divination, and Pyromancy to suit the game state. It punishes static gunlines and horde armies by flooding the board with bodies that never have to choose between moving and fighting, making every threat angle simultaneously active. It cracks open against elite, low-model lists that can delete key squads before the combined-arms pressure accumulates, exposing how much the build relies on volume rather than raw hitting power.
993: Built around Deathwatch Terminator Squads, Librarians (on foot and in Terminator armour), Deathwatch Veterans, and Indomitor Kill Teams, this list plants a durable armoured core mid-board and layers psychic discipline buffs across the entire force each battle round — cycling between re-rolls, movement, and firepower as the situation demands. The win condition is overwhelming a single target per phase with massed special-issue ammunition and heavy weapons, using Temporal Corridor to teleport the Terminator brick into threatening positions while Veterans and Indomitors hold and contest objectives. It punishes heavy gunline and horde armies hardest, flooding the mid-table with resilient multi-wound bodies that absorb shooting and then dump lethal volume fire in return. It cracks under focused elite melee pressure or fast alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete the Terminator brick before its psychic buffs compound.
994:
Built around multiple Norn Assimilators, Norn Emissaries, Maleceptors, the Swarmlord, and Biovores, this list runs primarily under Talons of the Norn Queen, using its Singular Purpose ability to retask individual Monster units each Command phase as the game state shifts.

The plan is to flood the mid-table with high-OC Monsters that threaten multiple angles simultaneously, forcing opponents into reactive positions while Biovores chip screens and the Swarmlord enables aggressive repositioning to lock down scoring zones.

It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't clear multiple large-base threats per turn before the Monsters dig into objectives and hold through raw Objective Control.

The build struggles against elite melee or alpha-strike lists that can cripple key Monsters early, since losing Starting Strength degrades the threat profile before the Singular Purpose flexibility ever pays off.
995: Built around Exocrines, Tyrannofexes, Maleceptors, Norn Emissaries, a Hive Tyrant, Neurotyrant, Zoanthropes, and Biovores backed by Hormagaunt screens, this Invasion Fleet list blends a heavy shooting battery with a highly mobile, tool-rich frontline. The plan is to soften targets with massed indirect and direct fire while Maleceptors, Norn Emissaries, and the Hive Tyrant push aggressively into mid-board, contesting objectives and creating kill lanes that turn scoring opportunities into threat responses. It punishes static gunlines and elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear durable synapse-linked monsters across multiple vectors simultaneously. It cracks when faced with fast, high-volume anti-monster firepower that can strip the big creatures before the shooting battery can trade efficiently, leaving the Hormagaunt screens overexposed.
996: Built around Neurolictors, the Swarmlord, a Neurotyrant, Screamer-Killers, and Biovores, this Ambush Predators list drops assassins and monsters from deep strike to threaten every corner of the board simultaneously. The win condition is coordinated pressure: Neurolictors deep strike to threaten or eliminate characters while Screamer-Killers and Swarmlord crash into the midboard, using the Neurotyrant's synapse bubble to keep the killing engine coherent. It punishes elite, character-heavy lists hard — Neurolictors' re-roll hit rolls of 1 against CHARACTER units make assassinating exposed leaders genuinely reliable. However, high-volume, low-character lists that can screen the deep strike corridors and simply outgun the relatively fragile monster package will crack this build open before its threats can converge.
997: Built around multiple Tyranid Primes with Lash Whip, swarms of Hormagaunts, Maleceptors, Raveners, and Tyrannofexes operating under Invasion Fleet, this is a mobile horde army that floods the board with layered threats at every range band. The win condition is overwhelming volume — Primes buff adjacent Hormagaunt blobs into a grinding mid-table brawl while Tyrannofexes provide anti-armour overload and Maleceptors apply psychic pressure, all generating consistent scoring through presence and denial. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally, as the sheer number of activations and bodies makes efficient trading impossible while Biovores chip screens from safety. Armies that can focus high-damage shooting into the Maleceptors and Tyrannofexes before the swarm engages can strip the backbone early, and anything with strong blast weapons or wide-template damage tears through the Hormagaunt blobs that hold the scoring engine together.
998: Built around Hormagaunts, Tyranid Primes with Lash Whips, Biovores, Neurolictors, and a Neurotyrant, this is a mobile swarm with a deep-striking harassment spine and a synapse-dependent infantry core. The plan is to flood midboard objectives with Hormagaunt blobs kept in fighting shape by the Primes' Lash Whip buffs, while Neurolictors deep strike in to disrupt and pin opposing characters, and Biovores chip away at screens from range. It punishes infantry-heavy armies that rely on dense screens and backfield objective holders, as the combination of deep-striking pressure and volume bodies makes safe positioning nearly impossible. It cracks open against elite high-damage lists that can delete Hormagaunt squads in bulk before synapse support arrives, leaving the swarm leaderless and below fighting strength.
999: Built around massive Termagant blobs, Biovores, Tyrannofexes, the Neurotyrant, the Swarmlord, Lictors, and Von Ryan's Leapers, this is a mobile swarm that layers cheap bodies over a gunline backbone. The plan is to flood objectives with expendable Termagants while Biovores and Tyrannofexes grind opposing units from range, with Swarmlord and Neurotyrant amplifying synapse-dependent buffs and Lictors enabling flexible deep-strike pressure. It punishes low-model-count lists that can't clear waves of chaff fast enough to also deal with heavy artillery and infiltrators simultaneously. It cracks apart against high-volume, high-strength shooting that deletes horde screens quickly, exposing the slower support pieces to focused fire before the swarm can score meaningful board presence.
1031: Built around Sydonian Dragoons with taser lances, Belisarius Cawl, Skitarii Rangers, Ironstrider Ballistarii, Skorpius Disintegrators, Sicarian Infiltrators, and Thulia Ghuld, this is a layered mobile force that floods midboard with infantry screens while cycling independent kill elements forward. The win condition is strangling opponent movement with Infiltrators and Rangers holding objectives while Dragoons and Ballistarii apply mobile anti-armour pressure turn over turn, letting Disintegrators farm secondaries from safe skimmer positions. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot contest multiple objective zones simultaneously, as the infantry density overwhelms their clearing capacity. It cracks open against hard alpha-strike lists or high-AP heavy shooting that can strip the midboard screens before the Dragoons close distance and the Disintegrators find clean lanes.
1032: Built around Hastarii Fusiliers, Skitarii Rangers, Servitor Battleclades, and Skorpius Duneriders ferrying them forward, with Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, and Tech-Priest Manipuli stacking buffs across a mass of cheap TECH-PRIEST bodies that benefit from 4+ Invulnerable saves and Feel No Pain 5+ under Lords of the Forge. The plan is to flood mid-table with transported infantry blobs, layer overlapping fields of fire from Ironstrider Ballistarii and Hastarii units, and grind scoring through sheer volume of bodies that are harder to remove than they look. It punishes armies that rely on incremental damage and attrition, since the FNP stacking on Tech-Priests and the mass body count make efficient trades extremely difficult. However, hard-hitting alpha-strike lists or concentrated high-AP shooting can strip transports early and strand infantry in the open, collapsing the whole layered fire structure before it gets rolling.
1029: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Kastelan Robots with their Cybernetica Datashsmiths, Onager Dunecrawlers, and a deep bench of Tech-Priests all hardened by the Lords of the Forge detachment's 4+ Invulnerable Save and Feel No Pain 5+, this is a grinding mid-table brawler that floods objectives with durable infantry screens and near-unkillable walker threats. The win condition is attrition: Tech-Priests use Baffling Data Screed to erode enemy vehicles at close range while Kastelans and Dunecrawlers hold the midfield and Rangers plus Sicarian Infiltrators contest secondary objectives across the board. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't generate enough volume of fire to push through stacked defensive layers on multiple fronts simultaneously. It cracks open against high-mobility lists that ignore its gunline entirely, cherry-pick exposed Tech-Priests before their defensive buffs matter, and out-score it on primaries through speed rather than combat.
960: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Tech-Priest Manipuli, Servitor Battleclades, Skitarii Vanguard, Sicarian Infiltrators, Ironstrider Ballistarii, Skorpius Duneriders, and the full supporting cast of Rangers, Pteraxii, Kataphron Destroyers, and Thulia Ghuld, this list runs Lords of the Forge as its primary detachment — keeping Tech-Priests alive on 4+ invulnerable saves and Feel No Pain 5+ while weaponizing Baffling Data Screed to force enemy vehicles into reactive shooting. The plan is to flood mid-table with massed transported infantry and layered bodies, using Skorpius Duneriders to deliver Vanguard and Infiltrators into scoring positions while Ironstrider Ballistarii and Kataphron Destroyers overload opposing armour with mobile anti-tank output. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot clear multiple waves of cheap screening infantry before the gunline locks in range. Armies that can delete Duneriders early and deny the transport delivery — particularly alpha-strike heavy lists — strip the positional engine before it comes online.
1059: Built around Howling Banshees, Warp Spiders, Fire Dragons, Avatar of Khaine, Fuegan, Lhykhis, Jain Zar, Rangers, Swooping Hawks, Storm Guardians, Eldrad Ulthran, and War Walkers, this Warhost list floods the board with elite Aspect Warriors whose Agile Manoeuvres are supercharged by bonus Battle Focus tokens and enhanced Swift as the Wind movement. The plan is to generate overwhelming layered lethality through coordinated multi-unit strikes — Fire Dragons and Fuegan crack armour while Banshees and Jain Zar shred infantry in melee, with Rangers holding backfield objectives cheaply. It punishes lists that cannot screen multiple simultaneous threats, as the sheer volume of mobile, specialist units creates impossible target-priority decisions. However, the build struggles against anything that can out-attrition its fragile elites or alpha-strike its key characters before the Aspect engine assembles.
1056: Built around Warlock Conclaves, Farseers, Howling Banshees, Fire Dragons, and Jain Zar operating under Fateful Performance and the Seer Council's Fate dice engine, this list floods the board with elite Aeldari infantry backed by War Walkers and Corsair Voidreavers. The win condition is layered lethality on a precise turn sequence: Fate dice smooth out Stratagem activation, Banshees and Jain Zar charge through screens untouched, and Fire Dragons delete whatever armour the melee wave exposes. It punishes mid-density armies that can't screen every angle simultaneously, overwhelming them with interlocking threat vectors across multiple unit types. Tight castle defensive lists with durable bodies in every lane drain Fate dice faster than they refill, clogging the engine and forcing unfavourable combat trades.
1058: Built around multiple Troupe squads led by Troupe Masters and supported by the Avatar of Khaine, Prince Yriel, Lhykhis, Corsair Voidscarred, and Warp Spiders, this list floods the board with fast, layered Harlequins infantry ferried in Starweavers and Falcons across three interchangeable detachments — Eldritch Raiders, Twilight Flickers, or Serpent's Brood. The engine is disembark-and-charge: Troupes pile out of transports, stack lethal output from multiple angles, and use the Avatar's presence to anchor mid-table brawls while Rangers and Voidscarred hold flanks and score. It punishes armies that rely on single-layer screens or fragile backfield objective holders, as the sheer volume of fast bodies arriving from multiple vectors overwhelms conventional denial. However, high-volume mortal wound output or blast weapons that strip the cheap transport screen early leave the Troupes stranded and exposed before they can close.
1061: Built around Warp Spiders, Rangers, Lhykhis, Striking Scorpions, the Avatar of Khaine, and Fuegan, this is a layered Aspect Warrior force that floods the board with mobile, lethal infantry backed by skimmer firepower. The plan is to use Rangers and Striking Scorpions to contest and screen objectives early while Warp Spiders and Fuegan threaten high-value targets with lethal damage output, letting the Avatar and Lhykhis anchor brawls and create scoring pressure across multiple points simultaneously. It punishes mid-table infantry-heavy lists hard, where layered lethality and the ability to advance and charge under Eldritch Raiders lets it dictate engagement ranges and overwhelm screens before they can anchor. It cracks open against elite, low-model-count armies that can selectively delete key pieces — losing Fuegan or the Avatar early collapses the mid-table brawl presence that makes the objective pressure sustainable.
1062: Built around the Avatar of Khaine, Prince Yriel, Eldrad Ulthran, and massed Corsair infantry — Skyreavers, Voidreavers, and Voidscarred — operating primarily out of Armoured Warhost, with roughly half of lists supplementing via Eldritch Raiders to let advancing units still declare charges.
