1073: Built around Thunderwolf Cavalry, Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, and Bjorn the Fell-Handed, this is a mid-table brawler that floods the board with durable, high-threat melee units across multiple unit types. Operating under Saga of the Great Wolf, the list uses rotating Hunting Packs — particularly Encircling Jaws for re-rolled Advance and Charge rolls — to ensure multiple units crash into combat simultaneously, trading kill-for-kill and contesting midfield objectives through sustained melee pressure. It punishes slower gunlines that can't prioritise targets effectively, as Terminators, Cavalry, and Bjorn all demand different answers and collectively overwhelm single-threat removal plans. It cracks under coordinated alpha-strike lists or high-mobility armies that deny the charge, since the engine collapses when its brawlers are stranded out of combat with no scoring payoff.
1074: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Thunderwolf Cavalry, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, Wulfen with Storm Shields, Ragnar Blackmane, and a dense supporting infantry core, this list runs Saga of the Beastslayer to blanket every attack against Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles with Lethal Hits. The plan is to crash multiple elite melee threats into the midboard simultaneously, using Thunderwolf Cavalry as fast-moving shock units and Terminators as the hammer, grinding through high-value targets to complete the Saga tally and extend Lethal Hits army-wide. It punishes elite armies with expensive Characters and Vehicles by converting weight-of-dice into reliable wounds against exactly those targets, while the infantry screen holds objectives behind the assault wave. Spread-out horde armies that deny clean charges and force piecemeal commitment crack this open, since the list's threat concentration means poor sequencing or early attrition leaves it without enough activation flexibility to recover.
1075: Built around Thunderwolf Cavalry, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Logan Grimnar, Ragnar Blackmane, Arjac Rockfist, and supporting characters, this Champions of Fenris list is a mobile melee beatdown machine with a Gladiator Lancer providing ranged backbone. The win condition is coordinated multi-threat assault: Characters exploit Countercharge to Heroic Intervene repeatedly without burning the stratagem for anyone else, letting elite combat units crash into opponents across multiple phases while Thunderwolves threaten wide flanks and Wolf Guard Terminators lock down mid-table. It punishes slower melee or elite infantry lists that can't handle simultaneous charges from multiple high-damage units across different threat vectors. It struggles against shooting-heavy gunlines and alpha-strike lists that can delete key combat pieces before they close, since the entire engine collapses if the assault wave is thinned before contact.
1085: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened, Scarab Occult Terminators, Sorcerer in Terminator Armour, Tzaangors, Rubric Marines, and Sekhetar Robots under the Rubricae Phalanx detachment, this is a mass-horde army with surprising mid-table punch — waves of cheap Tzaangor bodies backed by elite Terminator muscle. The plan is to flood the midfield with expendable screens, lock down objectives through sheer body count, and let Scarab Occult Terminators and Sorcerers deliver layered lethal firepower once the enemy is committed. The Rubricae Phalanx's damage-1 save bonus makes Rubric Marines punishingly durable against armies relying on small-arms spam, bolter equivalents, or mortal-wound-light shooting to grind through infantry. High model count and mid-table presence punishes aggressive alpha-strike lists that expect to clear efficiently, but concentrated high-damage, multi-damage weapons that bypass the damage-1 buff will crack the elite core apart.
1083: Built around Kairos Fateweaver, Lords of Change, Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Scarab Occult Terminators, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, Tzaangors, and Rubric Marines operating under the Changehost of Deceit, this list floods the board with layered Psyker-aura synergies — most critically the Daemonic Illusions 4+ invulnerable save against ranged attacks, blanketing multiple units simultaneously. It wins by combining mid-table brawling pressure from Scarab Occult Terminators and horde screening from Tzaangors with sustained psychic attrition, using mobile Enlightened to skimmer-fire across objectives while the Psyker bubble keeps everything alive. Spread-out armies that rely on shooting to strip bodies struggle badly against the stacking invulnerable coverage and sheer model count. However, elite melee forces that can bypass the ranged saves and collapse the Psyker bubble in close combat will unravel the defensive engine fast.
703: Built around Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators with Sorcerers in Terminator Armour leading them, Mutalith Vortex Beasts, and Exalted Sorcerers, this is a Rubricae Phalanx list that plays a dense, layered infantry wall with meaningful elite punch. The engine is grinding attrition through sheer body count and resilience — the detachment's damage-1 save bonus makes Rubric Marines punishingly hard to clear with small-arms fire, letting the list hold objectives while Scarab Occult and Mutaliths apply mid-board pressure and skimmer fire chips from range. It punishes lists that rely on massed low-damage output, particularly horde mirrors and light-infantry gunlines that simply cannot generate enough high-damage hits to cut through stacked saves. However, concentrated high-damage multi-wound shooting or combat units bypass the damage-1 immunity entirely, and the limited mobility of the core infantry means a fast, explosive alpha-strike list can seize board control before the wall gets established.
1086: Built around Lords of Change, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Sorcerers, Flamers, Screamers, and Tzaangor Enlightened, this list runs Changehost of Deceit to wrap a 4+ invulnerable save against ranged attacks onto Scintillating Legions units within 6" of a Psyker, turning the entire force into a durable, shape-shifting threat across the board. The win condition is layered attrition and mobility: Flamers and Lords of Change apply lethal ranged pressure while Screamers and Enlightened skate objectives, forcing opponents to choose between trading into a resilient midfield brawl or ceding ground. It punishes elite low-volume shooting armies hardest, where the pervasive invulnerable aura degrades already limited damage output to near-nothing. It struggles against high-volume mortal wound generation or melee armies that can close quickly and bypass the aura entirely by fighting rather than shooting.
1081: Built around Defilers, Forgefiends, Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Sekhetar Robots, Scarab Occult Terminators, Rubric Marines, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, Tzaangor Shamans, Exalted Sorcerers on Discs, and Tzaangors, this list layers a psyker-buffed vehicle core under the Warpforged Cabal and Ritual of Regeneration detachment pairing — keeping Psykers within 6" of Vehicles to unlock full re-roll suites on Hits, Wounds, and Damage while healing Psykers through successful Rituals. The win condition is sustained anti-armour overload: Forgefiends and Defilers cycle re-rolls through adjacent Psykers turn after turn, while durable infantry blobs hold the mid-table and screen the gun platform. It punishes lists that rely on single heavy threats or low-volume fire, since the re-roll engine absorbs variance and the Ritual healing loop keeps key Psykers alive longer than opponents budget for. It cracks under elite melee alpha strikes or long-range anti-tank pressure that separates Vehicles from their Psyker bubbles before the re-roll engine can fire.
1079: Built around massed Termagant swarms backed by Biovores, Tyrannofex, Exocrine, and Zoanthropes with Neurotyrant support, layered with Genestealers, Broodlord, Norn Emissary, and Neurolictor flex pieces across Invasion Fleet. The plan is to flood objectives with expendable bodies while the gunline chips at targets from range, then pivot whichever tool fits the moment — the neurolictor and Norn Emissary create pressure across multiple board zones simultaneously, forcing opponents to answer threats they can't all cover. It punishes tightly concentrated elite lists that can't clear hordes efficiently, burying them in ablative wounds while the heavy shooting and melee clean up survivors. However, mass mortal-wound output and high-volume anti-Infantry shooting craters the gant screen early, stripping the army of its board presence and exposing the expensive backline pieces before they can cycle effectively.
1077: Built around Maleceptors, Tyrannofexes, Exocrines, Biovores, Norn Emissaries, Lictors, Neurolictors, a Hive Tyrant, and Deathleaper — running Ambush Predators and Crusher Stampede — this is a psychic-gunline hybrid that floods the board with heavy firepower and deep-striking assassins. The plan is to anchor objectives with full-Strength Monsters gaining +2 OC from Crusher Stampede while Lictors and Neurolictors deep strike in to threaten Characters and crack open defended positions, letting the Tyrannofex and Exocrine backfield punish anything forced into the open. It punishes static, low-mobility gunlines that can't simultaneously clear deep-strike threats and weather sustained high-volume heavy fire from multiple Monster platforms. It cracks under elite melee pressure or alpha strikes that quickly reduce Monsters below Starting Strength, stripping the OC advantage and forcing an already middling list into reactive, defensive play.
1078: Built around hormagaunt swarms driven forward by Tyranid Primes with Lash Whips, Neurotyrant and Maleceptor psyker support, Norn Emissary threats, and Neurolictor infiltration pressure, all operating under the Synaptic Nexus's rotating Synaptic Imperatives that buff whichever unit needs it most each round. The plan is to flood midboard objectives with cheap, synapse-buffed hormagaunts while Norn Emissaries and psykers surgically remove key opposing pieces, scoring through sustained board control rather than one explosive turn. It punishes infantry-heavy armies that can't efficiently clear volume, where the combination of screening gaunts and hard-to-shift synapse creatures makes every trade inefficient for the opponent. It cracks under anti-horde firepower that removes the gaunt screens early, collapsing synapse coverage and leaving the more expensive pieces exposed and unsupported.
1080: Built around Termagants, Biovores, the Swarmlord, Norn Assimilators, a Hive Tyrant, Tyrannofex, Winged Tyranid Prime, and Norn Emissary under the Assimilation Swarm detachment, this is a regenerating combined-arms swarm that blends horde bodies with monstrous-creature muscle. The win condition is attrition through the Harvester regeneration loop — restoring wounds or returning dead Termagant models each Command phase to deny your opponent the kills they need to control objectives and score secondaries. It punishes slow, low-volume-of-fire gunlines that can't permanently erase regenerating units fast enough, while the Tyrannofex and Norn Assimilators provide anti-tank overload pressure. However, high-volume, high-AP shooting that drops multiple threats in a single phase breaks the regeneration engine before it compounds.
1076: Built around the Norn Assimilator, Norn Emissary, Biovores, Red Terror, Pyrovores, Psychophage, and Haruspex under the Talons of the Norn Queen detachment, this is a mobile creature-heavy swarm that floods the board with versatile, hard-to-remove bodies. The Singular Purpose ability lets each unit retarget its specialisation each Command phase, letting the list adapt its threat profile turn-by-turn while Biovores apply indirect pressure and monstrous melee pieces grind through the midfield. It punishes slow, static armies that can't reposition to address simultaneously shifting threat vectors across multiple board sectors. It cracks against elite shooting lists that can sequence kills faster than the swarm can reorient, stripping key pieces before Singular Purpose pays off.
1087: Built around Goremongers, Jakhals, Forgefiends, Exalted Eightbound, Daemon Princes of Khorne, Angron, and Eightbound, this is a mobile, multi-threat assault force that floods every board sector with dangerous bodies across a wide threat bracket. The win condition is overwhelming opponent decision-making — Forgefiends crack armour at range while Eightbound, Exalted Eightbound, and Angron crash into melee simultaneously, forcing trades that always favour the World Eaters' volume and lethality, with Jakhals and Goremongers screening lanes and contesting secondaries cheaply. It punishes static gunlines and elite low-model-count armies that cannot efficiently clear multiple converging threats across the full table width. Faster, more cohesive melee armies or shooting lists with strong chaff clearance can erode the screening layer early, collapsing the threat timing this build depends on to land its charges safely.
